# Vommet changes compared with Commet

Everything this fork changes relative to upstream [Commet](https://github.com/commetchat/commet),
so the fork stays auditable and easy to rebase. **Rule: every change to Commet's code or
behaviour adds an entry here in the same commit.** Issue numbers refer to
[this repo's tracker](https://nether.codes/robocub/vommet/issues).

Status: **main** = merged; **testing** = on the [`testing`](https://nether.codes/robocub/vommet/src/branch/testing)
branch (in tester builds) and on its own branch, waiting for hands-on testing before it is merged.

## Identity and separation from Commet's infrastructure

| Change | Where | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Application id `chat.commet.commetapp` → `im.nether.chat` on Android, Linux and Windows (installs beside Commet); Android Kotlin package moved | android/, linux/, windows/, msix config | main |
| Linux builds use the production app id `im.nether.chat` (`COMMET_PROD=1`; CI built `im.nether.chat.develop`, so docks showed no icon) and the X11 window class is the app id (`g_set_prgname`) | `linux/main.cc`, Linux CI workflows | testing (`fix/linux-app-id`, `ci/flatpak`) |
| Third-party proxy default `proxy.commet.chat` → `proxy.nether.im` ([vommet-proxy](https://nether.codes/robocub/vommet-proxy)) | `config/preferences.dart` | main |
| Update checker disabled (`UpdateChecker.hasReleaseFeed = false`): Commet's feed describes Commet, and Windows auto-update would replace the fork with Commet | `utils/update_checker.dart` | main |
| `push.commet.chat` removed from the push-gateway choices (it serves Commet's Firebase project) | notification settings | main |
| Default push gateway `push.commet.chat` → `matrix.gateway.unifiedpush.org` (UnifiedPush builds); pushers on the old default re-register on next start | `config/preferences.dart` | testing (`fix/own-push-gateway`) |
| README: fork disclosure, slogan, changes and plans, footer | `README.md` | main |
| Name "Vommet" everywhere (window title, app labels, desktop entries, Windows resources, English strings); executable `vommet` | many | testing (`chore/branding`) |
| Logo (Twemoji 🤮/🤩 adaptation, CC-BY 4.0) and all platform icons, generated by `scripts/generate_vommet_icons.py` from `vommet.svg` / `vommet-mono.svg` | `assets/images/app_icon/`, platform icon dirs | testing (`chore/branding`) |
| "Source Code" / "License" links and both in-app bug reporters point at nether.codes instead of Commet's GitHub (`BuildConfig.sourceUrl`, `issueHost`, …) | about page, log page, crash screen | testing (`chore/branding`) |
| Donations: Settings "Donate" entry and the post-update "please donate" dialog removed (their flow went to commet.chat) | settings, main page | testing (`chore/fork-settings`) |

## Changed defaults

| Setting | Commet | Vommet | Status |

| Settings › General › Media › Public Rooms (`preview_media_in_public_rooms`) | off | **on** | testing (`chore/fork-settings`) |
| Settings › Experiments › Encrypted Element Call (`experiment_enabled_e2ee_element_call`) | off | **on** | testing (`chore/fork-settings`) |
| Homeserver pre-filled on the login screen (`assets/config/global_config.json`) | matrix.org | **nether.im** | testing (`chore/fork-settings`) |

Only people who never touched these toggles get the new default. The homeserver is only a pre-filled field; any server can still be typed in.

## Integration tests

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Integration tests (`integration.yml`, `.vommet/it/`): the Linux app driven by Flutter integration_test against a throwaway Tuwunel at https://localhost under Xvfb, with screen recording; curated `vommet_runner.dart` (upstream's login tests pass; the rest are being rewritten); nightly on testing | testing (`ci/integration-tests`) |
| Startup: `initializeMessages` (a `SynchronousFuture`) inside `Future.wait` tripped a null check on every launch (swallowed in the app); wrapped in `Future.value` | testing (`ci/integration-tests`) |
| Desktop main page: `mainView` was wrapped in a second `Expanded` around its own `Flexible`/`Expanded` (competing ParentDataWidgets); now one wrapper, same layout as release builds | testing (`ci/integration-tests`) |
| `CustomSafeArea` never cancelled its text-field-focus subscription (setState after dispose, leaked state) | testing (`ci/integration-tests`) |
| `RustLib.init` runs once per process (the tests run app init per test) | testing (`ci/integration-tests`) |
| Startup waits for the SDK's own quick first sync (`firstSyncReceived`) instead of `oneShotSync()`, which could join a 30 s long-poll and hold the app-ready point (links, notifications) for ~30 s; startup sync telemetry says whether sliding sync was used and times its first rounds (upstream Commet has the same wait) | — | testing (`fix/first-sync-wait`) |
| Link previews from Tuwunel (and any server that sends Open Graph numbers as JSON numbers) render instead of staying on the loading shimmer forever; `og:*` fields are read by type (`MatrixUrlPreviewComponent.ogString/ogInt`) rather than cast with `as String?` (YouTube links were the visible case) | — | branch (`fix/url-preview-numeric-og`) |
| Timeline stops loading older history after 3 pages in a row with no messages (only membership/profile changes, which fold into one summary row and never fill the view) and shows a "Load older messages" button instead of paging back through the whole room; pressing it loads until the view fills or the room's start, without pausing again | — | testing (`fix/history-empty-pause`) |
| Calendar rooms keep syncing their external calendars: the sync pass walks every room with a pause between rooms, and a room joined or left meanwhile ended it with a ConcurrentModificationError (logged on every launch on a 237-room account); it also never scheduled the next pass after a failure. Upstream has the same code | — | branch (`fix/calendar-sync-room-list`) |
| Developer › Performance (and opt-in diagnostics) time each space's room-list update, which runs for every space whenever a room is added, to find a ~6 s startup freeze on a 237-room phone | — | branch (`perf/space-list-timer`) |
| Faster startup: the sidebar recounted every room's unread badge on every single room update (each room reports one as its state loads, so hundreds of full recounts at startup); it now recounts once per burst, within 100 ms. Upstream has the same code | — | branch (`perf/sidebar-count-coalesce`) |
| Faster startup: each space's colour scheme (derived from its avatar on the UI thread) was recomputed on every update of the space, many times while spaces load; it is now computed once per avatar and starts 5 s after launch. A startup CPU profile of a 237-room account spent ~15% of its first 8 s there. Upstream has the same code | — | branch (`perf/space-color-scheme-once`) |
| Space colour schemes are worked out in a background isolate (`ImageSeedColor`: scale to 112 px on the UI isolate, colour clustering and scoring in an isolate, then `ColorScheme.fromSeed` with the same variant), so the same colours no longer cost ~1 s of UI-isolate time a few seconds after launch | — | branch (`perf/space-color-scheme-once`) |
| Faster startup and syncing with many rooms: every room, space and room emoji manager listened to the client's shared streams (state changes, events, notifications, syncs) and filtered for its own room, so each item was delivered to all of them (~500 deliveries per state change on a 237-room account). A router now listens once and hands each item to its room only (`RoomStreamRouter`). Upstream has the same pattern | — | branch (`perf/room-event-router`) |
| Settings › Advanced › Renderer (Android): Default, OpenGL or Compatibility (Skia), applied at the next launch by a new `VommetApplication`; falls back to the default after two launches that never drew a frame. For phones where Impeller drops letters from text | — | testing (`fix/android-renderer-choice`) |
| Up arrow in an empty composer fills the text with the last message when it starts an edit (macOS left the composer empty) | 898 | main (`fix/898-up-arrow-edit-text`) |

## Deliberately unchanged

- Matrix event types and account-data keys under `chat.commet.*` (calendars, photo albums, recent emoji, sidebar order…), so data stays compatible with Commet.
- The `commetchat://` URL scheme (widget deep links), Flutter MethodChannel names, and the Rust library name `rust_lib_commet`.
- Strings that credit or point to Commet on purpose (README credits, "donate to Commet" text in profile badges).

## GitHub copy

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| GitHub copy (`github-copy.yml`): one-way force-push of main, testing and ci/windows* to github.com/dark-collective/vommet for Windows CI; replaces the Forgejo push mirror (its `+refs/*:refs/*` fetch refspec wrote GitHub's state back over ours) | main |
| GitHub copy pushes snapshots only (main, testing, ci/windows*, ci/xplat*), to a standalone (non-fork) repo: each branch is one orphan commit (tree = the Forgejo tip's tree, no parent, neutral message without '#'), so our issue numbers can't link to Commet's PRs; a guard refuses any other or issue-linking commit, and every other GitHub branch is pruned | testing (`chore/github-snapshot`) |

## CI speed

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Housekeeping workflows (`github-copy`, `upstream-sync`, `upstream-promote`, `nightly`) run on a separate 2-slot "light" Forgejo runner, so they never wait behind builds in the main runner's single slot (the GitHub builds start when github-copy finishes) | main |
| Heavy CI jobs (build, APK, Flatpak, integration) skip on a push when the exact commit, or the green testing containing it, already passed them (`.vommet/ci/already-passed.sh`); the Flatpak bundle also builds on sync/testing, so release files come from the candidate's runs | main |
| CI image `.vommet/ci/Dockerfile` (apt packages, Flutter, Rust, Android SDK, Tuwunel preinstalled; built on the runner, used locally): jobs no longer install toolchains on every run | main |

## Nightly runs

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| `.forgejo/workflows/nightly.yml` on main starts the nightly integration workflows on testing via the API (Forgejo only fires `schedule:` on the default branch, so their own crons never ran) | main |
| Nightly runs at 06:55 UTC (was 03:41, which collided with sync cuts) and skips the full integration suite when testing's commit already passed it, except on Sundays (flake probe); synapse and secure-setup suites always run | main |
| `.vommet/gpu-check/`: a nightly check on a real GPU (Intel iGPU test container) that runs the newest testing Linux build's docked widget through dock, pop out and full screen on Wayland and X11, and posts `widgets-gpu / linux (cubuntu igpu)` on testing (CI machines have no GPU, which hid the black pop-out) | main |

## Upstream CI review hold

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| The upstream sync holds upstream commits that change CI files (`.forgejo`, `.gitea`, `.github/workflows`, `.github/actions`, `.vommet`): the candidate is cut on the last reviewed upstream commit (`.vommet/upstream-ci-reviewed` on main) and the report lists what to review, so upstream workflow changes never run with the fork's secrets unreviewed | pending main (`ci/upstream-ci-review-hold`) |

## Pull request builds on GitHub

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Pull requests build on the GitHub copy instead of the single-slot Forgejo runner: `pr-github.yml` (light runner, every 10 min) copies each open PR head there as a parentless snapshot tag `ci-pr-<n>` whose `.github/` holds only our `vommet-pr.yml` (no secrets, read-only token), and mirrors the result onto the PR as the status `build / linux (github)`; fork PRs only from authors with write access or with the `ci-approved` label. build.yml's jobs skip on pull_request events | pending main (`ci/pr-github`) |
| The nightly integration suites on testing (full suite unless already green, secure setup, Synapse UTD and unread-dot variants) run on the GitHub copy (`vommet-nightly.yml`, pushed as `ci/windows-nightly` by `nightly.yml`), which posts the results on testing as `... (github nightly)` statuses; they no longer occupy the Forgejo runner | pending main (`ci/pr-github`) |

## Message forwarding

| Change | Issue | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Experiment (Settings › Experiments › Chat and messages › Forward messages, off by default): Telegram-style forwarding. "Forward" in the message menu opens a searchable room list; the chosen room opens with the message waiting in a bar above the message box (× cancels). Tapping the bar shows a preview with Hide sender name, Hide caption (media with a caption), Change recipient, Apply changes and Do not forward. Text typed with it is sent first, then the forward. With the sender shown the event follows MSC4553 under its unstable prefix `org.matrix.msc4553.forwarded` (origin + a copy of the original content; other clients see a "Forwarded from … - view original message" fallback); with it hidden it is a plain copy. Received MSC4553 forwards render the original with a "Forwarded from" header and can't be edited; MSC2723 (`com.famedly.app.forwarded`) forwards get the header only. Stickers always forward as a copy (MSC4553 covers messages only). Hide caption also changes the copy in `content`, which MSC4553 otherwise says to keep unchanged. Media whose body is empty or missing forwards with its filename as the body (no caption). Pending forwards are kept per room in memory. (`client/matrix/forwarding/`, `ui/organisms/forward_message/`, chat/composer/message layout hooks). Upstream request: commetchat/commet#336 (no upstream PR) | — | testing (`feat/forward-messages`, after `feat/room-picker-search`) |
| Experiment (Settings › Experiments › Chat and messages › Forward messages, off by default): Telegram-style forwarding. "Forward" in the message menu opens a searchable room list; the chosen room opens with the message waiting in a bar above the message box (× cancels). Tapping the bar shows a preview with Hide sender name, Hide caption (media with a caption), Change recipient, Apply changes and Do not forward. Text typed with it is sent first, then the forward. With the sender shown the event follows MSC4553 under its unstable prefix `org.matrix.msc4553.forwarded` (origin + a copy of the original content; other clients see a "Forwarded from … - view original message" fallback); with it hidden it is a plain copy. Received MSC4553 forwards render the original with a "Forwarded from" header and can't be edited; MSC2723 (`com.famedly.app.forwarded`) forwards get the header only. Stickers always forward as a copy (MSC4553 covers messages only). Hide caption also changes the copy in `content`, which MSC4553 otherwise says to keep unchanged. Pending forwards are kept per room in memory. (`client/matrix/forwarding/`, `ui/organisms/forward_message/`, chat/composer/message layout hooks). Upstream request: commetchat/commet#336 (no upstream PR) | — | testing (`feat/forward-messages`, after `feat/room-picker-search`) |

## Voice isolation

| Change | Issue | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Experiment "Noise suppression" (Settings › Experiments; off by default), then Settings › Voice › Audio Settings › "Noise suppression" (Linux, Windows, Android): Automatic (default once opted in) benchmarks DeepFilterNet3 in the background and falls back to RNNoise if it runs late in a call; Standard runs RNNoise 0.2 (BSD-3); Best runs DeepFilterNet3 (MIT/Apache-2.0, network implemented in Rust, no inference runtime); Basic keeps only WebRTC's own suppressor. Both engines live in the `rust/voice` crate (vendored RNNoise in `third_party/rnnoise` plus our `os_support.h`, which the 0.2 release omits; DeepFilterNet3 weights in `third_party/deepfilternet`), linked into `rust_lib_commet` on desktop and built as `libvommet_voice.so` on Android by the `rust/voice_builder` plugin, which also registers it with flutter_webrtc's capture post-processing. Dart reaches it through `dart:ffi`. They run on the microphone inside libwebrtc's capture pipeline, and WebRTC's own suppressor is turned off while they do. It needs `setCapturePostProcessor` (desktop) from our flutter_webrtc fork, branch `vommet-1.6` of [nether/vommet-flutter-webrtc](https://nether.codes/nether/vommet-flutter-webrtc), which also carries the screen-share audio changes; stacked after `feat/screenshare-audio-linux`, whose override it moves to that branch. `integration_test/voip/voice_filter_test.dart` checks it end to end; a comment on `WebrtcDefaultDevices.initDummyConnection` records why that connection must stay open (Linux audio-device restart bug) | #3 | branch (`feat/voice-isolation`) |

## Native OIDC sign-in

| Change | Issue | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Native OIDC sign-in (MSC2964/2965/2966/2967): when the homeserver publishes `/_matrix/client/v1/auth_metadata`, the login screen shows one "Continue" button that opens the server's sign-in page in the browser, instead of the single sign-on buttons; "Sign in with a password instead" stays. One path at a time: while the password form is open, the browser buttons hide and the link reads "Sign in with your browser instead" (two look-alike "Login" and "Continue" buttons confused testers). Vommet registers itself as a native client (`client_uri` https://vommet.app) with a loopback redirect `http://127.0.0.1:<random port>/oauth/callback` on Linux/Windows and `app.vommet:/oauth` on Android/iOS/macOS (new Android intent filter); not offered on web. Code exchange and token refresh are Vommet's own, because the SDK reads `expires_in` as milliseconds; only OIDC sessions get the refresh handler (`onSoftLogout`), so password and SSO sessions behave as before | #45 | testing (`feat/native-oidc`) |

## Capture diagnostics

| Change | Issue | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Diagnostics schema v2: a `capture` event records whether the microphone or screen capture started, how long it took, how many input devices there were and whether the device picked in settings was missing. It also records a fixed device type (built-in/USB/Bluetooth/virtual/HDMI), reduced from the device label on the device; labels and error messages are never sent. The call backends start the microphone without waiting for it, so whether it started is measured by watching for the published microphone after joining. The screen-share start wasn't awaited either, so its failure vanished; it is now logged and recorded at the call view. ## Quieter notifications only while you're chatting elsewhere

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| "Silence Notifications" (on by default, Android) quieted every notification while any other device of the account had been seen in the last 10 minutes; a desktop client or browser tab left open keeps that fresh, so one account could stay silent for good. Now a notification is only quieted when another device was seen in the last 5 minutes AND your latest message or reaction in that same room is from the last 5 minutes AND it wasn't sent from this device (the app records the IDs of events it sent, `push_notification/sent_here.dart`, so no clocks are compared). The check fetches only your own recent events and gives up after 3 s; on any error or delay it notifies normally (`modifiers/suppress_other_device_active.dart`, unit test `notification_quiet_other_device_test.dart`). The setting is now called "Quiet notifications while I'm chatting on another device", its description says what on and off do, and a "Right now: …" line under it says whether another of your devices is online (rechecked every minute while shown; `quiet_status.dart`) | testing (`fix/notify-silence-active-chat`) |
## Notifications from every account

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| With several accounts signed in, pushes for all of them arrive (they share one UnifiedPush endpoint). The account a push is for is read from the Matrix push's `devices[].data.local_client_id`, where homeservers put it and UnifiedPush gateways forward it; only Commet's own gateway flattened it to the top level, the one place the app looked. The fallback (which account has the room) now asks the running accounts first, and its background cache is rewritten whenever rooms or accounts change instead of only at startup, so a push for a room joined later isn't dropped | topic (`fix/push-account-routing`) |

| Change | Status |
|---|---|

Vommet's registrations now carry the session's device id, and at startup Vommet removes its own registrations (only ones carrying its namespaced device-id key, so never Commet's, which share the app id) whose session is signed out or unused for 90 days; standard client APIs only, so any homeserver (a device that comes back registers again). Raw pusher data stays behind developer mode | topic (`fix/pusher-housekeeping`) |

## Notification diagnostics (telemetry schema v9)

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Opt-in diagnostics only: `notify_setup` is now recorded once per account (numbered by position, `account_index`/`accounts`; room counts per account) instead of only the first, and a new `notify_counts` event reports what happened to notifications since the last report: shown, quieted (another device / other rule), dropped (room open, Do Not Disturb, notifications off, other rule), "couldn't show" notices, failures, and handling time. The counters live in shared preferences so the background push isolate can add to them, are only written while diagnostics are on, and are deleted when diagnostics are turned off or "Delete my diagnostics" is used (`telemetry/notify_counts.dart`, hook in `NotificationManager.notify`). Counts only, never rooms, senders or content. Only notifications that reach `NotificationManager.notify` are counted (pushes lost before that, or handled before preferences load, aren't) | testing (`feat/telemetry-notify-counts`) |

|---|---|
| Space main page: nested subspace cards step up a shade per level (blended from the text colour on themes without container shades, e.g. AMOLED, where the cards had vanished), a faint neutral line runs down each subspace's rooms as in the sidebar's subspace guides, and subspace headers are compact (no padding around the name, 40/32 px avatars) so a space and its first subspace sit close; a coloured edge bar was tried and removed as too busy (`space_summary_view.dart`) | testing (`feat/space-page-subspace-cards`) |
## Manage a space's rooms

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Experiment `experiment_manage_space_rooms` (Layout and sidebar): "Manage rooms" in the space menu (people allowed to edit the space) opens an editor like Discord's "Edit channels": the space as a tree in the owner's order, a drag handle on every row, and a ⋯ menu to move a room up/down, into another subspace (added there before it's removed here, so a failed save never orphans it) or out of the space (never deletes the room). Changes are collected, summarised and only applied on Save; removed rows stay crossed out with Undo. On phones, long-press on the space home page then only opens the room menu (it used to start a drag too). Shared space code (also used by the space home page and "Create or add a room"): reordering keeps children the app can't show (not joined) in their places, never writes a removed child back, and gives a just-added child our server as `via`; adding a child writes the space's entry and treats the room's link back to the space as best effort (it needs power in that room), copying `via`/`suggested` on a move; only rate limits and network errors are retried, others are reported instead of being retried for minutes and then ignored (`ui/pages/manage_space_rooms/`, `matrix_space.dart`, unit test `space_rooms_edit_test.dart`) | testing (`feat/manage-space-rooms`) |

## Trust warnings in direct messages

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Vommet remembers each direct-message partner's identity key; when it changes, a red shield appears after their name and a strip above the message box says someone could be impersonating them (It was them / Verify). If they never set up secure messaging, a dismissible banner says Vommet can't confirm it's really them (What does this mean? / Let them know, which drafts a friendly heads-up), and starting a new direct message with them asks first. Sending something that decodes as a Matrix recovery key stops with "That looks like a recovery key" (Don't send it / It's not mine, send anyway). On by default, switchable on the Experiments page (Vommet issue 130). The same pins also stop room history from being sent to someone whose identity changed when you invite them (MSC4268), until you press It was them or verify them | `feat/dm-trust-warnings` |
| An identity Vommet pinned whose master key disappears (a server can serve a contact's keys without it, and add a device of its own) counts as changed (red strip and shield) instead of the dismissible "not set up" banner; keys not fetched yet (fresh sign-in, cleared cache) stay unknown until they are. It was them with no master key forgets the pin (`identity_pins.dart`) | `feat/dm-trust-warnings` |

## Secure messaging setup at sign-in (Vommet issue 129)

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Right after sign-in and before any room opens, accounts that need it get a plain-language secure messaging setup (cross-signing + key backup; the UI never says "cross-signing"). New account: welcome → choose how to save the recovery key (encrypted password manager, recommended, via the system save prompt with a Google Password Manager caveat when Android's autofill service is Google; a 6-word phrase from the EFF large wordlist, with "Copy to clipboard" and, on Android/Apple only, "Save to password manager"; or an own recovery password with a strength meter and a warning when it's the login password, known only right after a password sign-in, kept in memory as a salted hash) → confirm you really have it (autofill/paste the key, type 2 phrase words, retype the password) → done. Existing account on a new device: approve from another device (existing emoji verification) or enter the recovery key/phrase/password, then all message keys are fetched from the backup (fixes upstream Commet issue 1046). Lost everything: a separate start-over path behind a hold-to-confirm. Skip is warned twice (the second says it's for developers, hold to skip) and leaves a reminder banner at the top of the room list; Settings › Security gets a "Set up secure messaging" button. "Still have your recovery key?" check-ins after 3 days, then monthly. Screenshots are blocked while a key or phrase is on screen (Android FLAG_SECURE). 4 offline explainer cards, "Read the full guide" → vommet.app/help/secure-messaging. Accounts already set up never see a screen (judged from local state first). Keys are only ever created when the server confirms nothing exists (no master key, no secret storage, no backup; a failed check counts as "don't know", never "nothing"); only the explicit start-over and "make a new key" paths replace an identity, and "make a new key" keeps the message backup. Shared: closing the account-confirmation (UIA) dialog cancels the request instead of leaving it waiting forever, SSO gets an "I've finished in the browser" retry, and the account-page approval stage for OIDC accounts (stable m.oauth and unstable org.matrix.cross_signing_reset, MSC4312) is supported. On by default; experiment `experiment_secure_setup` (Chat and messages) only so it can be turned off for crash triage. Shared `SecureMessaging` own-trust-state helper (`client/matrix/secure_messaging_state.dart`) for Vommet issue 130 (`ui/pages/secure_setup/`, `VommetSecureScreen.kt`, unit test `secure_setup_test.dart`) | testing (`feat/secure-setup`) |
| Settings › Security for a device that isn't confirmed yet (account already set up): the panel (now "Encryption & recovery") leads with a "Confirm this device" card, "Enter recovery key" opening the setup straight at the key step and "Use another device instead" straight into approval; the rows read "Device confirmation" (its button enters the key instead of a red "Reset") and "Message history backup"; the "Unverified" alert and "Set up secure messaging" (now only for accounts never set up) give way to it. Before, entering the key hid behind "Message backup › Restore" | testing (`feat/secure-setup`) |
| Settings › Security › "Replace my recovery key" (set-up accounts): pick "I want a new recovery key" (enter the current key/phrase/password; every secret moves under a new key, same identity and same backup, so contacts see no change and the old key stops working) or "Someone may have used my key" (new key, new identity, new backup holding every message key this device has, then a change-password step: the account page for OIDC accounts, otherwise current/new password with "Also sign me out everywhere else" on by default). Integration suite `integration_test/secure_setup_runner.dart` against the CI homeserver: fresh accounts per test; own-password setup through the real account-password dialog and confirm step, skip (both warnings, interrupted hold), recovery key on a new device restoring history, approval from another device, replace key / someone used my key / make a new key (each checked by decrypting old history on a new raw device), nothing replaced without consent, a closed password dialog never hangs setup (`ui/pages/secure_setup/change_password.dart`) | testing (`feat/secure-setup`) |
| Fixes found by that suite: after a fresh sign-in the setup never appeared (the status check waited for a first sync that's only started for saved sessions, timed out after 30 s, read "unknown" and closed itself; now it waits for the client's own first sync); setup could handle the first step twice ("Wrong State" on accounts with existing secret storage); the two skip warnings and the recovery-key check-in threw a layout assertion on desktop (now a plain `SetupDialog`, max 420 wide, laid out at phone and desktop width by `unit_test/secure_setup_dialogs_test.dart`); button labels shrink to fit instead of overflowing. Log lines for the sign-in decision and each unlock step (no ids) | testing (`feat/secure-setup`) |
| A recovery key copied for a password manager comes off the clipboard again when setup is left any way (skip, close), not only after the confirm step; same for Commet's own cross-signing setup page under Settings › Security (`recovery_key_clipboard.dart`, `secure_setup_flow.dart`, `cross_signing_view.dart`) | testing (`feat/secure-setup`) |

## Room threads

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Threads list: every thread in the room, newest activity first, with who started it, its first message, the reply count and the newest reply; "All threads" / "My threads" filter (threads you started or replied in); loads more as you scroll and refreshes when a thread gets a reply. Opens from the room's Threads button (next to Pinned Messages) or, with the Discord-style layout, the member panel's Threads tab. Uses the server's `/threads` API (Matrix v1.4) | branch (`feat/room-threads`, after `feat/member-panel-tabs`) |

| A thread whose root isn't in the server's relations response (servers other than Synapse leave out `original_event`) fetches the root itself, so threads opened from the list show their first message | branch (`feat/room-threads`) |
| Settings › Experiments › Chat and messages › Read state per thread (off by default): threaded read receipts (MSC3771) — reading a thread marks only that thread read, the main timeline sends `main` receipts so opening the room no longer marks every thread read, and the Threads list marks threads with unread replies (dot, bold). Marking the whole room read from the room list stays unthreaded | branch (`feat/room-threads`) |

## Thread view keeps every reply

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| An open thread no longer loses replies: a reply attaching to the root made the thread view write the root over its newest reply (root shown at the bottom, replies missing). Pages stay newest first without duplicates, and a short thread opens with its root on Tuwunel, which hands out a next page token even on the last page. The Threads list hides a thread whose root was deleted and has no replies left | branch (`feat/room-threads`) |

## Thread view lists each message once

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| An open thread no longer shows messages twice or replies above the root: thread messages the room timeline announces again (as it pages through the same messages) refresh their copy in the thread instead of being added, and new ones are placed by time | branch (`feat/room-threads`) |
## Block users

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Settings › Experiments › Chat and messages › Block users (off by default): Block / Unblock in a person's profile menu (with a confirmation saying what it does), and Settings › Security › Blocked users listing everyone you've blocked with Unblock buttons, plus blocking by Matrix ID. Uses the account's `m.ignored_user_list`, so the server drops their messages, invites and calls and other Matrix apps honour it; unlike the SDK's `ignoreUser` it doesn't clear the cache or leave DMs | branch (`feat/block-users`, after `fix/profile-nickname-others`) |
| Messages from blocked users already in the local cache are hidden too (whether blocked here or in another app), and appear or disappear in open rooms as soon as the list changes, also when it changes on another device. Messages they sent while blocked aren't fetched back after unblocking | branch (`feat/block-users`) |
| Upstream fix: a timeline entry recomputes its collapsed state on every update, so a message that stops being hidden (e.g. after unblocking) draws again instead of staying an empty collapsed row | branch (`feat/block-users`) |
| Fix: the block list is read again once the account's data has loaded, so blocked users stay hidden after a restart (the list was read before the SDK had loaded it, so it came up empty until the server next sent it) | branch (`feat/block-users`) |
| Fix: room previews (room lists, quick switcher) leave out a blocked user's last message, and blocking or unblocking updates them right away instead of keeping the old text until the next message | branch (`feat/block-users`) |

## Performance diagnostics breakdown (telemetry schema v11)

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Opt-in diagnostics only: `frame_stats` gains the UI thread's (build) and GPU thread's (raster) slowest-5% and worst times, so a slow frame shows whether Dart work or drawing cost it. New `loop_lag` event: how often and how long the UI event loop is blocked (a 500 ms timer's lateness, foreground only; `telemetry/loop_lag.dart`). New `sync_stats` event: how many sync responses were applied and how long applying them took (`telemetry/sync_stats.dart`). `sync_initial` and `sync_error` gain `own_server`: whether the account is on nether.im (a fixed name compared in the app, never sent), never which other server. Numbers and booleans only, reported with the 15-minute perf summary | branch (`feat/telemetry-perf-v11`, after `feat/telemetry-name-tag`) |

## Database and sync-contents diagnostics (telemetry schema v14)

| Change | Status |

They had always shipped empty, because the database package names them in plain English ("Store event update") and only identifier-shaped timer names pass; those names come from a fixed list, so they are made identifiers. `sync_stats` also counts what the window's syncs contained (rooms, timeline events, state events) and how many events the slowest sync carried. Numbers only | branch (`feat/telemetry-db-timers`, after `fix/69-space-nicknames`) |

## One call per room, however often you tap Call

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Tapping Call again while a join is still connecting (it takes seconds on Android) no longer makes a second session for the same room: a join while one runs, or while you're already in that room's call, returns that call; starting a call notifies the room once. Each LiveKit call also gets its own session id instead of `""`, so two calls never share one mute state, and ending one no longer drops the other from the call list. Before, the duplicate showed as two call cards whose mute buttons acted on a different connection from the one the call heard (Vommet issue 167) (`matrix_livekit_backend.dart`, `matrix_livekit_voip_session.dart`, `matrix_room_call_component.dart`) | queued (`fix/call-double-join`) |

## Call membership refresh

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Our call membership (`org.matrix.msc3401.call.member`) is re-posted every hour while we're in a call, keeping `created_ts` and growing `expires`, the way matrix-js-sdk does. Before, one post with `expires` = 4 h was never renewed, so Element Call and Element X dropped a Vommet member (and stopped sharing media keys with them) four hours into a call. Expiry everywhere (focus election, text-room call bar, room activities) now counts from `created_ts`, falling back to the event timestamp, and the legacy (experiment off) SFU election orders members by `created_ts` with ties on the state key, like Element Call, instead of by the latest post | testing (`fix/rtc-membership-refresh`) |

## Wake-from-idle diagnostics (telemetry schema v16)

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Opt-in diagnostics only: a `resume` event after the app comes back from at least 30 s in the background: how long it was away, how many accounts had a sync request already open and how old the oldest was, how long until the first and the last account finished a sync, and how many sync errors (and timeouts) happened in between. Checks whether a request left open while the device slept holds up new messages after waking (`telemetry/resume_telemetry.dart`). Durations and counts only | branch (`feat/telemetry-resume`, after `feat/telemetry-image-cache`) |
| Room keys are looked up for backup only after a new one was stored, instead of after every sync: that lookup is a database query (100–270 ms on a phone) and it queued with the sync's own writes. SDK fork `vommet-v6.1.1-ss.8` (ss.7 + this) | — | branch (`perf/sdk-key-upload-gate`, after `perf/drift-db-fragment-cache`) |
| Checking for unsent messages (Offline sending, at startup) reads only a room's unsent list instead of loading and decoding its whole list of stored message ids: on a 209-room account that was ~110 ms per room, competing with the startup loads behind the splash. Unsent messages in a room with no stored history yet are no longer skipped. Drift store fork `vommet-v6.1.1-db.2` (db.1 + this) | — | branch (`perf/sdk-key-upload-gate`) |
| Saving new messages to the on-device database is lighter: the app used to re-read and re-write a room's whole list of cached message ids for every single message in a sync, and open a nested database transaction per message (each a round trip to the database isolate); now the list is edited in memory and written once per sync, with no nested transactions. Measured 1.5–2.6× faster per sync on a desktop, more on phones (drift store fork tag vommet-v6.1.1-db.1) | — | testing (`feat/sliding-sync`) |

## Debugging and performance diagnostics (telemetry schema v17)

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Opt-in diagnostics only: new `message_send` event per text message, reply, edit, thread message, reaction, redaction and sticker (message length in characters, whether it had formatting, how many people it mentioned, time spent on markdown, time the SDK took to send with its retries, outcome and error kind; never the text or who). New `http_stats` 15-minute summaries per kind of homeserver request (sync, send, media download/thumbnail/upload, keys, profile, state, history, members, push, account data...): count, errors, p95 and worst time, bytes received, and whether it was the user's own server. The kind comes from the shape of the URL's path; the URL is never kept (`telemetry/telemetry_http.dart`, handed to the SDK as its http client). New `call_stats` once a minute during a LiveKit call: connection quality word, participants, how many remote participants report poor quality, packets received and lost, jitter, concealed audio (audible glitches), bitrate, round-trip time, video frame rate and size, and whether a screen share is on (`telemetry/call_stats.dart`). New `crypto_state` once per account: encryption on, cross-signing and key backup set up and their secrets cached, this device verified, device counts (unverified, blocked), room counts (encrypted). New `memory_pressure` event when the OS asks for memory (RSS, image cache, open timelines, foreground). `timeline_crypto` adds why messages couldn't be decrypted (no key, corrupted channel, requestable; counts from the SDK's fixed phrases). `sync_stats` adds foreground gaps between finished syncs (worst, how many over 90 s). `perf_summary` adds open timelines, database size on disk, dropped/overflowed diagnostic events, server clock skew. `app_ready` gains the startup steps' timers (they had never shipped: the general timers are English phrases, now mapped from a fixed list to identifiers; a timer with an account name in it stays out). The report envelope gains total memory, low-RAM flag (Android), screen size and pixel density, text scale and accessibility toggles (bold text, reduce motion, high contrast), the Linux desktop family and software-GL flag. Numbers, booleans and fixed-list values only; the privacy page lists it all | branch (`feat/telemetry-v17-debug`, after `feat/telemetry-resume`) |
| Opt-in diagnostics only (schema v18): Android crash reports carry the build id and the frames' offsets into the app's own instructions (`i+<hex>`/`v+<hex>`), because the APK is built with `--split-debug-info` and its Dart stack traces are non-symbolic, so every Android crash arrived with no location. `flutter symbolize` with that build's symbols turns them into file:line. Repeat-counting now also tells Android crashes apart by their top offset | branch (`feat/telemetry-v17-debug`) |
| Opt-in diagnostics only: the startup report's timers also include how long the splash waited for the rooms' state, the deferred room-state loads, and the time to the first frame since launch (they were missing from the fixed list; the room count in the deferred loads' name is dropped) | branch (`feat/telemetry-v17-debug`) |

## Telemetry: freezes as they happen

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Opt-in diagnostics only (schema v20): a `ui_stall` event the moment the app freezes for 5 s or more, flushed at once so a force-quit doesn't lose it. Kinds: `loop` (the Dart event loop was blocked, reported when it ends), `platform` (the platform/window thread, which on Linux also delivers input and draws, hasn't answered a no-op probe; reported while stuck and when it recovers), `frame` (a frame was requested but none started while focused). Carries the duration, whether it's still ongoing, foreground, whether a call is active, seconds since the last call ended and that call's peak participants. Rides LoopLag's existing 500 ms foreground tick (one probe message every 2 s, a counter bump per frame), at most 20 events per session (`telemetry/ui_stall.dart`) | branch (`feat/telemetry-ui-stall`, after `feat/telemetry-ss-resets`) |
| Opt-in diagnostics only (schema v21): `first_sync`, once per launch: when the first sync's request went out, when its response arrived and when it was applied (counted from launch), and how long the UI isolate was blocked until then (total, worst, stalls over 100 ms); the startup report also times the rooms' deferred state query vs. applying it, and building the room list. Times and counts only | — | branch (`feat/telemetry-startup-trace`, after `feat/telemetry-ui-stall`) |

## Leaving a call doesn't wait on a slow homeserver

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Hanging up waits at most 3 s for the "left the call" state event, then ends the call on screen and keeps retrying the clear in the background (2/5/10/30/60 s backoff, up to 10 min); upstream waited for it, so a slow homeserver kept people in the call for over a minute and each extra hang-up click started another leave. Hanging up twice reuses the pending clear, and rejoining the same room first waits for a clear in flight so it can't wipe the new membership (`matrix_rtc_leave.dart`) | testing (`fix/leave-call-background-state`) |

## Speaking in a call on another homeserver's SFU

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| lk-jwt-service 0.7+ gives users of homeservers it doesn't serve a listen-only LiveKit token, so joining a call whose elected SFU is another homeserver's heard everyone but every unmute timed out after 10 s (`TrackPublishException`, also Commet upstream), with no own tile and not counted in the call. When the call's token can't publish, we now publish on our own homeserver's SFU with a `multi_sfu` membership and listen on the call's SFU (the multi-SFU listener runs for that call even with the experiment off, and never migrates back to a listen-only SFU). With no SFU of our own, unmuting fails at once with a clear reason instead of hanging (`matrix_rtc_publish_rights.dart`, `matrix_livekit_backend.dart`, `matrix_rtc_multi_sfu.dart`, `matrix_livekit_voip_session.dart`) | queued (`fix/call-unmute-dead`) |
| Element Call participants with an opaque LiveKit identity (newer lk-jwt services hash it; no `:`) made the call's track handlers throw a RangeError, so their tracks got no tile (empty grey call view). Their user is now found by matching the identity hash against the call's memberships, falling back to the identity (`livekit_identity.dart`, `matrix_livekit_voip_session.dart`, `matrix_rtc_multi_sfu.dart`) | queued (`fix/call-unmute-dead`) |

## Shared history diagnostics (fix/shared-history-diagnostics, telemetry schema v24)

| Change | Why | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Messages from before you joined an encrypted room that the inviter's history bundle (MSC4268) listed as not shared now read "The sender didn't share this message with people who joined later" instead of "Failed to decrypt event", and the "Earlier messages were shared by …" note adds that some weren't, when that happened. SDK `vommet-v6.1.1-ss.12` keeps the bundle's `m.history_not_shared` session ids per room. Opt-in diagnostics only (schema v24): `history_share`, one per bundle sent or received and per new outbound session, with a fixed outcome word (sent, nothing shareable, invitee has no cross-signed devices, identity changed, imported, refused and why, shared / not shared / history visibility unknown) and counts of keys, withheld keys, skipped keys and invitee devices; `timeline_crypto` adds `utd_history_not_shared`. Never which room, who, keys or session ids (`telemetry/history_sharing_telemetry.dart`) | A tester invited to an encrypted room saw the "shared by" note but every earlier message still failed to decrypt, with nothing saying why or how many keys arrived | overlay (`fix/shared-history-diagnostics`) |
| The MSC4268 "may be shared with people invited later" flag on our message keys goes out under exactly one name, `org.matrix.msc3061.shared_history` (new keys, re-shares to added devices, key backup; SDK `vommet-v6.1.1-ss.14`). We still read all three names | Released matrix-rust-sdk (Element Web, Element X; up to matrix-sdk 0.19.1) reads only `m.shared_history` and the unstable name, so when an Element user invited someone, every message sent from Vommet was held back as not shared (Vommet issue 441). SDK ss.13 then wrote all three names, but matrix-rust-sdk reads them as aliases of one field and drops a key carrying two of them ("duplicate field"), so Element couldn't decrypt anything Vommet sent in a shared-history room, and those keys didn't restore from key backup there either | overlay (`fix/shared-history-diagnostics`) |
| Older messages restored from key backup keep decrypting after a restart (on the web: every page reload): a room key that arrives later for the same session, starting at a later message (sent to this device when someone writes again), no longer replaces the full copy restored from the backup. The SDK compares with the stored session, not only the ones in memory (SDK `vommet-v6.1.1-ss.16`, which also carries ss.15's faster own-device-list load) | After a reload the web app showed older messages as "Failed to decrypt" ("unknown message index") as soon as someone sent a new message (Vommet issue 353) | overlay (`fix/shared-history-diagnostics`) |
| Web (WebAssembly build): signing in works and the cross-signing / key backup state is right: SDK `vommet-v6.1.1-ss.17` (= ss.16 + 2 commits) reads whole numbers back from IndexedDB as `int` and no longer awaits on both sides of `&&` in cross-signing, key backup and verification code. No change on native or in the JS build | Under dart2wasm the browser's numbers arrive as `double`, so every `as int` on stored data threw; and dart2wasm miscompiles `&&` with an await on both sides (a false left side came back as `null` or `true`) | overlay (`fix/shared-history-diagnostics`) |
| Web (WebAssembly build): images, stickers and files from others load, and uploads go through: SDK `vommet-v6.1.1-ss.18` (= ss.17 + 1 commit) awaits once in `Client.authenticatedMediaSupported`. No change on native or in the JS build | dart2wasm also miscompiles `\|\|` with an await on both sides: it returned the `GetVersionsResponse` instead of a `bool`, so every authenticated media download and upload failed | overlay (`fix/shared-history-diagnostics`) |
| Messages sent from Vommet decrypt in Element again in rooms where they had stopped: a message key made by SDK ss.13 (the shared-history flag under all three names) is replaced by a new one on the next message, keys we forward on request carry one name, and a one-time pass rewrites backed-up keys that carry several names (the server's own copy, with one name). SDK `vommet-v6.1.1-ss.19` (= ss.18 + 1 commit) | ss.14 only fixed keys made after it. A room kept using its ss.13 key for up to 100 messages or a week, and devices that had dropped that key were never sent it again, so Element (Element X, Element Web) couldn't decrypt anything we sent there; restoring from key backup failed the same way (Vommet issue 519) | overlay (`fix/shared-history-diagnostics`) |
## Media spoilers, MSC4193 (feat/media-spoilers)

| Change | Why | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Pictures and videos can be sent and received as spoilers (MSC4193, not in the spec yet). Sending: the attachment dialog has a "Mark as spoiler" switch (off by default, pictures and videos only, "Blurred for everyone until they tap it.") with an optional reason; the preview blurs to match; Vommet sends only the unstable `page.codeberg.everypizza.msc4193.spoiler` (+ `.spoiler.reason`) keys. Reading: those and the stable `m.spoiler` / `m.spoiler.reason`. A received spoiler (incl. pictures sent as `m.file`) shows its blurhash or a plain fill with "Spoiler · Tap to reveal" and the reason; nothing is downloaded, decrypted or played until tapped. Revealing is per message, for this viewer, in memory only; a "Hide" chip covers it again. Spoilers stay out of media mosaics; the gallery, the Media tab and photo albums keep them covered until tapped; notifications, reply previews and the room list say "Image (spoiler)" / "Video (spoiler)" with no thumbnail or file name. Edits keep the keys (`utils/media_spoiler.dart`, `ui/atoms/media_spoiler_cover.dart`) | Testers saw Sable cover a picture as a spoiler that Vommet showed in the clear (Cinny and mautrix-discord send the same keys); operator approved implementing the MSC (10-14). Upstream Commet has an open issue for it and no PR | testing (overlay `feat/media-spoilers`) |

## Call leftovers, no-call-server message, reaction guard (fix/call-leftovers-and-errors)

| Change | Why | Status |

| At start (after the first sync) Vommet clears the call membership its own device left behind when the app was quit or killed mid-call, in every room, unless a call is running there. | Without it, homeservers lacking delayed events (MSC4140) kept showing you "in the call" for hours after quitting. | In testing |
| Starting a call on a homeserver with no call service now says so in plain words (and also reads the MSC4143 rtc/transports endpoint before giving up) instead of "Failed to find a valid LiveKit service". | Self-hosted servers without LiveKit gave a cryptic error. | In testing |
| The message menu no longer fails (taking the reaction button with it) when an emoji pack cannot be loaded; it falls back to the packs that load. | Reactions vanished in some rooms for one tester. | In testing |
## Linux notification markup

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Linux notifications escape message text, link titles, image alt text and the caller's name (`&`, `<`, `>`, and quotes in attributes) before they reach the notification daemon, and drop characters XML can't hold: on daemons that read the body as markup (dunst, KDE, xfce, mako), a message or name containing `<b>` or `<a href=...>` was rendered as formatting or a link. The daemon's "body-markup" capability is read once at startup; daemons without it get plain text and no formatting, and if the capabilities can't be read the body is escaped (`linux_notifier.dart`, `linux_notification_markup.dart`, `linux_notification_formatting.dart`) | testing (`fix/linux-notification-markup`) |

JPEG stays JPEG, other formats become PNG, and EXIF (location) is dropped. GIFs are left alone. Tapping the thumbnail no longer removes it | pending main (`feat/crop-attachment`) |

## Tray icon and close to tray on Linux

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Linux gets a system tray icon (Vommet issue 454): a StatusNotifierItem with a dbusmenu menu, both served over D-Bus in pure Dart (package:dbus, already a dependency), so there's no native library and no CI image or Flatpak module change; the Flatpak only gains `--talk-name=org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher`. It shows on hosts like KDE Plasma, Waybar, XFCE and GNOME with the AppIndicator extension, and only when a tray host is present. A left click shows or hides the window; the menu has Show/Hide and Quit. Settings › Window Behaviour gets "Show tray icon" (on) and "Close to tray" (off): with the second one on, closing the window hides it (off the taskbar too) while the icon is shown, and `--minimize` starts hidden in the tray. A logout or shutdown still quits, and if the tray goes away while the window is hidden the window comes back (`utils/tray/linux_tray.dart`, `utils/tray/app_tray.dart`, `window_close_handler.dart`, `window_management.dart`, `window_settings.dart`). ## SVG avatars

| Change | Issue | Status |
|---|---|---|
| SVG avatars, room and space icons, banners and emotes show instead of nothing. Servers can't thumbnail SVG (Synapse answers 400), so when a thumbnail is refused the original is fetched if it is an SVG of at most 1 MiB (the download stops after 4 KiB if it isn't one), and SVGs are drawn to a PNG on the device with flutter_svg. Before drawing, the SVG is checked: under 20,000 elements once `<use>`/`url(#id)` references are expanded, no reference loops, no DTD entities, at most 2048 px a side; anything else shows the placeholder. flutter_svg never fetches anything (`<image>` only from `data:` URIs) (`utils/image/svg_image.dart`, `matrix_svg_download.dart`, `matrix_mxc_image_provider.dart`, unit test `svg_image_test.dart`) | Vommet issue 309 | branch (`fix/309-svg-avatars`, after `fix/banner-thumbnail-scale`) |

## iOS and macOS builds

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| iOS: Podfile no longer declares a `RunnerTests` target, which the stock Runner project doesn't have, so `pod install` works (issue 43) | topic (`fix/ios-macos-build`) |
| iOS deployment target 11.0 → 15.0 (Runner project, Podfile, and every pod in `post_install`): Xcode 27 builds nothing older (issue 461) | topic (`fix/ios-macos-build`) |
| macOS deployment target 10.15 → 12.0 (Runner project, Podfile, and every pod in `post_install`): Xcode 27 builds nothing older (issue 461) | topic (`fix/ios-macos-build`) |
| macOS `Podfile.lock` updated: sqlite3 3.51.1 → 3.52.0 (sqlite3_flutter_libs now requires ~> 3.52.0, so `pod install` failed), WebRTC-SDK 137.7151.04 → 150.7871.01 (flutter_webrtc's constraint) (issue 43) | topic (`fix/ios-macos-build`) |
| macOS: `rust_lib_commet.podspec` links libc++ and Accelerate, which whisper.cpp (voice transcription, issue 70) needs; the app failed to link without them (issue 462) | topic (`fix/ios-macos-build`) |
| vodozemac is initialised through `flutter_vodozemac`, which loads `flutter_vodozemac.framework` on iOS and macOS; the plain `vodozemac` init looked for `vodozemac_bindings_dart`, so on Apple platforms E2EE was off and OIDC login failed (issue 459) | topic (`fix/ios-macos-build`) |
| iOS and macOS use the system emoji font (Apple Color Emoji) instead of the bundled Twemoji COLR font, whose glyphs Apple's text stack draws blank, so emoji in messages, reactions and the verification screen show up again (issue 463) | topic (`fix/ios-macos-build`) |
| iOS `Info.plist` explains why Vommet uses the camera, the microphone and the photo library (`NS…UsageDescription`); without them iOS killed the app as soon as a call, a voice message or a photo picker asked for access (issue 43) | topic (`fix/ios-macos-build`) |
| macOS: microphone and camera usage descriptions in `Info.plist` and the sandbox entitlements `device.audio-input` and `device.camera`; without them macOS killed the app when it joined a call (issue 43) | topic (`fix/ios-macos-build`) |
| iOS and macOS: name Vommet (iOS display name and bundle name, macOS `Vommet.app`) and app id `im.nether.chat`, like Android, Linux and Windows (also the macOS display name and the Runner scheme; was `chat.commet.commetapp`, `.macos` on macOS), so the fork installs beside Commet there too (issue 43) | topic (`fix/ios-macos-build`) |

|---|---|
| The Flatpak no longer asks for NetworkManager on the system bus (`--system-talk-name=org.freedesktop.NetworkManager` dropped from `im.nether.chat.yaml`). On Linux `connectivity_plus`'s backend is replaced at startup (`lib/utils/linux_connectivity.dart`): the Flatpak asks the desktop portal's NetworkMonitor (`GetAvailable`, `changed`), other Linux builds ask NetworkManager and then the portal, and when neither answers within 3 s the network counts as up. Without this, the check never completed once the bus was gone, so LiveKit (which awaits it before joining a call) stalled. The widget runner skips `network_info_plus`'s NetworkManager lookup in the Flatpak (else time-limited) and uses the interface list. Vommet issue 340 | branch (`fix/340-flatpak-network-portal-rebased`) |

|---|---|---|
| Experiment (Settings › Experiments › Chat and messages › Forward messages, off by default): Telegram-style forwarding. Tapping the bar shows a preview with Hide sender name, Hide caption (media with a caption), Change recipient, Apply changes and Do not forward. Text typed with it is sent first, then the forward. With the sender shown the event follows MSC4553 under its unstable prefix `org.matrix.msc4553.forwarded` (origin + a copy of the original content; other clients see a "Forwarded from … - view original message" fallback); with it hidden it is a plain copy. Received MSC4553 forwards render the original with a "Forwarded from" header and can't be edited; MSC2723 (`com.famedly.app.forwarded`) forwards get the header only. Stickers always forward as a copy (MSC4553 covers messages only). Hide caption also changes the copy in `content`, which MSC4553 otherwise says to keep unchanged. Media whose body is empty or missing forwards with its filename as the body (no caption). Pending forwards are kept per room in memory. (`client/matrix/forwarding/`, `ui/organisms/forward_message/`, chat/composer/message layout hooks). Upstream request: commetchat/commet#336 (no upstream PR) | — | testing (`feat/forward-messages`, after `feat/room-picker-search`) |

## Voice isolation

| Change | Issue | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Experiment "Noise suppression" (Settings › Experiments; off by default), then Settings › Voice › Audio Settings › "Noise suppression" (Linux, Windows, Android): Automatic (default once opted in) benchmarks DeepFilterNet3 in the background and falls back to RNNoise if it runs late in a call; Standard runs RNNoise 0.2 (BSD-3); Best runs DeepFilterNet3 (MIT/Apache-2.0, network implemented in Rust, no inference runtime); Basic keeps only WebRTC's own suppressor. Both engines live in the `rust/voice` crate (vendored RNNoise in `third_party/rnnoise` plus our `os_support.h`, which the 0.2 release omits; DeepFilterNet3 weights in `third_party/deepfilternet`), linked into `rust_lib_commet` on desktop and built as `libvommet_voice.so` on Android by the `rust/voice_builder` plugin, which also registers it with flutter_webrtc's capture post-processing. Dart reaches it through `dart:ffi`. They run on the microphone inside libwebrtc's capture pipeline, and WebRTC's own suppressor is turned off while they do. It needs `setCapturePostProcessor` (desktop) from our flutter_webrtc fork, branch `vommet-1.6` of [nether/vommet-flutter-webrtc](https://nether.codes/nether/vommet-flutter-webrtc), which also carries the screen-share audio changes; stacked after `feat/screenshare-audio-linux`, whose override it moves to that branch. `integration_test/voip/voice_filter_test.dart` checks it end to end; a comment on `WebrtcDefaultDevices.initDummyConnection` records why that connection must stay open (Linux audio-device restart bug) | #3 | branch (`feat/voice-isolation`) |

## Native OIDC sign-in

| Change | Issue | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Native OIDC sign-in (MSC2964/2965/2966/2967): when the homeserver publishes `/_matrix/client/v1/auth_metadata`, the login screen shows one "Continue" button that opens the server's sign-in page in the browser, instead of the single sign-on buttons; "Sign in with a password instead" stays. One path at a time: while the password form is open, the browser buttons hide and the link reads "Sign in with your browser instead" (two look-alike "Login" and "Continue" buttons confused testers). Vommet registers itself as a native client (`client_uri` https://vommet.app) with a loopback redirect `http://127.0.0.1:<random port>/oauth/callback` on Linux/Windows and `app.vommet:/oauth` on Android/iOS/macOS (new Android intent filter); not offered on web. Code exchange and token refresh are Vommet's own, because the SDK reads `expires_in` as milliseconds; only OIDC sessions get the refresh handler (`onSoftLogout`), so password and SSO sessions behave as before | #45 | testing (`feat/native-oidc`) |

Gives up after 10 minutes with no redirect. Release builds get the `com.apple.security.network.server` sandbox entitlement for the listener | Vommet issue 510 | pending (`review/feat/native-oidc-next`) |

## Quieter notifications only while you're chatting elsewhere

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| "Silence Notifications" (on by default, Android) quieted every notification while any other device of the account had been seen in the last 10 minutes; a desktop client or browser tab left open keeps that fresh, so one account could stay silent for good. Now a notification is only quieted when another device was seen in the last 5 minutes AND your latest message or reaction in that same room is from the last 5 minutes AND it wasn't sent from this device (the app records the IDs of events it sent, `push_notification/sent_here.dart`, so no clocks are compared). The check fetches only your own recent events and gives up after 3 s; on any error or delay it notifies normally (`modifiers/suppress_other_device_active.dart`, unit test `notification_quiet_other_device_test.dart`). The setting is now called "Quiet notifications while I'm chatting on another device", its description says what on and off do, and a "Right now: …" line under it says whether another of your devices is online (rechecked every minute while shown; `quiet_status.dart`) | testing (`fix/notify-silence-active-chat`) |
## Notifications from every account

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| With several accounts signed in, pushes for all of them arrive (they share one UnifiedPush endpoint). The account a push is for is read from the Matrix push's `devices[].data.local_client_id`, where homeservers put it and UnifiedPush gateways forward it; only Commet's own gateway flattened it to the top level, the one place the app looked. The fallback (which account has the room) now asks the running accounts first, and its background cache is rewritten whenever rooms or accounts change instead of only at startup, so a push for a room joined later isn't dropped | topic (`fix/push-account-routing`) |
## Push registrations

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Settings › Notifications lists the account's push registrations to everyone (was developer mode only): each with its push server, the session it belongs to and that session's last activity ("probably" when matched by name), a note on Commet's push server entries (only the Commet app gets those; keep them if Commet is used on that device), and Remove (with a confirmation; not for this device's own). Vommet's registrations now carry the session's device id, and at startup Vommet removes its own registrations (only ones carrying its namespaced device-id key, so never Commet's, which share the app id) whose session is signed out or unused for 90 days; standard client APIs only, so any homeserver (a device that comes back registers again). Raw pusher data stays behind developer mode | topic (`fix/pusher-housekeeping`) |

## Notification diagnostics (telemetry schema v9)

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Opt-in diagnostics only: `notify_setup` is now recorded once per account (numbered by position, `account_index`/`accounts`; room counts per account) instead of only the first, and a new `notify_counts` event reports what happened to notifications since the last report: shown, quieted (another device / other rule), dropped (room open, Do Not Disturb, notifications off, other rule), "couldn't show" notices, failures, and handling time. The counters live in shared preferences so the background push isolate can add to them, are only written while diagnostics are on, and are deleted when diagnostics are turned off or "Delete my diagnostics" is used (`telemetry/notify_counts.dart`, hook in `NotificationManager.notify`). Counts only, never rooms, senders or content. Only notifications that reach `NotificationManager.notify` are counted (pushes lost before that, or handled before preferences load, aren't) | testing (`feat/telemetry-notify-counts`) |

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| On Linux, full-size images are decoded within a pixel-count and longest-side limit instead of a fixed 1440 px height, so tall images (e.g. an 800x19600 screenshot, which became 59 px wide) keep a readable width; the image viewer decodes its own, much larger copy so a popped-out image stays sharp when zoomed | testing (`fix/linux-image-fullres`) |

## Picture gallery

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Experiment "Picture gallery": with a picture or video open from a room, Left/Right arrow keys (or a swipe on touch screens; a drag pans instead while zoomed in) move through the room's loaded pictures and videos, loading older ones at the start; Esc closes; shows "3 / 8" and the sender, preloads the neighbours, and has edge arrows on hover on desktop. Banners, avatars and link previews still open on their own | testing (`feat/lightbox-gallery`) |

## Picture gallery stays on the opened picture while the room loads

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| A picture opened in the "Picture gallery" viewer no longer flickers through other pictures while the room is still loading: older pictures arriving in front of it used to shift the page view for one frame before it caught up; the viewer now moves its scroll offset with the shift before redrawing (`lightbox_gallery.dart`) | testing (`feat/lightbox-gallery`) |

## Picture gallery: a pinch zooms instead of turning the page

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| In the "Picture gallery" viewer a two-finger pinch now always zooms the picture: the swipe to the next or previous picture steps aside as soon as a second finger touches (or a trackpad gesture starts scaling), instead of winning when the first finger had already slid a little. One-finger swipes still turn the page (`lightbox_gallery.dart`, `unit_test/lightbox_pinch_zoom_test.dart`) | testing (`feat/lightbox-gallery`) |
## Attachment dialog: "Remove hidden info", explained

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Attachment dialog: "Send Original" (which read like a compression switch) is now "Remove hidden info", on by default, for JPEG/PNG/WebP/BMP, listing what was found (location, camera or phone model, serial number, date taken, a name, software); PNG text chunks (author, AI prompts, XMP) are now removed too. Videos, GIFs, HEIC, PDFs and documents get an honest "Vommet can't remove hidden info from this kind of file" note (videos were shown the switch but never stripped). A "What's this?" link explains metadata per file type, with examples such as a Google Docs PDF carrying your account name (`attachment_processor.dart`, `metadata_explainer.dart`) | testing (`feat/strip-metadata-explained`) |

## Encryption markers

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| One icon right after a room's name says whether it is encrypted: nothing when it is, a grey crossed-out padlock when it isn't (public or invite-only), an amber one for a direct message that isn't encrypted, a green shield for a direct message with someone you verified; tap it for a short explanation with a link to the help page. The topic moves to its own line under the name, with an 8 px gap before the header buttons. The message box says "Send an unencrypted message" (with a crossed-out padlock) in rooms that aren't encrypted, and the call lobby uses the same marker. On by default, switchable on the Experiments page (Vommet issue 131) | `feat/encryption-markers` |

## Trust warnings in direct messages

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Vommet remembers each direct-message partner's identity key; when it changes, a red shield appears after their name and a strip above the message box says someone could be impersonating them (It was them / Verify). If they never set up secure messaging, a dismissible banner says Vommet can't confirm it's really them (What does this mean? / Let them know, which drafts a friendly heads-up), and starting a new direct message with them asks first. Sending something that decodes as a Matrix recovery key stops with "That looks like a recovery key" (Don't send it / It's not mine, send anyway). On by default, switchable on the Experiments page (Vommet issue 130). The same pins also stop room history from being sent to someone whose identity changed when you invite them (MSC4268), until you press It was them or verify them | `feat/dm-trust-warnings` |
| An identity Vommet pinned whose master key disappears (a server can serve a contact's keys without it, and add a device of its own) counts as changed (red strip and shield) instead of the dismissible "not set up" banner; keys not fetched yet (fresh sign-in, cleared cache) stay unknown until they are. It was them with no master key forgets the pin (`identity_pins.dart`) | `feat/dm-trust-warnings` |

## Secure messaging setup at sign-in (Vommet issue 129)

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Right after sign-in and before any room opens, accounts that need it get a plain-language secure messaging setup (cross-signing + key backup; the UI never says "cross-signing"). New account: welcome → choose how to save the recovery key (encrypted password manager, recommended, via the system save prompt with a Google Password Manager caveat when Android's autofill service is Google; a 6-word phrase from the EFF large wordlist, with "Copy to clipboard" and, on Android/Apple only, "Save to password manager"; or an own recovery password with a strength meter and a warning when it's the login password, known only right after a password sign-in, kept in memory as a salted hash) → confirm you really have it (autofill/paste the key, type 2 phrase words, retype the password) → done. Existing account on a new device: approve from another device (existing emoji verification) or enter the recovery key/phrase/password, then all message keys are fetched from the backup (fixes upstream Commet issue 1046). Lost everything: a separate start-over path behind a hold-to-confirm. Skip is warned twice (the second says it's for developers, hold to skip) and leaves a reminder banner at the top of the room list; Settings › Security gets a "Set up secure messaging" button. "Still have your recovery key?" check-ins after 3 days, then monthly. Screenshots are blocked while a key or phrase is on screen (Android FLAG_SECURE). 4 offline explainer cards, "Read the full guide" → vommet.app/help/secure-messaging. Accounts already set up never see a screen (judged from local state first). Keys are only ever created when the server confirms nothing exists (no master key, no secret storage, no backup; a failed check counts as "don't know", never "nothing"); only the explicit start-over and "make a new key" paths replace an identity, and "make a new key" keeps the message backup. Shared: closing the account-confirmation (UIA) dialog cancels the request instead of leaving it waiting forever, SSO gets an "I've finished in the browser" retry, and the account-page approval stage for OIDC accounts (stable m.oauth and unstable org.matrix.cross_signing_reset, MSC4312) is supported. On by default; experiment `experiment_secure_setup` (Chat and messages) only so it can be turned off for crash triage. Shared `SecureMessaging` own-trust-state helper (`client/matrix/secure_messaging_state.dart`) for Vommet issue 130 (`ui/pages/secure_setup/`, `VommetSecureScreen.kt`, unit test `secure_setup_test.dart`) | testing (`feat/secure-setup`) |
| Settings › Security for a device that isn't confirmed yet (account already set up): the panel (now "Encryption & recovery") leads with a "Confirm this device" card, "Enter recovery key" opening the setup straight at the key step and "Use another device instead" straight into approval; the rows read "Device confirmation" (its button enters the key instead of a red "Reset") and "Message history backup"; the "Unverified" alert and "Set up secure messaging" (now only for accounts never set up) give way to it. Before, entering the key hid behind "Message backup › Restore" | testing (`feat/secure-setup`) |
| Settings › Security › "Replace my recovery key" (set-up accounts): pick "I want a new recovery key" (enter the current key/phrase/password; every secret moves under a new key, same identity and same backup, so contacts see no change and the old key stops working) or "Someone may have used my key" (new key, new identity, new backup holding every message key this device has, then a change-password step: the account page for OIDC accounts, otherwise current/new password with "Also sign me out everywhere else" on by default). Integration suite `integration_test/secure_setup_runner.dart` against the CI homeserver: fresh accounts per test; own-password setup through the real account-password dialog and confirm step, skip (both warnings, interrupted hold), recovery key on a new device restoring history, approval from another device, replace key / someone used my key / make a new key (each checked by decrypting old history on a new raw device), nothing replaced without consent, a closed password dialog never hangs setup (`ui/pages/secure_setup/change_password.dart`) | testing (`feat/secure-setup`) |
| Fixes found by that suite: after a fresh sign-in the setup never appeared (the status check waited for a first sync that's only started for saved sessions, timed out after 30 s, read "unknown" and closed itself; now it waits for the client's own first sync); setup could handle the first step twice ("Wrong State" on accounts with existing secret storage); the two skip warnings and the recovery-key check-in threw a layout assertion on desktop (now a plain `SetupDialog`, max 420 wide, laid out at phone and desktop width by `unit_test/secure_setup_dialogs_test.dart`); button labels shrink to fit instead of overflowing. Log lines for the sign-in decision and each unlock step (no ids) | testing (`feat/secure-setup`) |
| A recovery key copied for a password manager comes off the clipboard again when setup is left any way (skip, close), not only after the confirm step; same for Commet's own cross-signing setup page under Settings › Security (`recovery_key_clipboard.dart`, `secure_setup_flow.dart`, `cross_signing_view.dart`) | testing (`feat/secure-setup`) |

## Room threads

| Change | Status |
