| Threads list: every thread in the room, newest activity first, with who started it, its first message, the reply count and the newest reply; "All threads" / "My threads" filter (threads you started or replied in); loads more as you scroll and refreshes when a thread gets a reply. Opens from the room's Threads button (next to Pinned Messages) or, with the Discord-style layout, the member panel's Threads tab. Uses the server's `/threads` API (Matrix v1.4) | branch (`feat/room-threads`, after `feat/member-panel-tabs`) |
| A thread opened from the list closes back to the list; the member panel remembers its open tab per room | branch (`feat/room-threads`) |
| A thread whose root isn't in the server's relations response (servers other than Synapse leave out `original_event`) fetches the root itself, so threads opened from the list show their first message | branch (`feat/room-threads`) |
| Settings › Experiments › Chat and messages › Read state per thread (off by default): threaded read receipts (MSC3771) — reading a thread marks only that thread read, the main timeline sends `main` receipts so opening the room no longer marks every thread read, and the Threads list marks threads with unread replies (dot, bold). Marking the whole room read from the room list stays unthreaded | branch (`feat/room-threads`) |

## Thread view keeps every reply

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| An open thread no longer loses replies: a reply attaching to the root made the thread view write the root over its newest reply (root shown at the bottom, replies missing). Pages stay newest first without duplicates, and a short thread opens with its root on Tuwunel, which hands out a next page token even on the last page. The Threads list hides a thread whose root was deleted and has no replies left | branch (`feat/room-threads`) |

## Thread view lists each message once

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| An open thread no longer shows messages twice or replies above the root: thread messages the room timeline announces again (as it pages through the same messages) refresh their copy in the thread instead of being added, and new ones are placed by time | branch (`feat/room-threads`) |
## Block users

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Settings › Experiments › Chat and messages › Block users (off by default): Block / Unblock in a person's profile menu (with a confirmation saying what it does), and Settings › Security › Blocked users listing everyone you've blocked with Unblock buttons, plus blocking by Matrix ID. Uses the account's `m.ignored_user_list`, so the server drops their messages, invites and calls and other Matrix apps honour it; unlike the SDK's `ignoreUser` it doesn't clear the cache or leave DMs | branch (`feat/block-users`, after `fix/profile-nickname-others`) |
| Messages from blocked users already in the local cache are hidden too (whether blocked here or in another app), and appear or disappear in open rooms as soon as the list changes, also when it changes on another device. Messages they sent while blocked aren't fetched back after unblocking | branch (`feat/block-users`) |
| Upstream fix: a timeline entry recomputes its collapsed state on every update, so a message that stops being hidden (e.g. after unblocking) draws again instead of staying an empty collapsed row | branch (`feat/block-users`) |
| Fix: the block list is read again once the account's data has loaded, so blocked users stay hidden after a restart (the list was read before the SDK had loaded it, so it came up empty until the server next sent it) | branch (`feat/block-users`) |
| Fix: room previews (room lists, quick switcher) leave out a blocked user's last message, and blocking or unblocking updates them right away instead of keeping the old text until the next message | branch (`feat/block-users`) |

## Performance diagnostics breakdown (telemetry schema v11)

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Opt-in diagnostics only: `frame_stats` gains the UI thread's (build) and GPU thread's (raster) slowest-5% and worst times, so a slow frame shows whether Dart work or drawing cost it. New `loop_lag` event: how often and how long the UI event loop is blocked (a 500 ms timer's lateness, foreground only; `telemetry/loop_lag.dart`). New `sync_stats` event: how many sync responses were applied and how long applying them took (`telemetry/sync_stats.dart`). `sync_initial` and `sync_error` gain `own_server`: whether the account is on nether.im (a fixed name compared in the app, never sent), never which other server. Numbers and booleans only, reported with the 15-minute perf summary | branch (`feat/telemetry-perf-v11`, after `feat/telemetry-name-tag`) |

| A thread card asks the server for the thread's reply count and newest reply instead of trusting the summary stored with the first message, which stays as it was when first downloaded (a deleted reply, or a server that later fixed its counts, left the card saying "3 replies" with the deleted text). ## Database and sync-contents diagnostics (telemetry schema v14)

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Opt-in diagnostics only: the database layer's timers (how many times each kind of database operation ran and how long it took, e.g. storing an event) now ship with the startup report and every 15-minute perf summary (as the time added since the last one). They had always shipped empty, because the database package names them in plain English ("Store event update") and only identifier-shaped timer names pass; those names come from a fixed list, so they are made identifiers. `sync_stats` also counts what the window's syncs contained (rooms, timeline events, state events) and how many events the slowest sync carried. Numbers only | branch (`feat/telemetry-db-timers`, after `fix/69-space-nicknames`) |

## One call per room, however often you tap Call

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Tapping Call again while a join is still connecting (it takes seconds on Android) no longer makes a second session for the same room: a join while one runs, or while you're already in that room's call, returns that call; starting a call notifies the room once. Each LiveKit call also gets its own session id instead of `""`, so two calls never share one mute state, and ending one no longer drops the other from the call list. Before, the duplicate showed as two call cards whose mute buttons acted on a different connection from the one the call heard (Vommet issue 167) (`matrix_livekit_backend.dart`, `matrix_livekit_voip_session.dart`, `matrix_room_call_component.dart`) | queued (`fix/call-double-join`) |

## Call membership refresh

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Our call membership (`org.matrix.msc3401.call.member`) is re-posted every hour while we're in a call, keeping `created_ts` and growing `expires`, the way matrix-js-sdk does. Before, one post with `expires` = 4 h was never renewed, so Element Call and Element X dropped a Vommet member (and stopped sharing media keys with them) four hours into a call. Expiry everywhere (focus election, text-room call bar, room activities) now counts from `created_ts`, falling back to the event timestamp, and the legacy (experiment off) SFU election orders members by `created_ts` with ties on the state key, like Element Call, instead of by the latest post | testing (`fix/rtc-membership-refresh`) |
## Experiments are opt-out

| Change | Status |

Sliding sync, read state per thread and nicknames per space stay opt-in, and a new entry can set `optIn: true` (`ExperimentRegistry.applyDefaults` → `BoolPreference.defaultOnKeys`, run from `Preferences.init`) | testing (`feat/experiments-opt-out`) |

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| New Settings › Data and storage tab (not on web, which has no file cache) with a Telegram-style Storage usage page: a donut and a list of what the media cache holds by type (images, videos, GIFs, files, other; read from each file's first bytes, since the cache stores no type), clearing the chosen types after a confirmation, the database size shown but never cleared, and sliders for "Media cache limit" (500 MB to 10 GB or unlimited, the default; least recently opened media goes first) and "Remove media not opened for" (1 day to 1 month or forever; 5 days stays the default, replacing Commet's fixed 5 days). The startup clean-up now runs 30 s after startup instead of during it. Clearing and clean-up only ever delete regular files inside the media cache directory (symlinks resolved, never followed) and forget a row only once its file is gone. Vommet issue 75, storage half (`file_cache.dart`, `drift_file_cache.dart`, `data_storage_settings_page.dart`, `main.dart`) | testing (`fix/75-cache-management`) |

## Wake-from-idle diagnostics (telemetry schema v16)

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Opt-in diagnostics only: a `resume` event after the app comes back from at least 30 s in the background: how long it was away, how many accounts had a sync request already open and how old the oldest was, how long until the first and the last account finished a sync, and how many sync errors (and timeouts) happened in between. Checks whether a request left open while the device slept holds up new messages after waking (`telemetry/resume_telemetry.dart`). Durations and counts only | branch (`feat/telemetry-resume`, after `feat/telemetry-image-cache`) |
| Room keys are looked up for backup only after a new one was stored, instead of after every sync: that lookup is a database query (100–270 ms on a phone) and it queued with the sync's own writes. SDK fork `vommet-v6.1.1-ss.8` (ss.7 + this) | — | branch (`perf/sdk-key-upload-gate`, after `perf/drift-db-fragment-cache`) |
| Checking for unsent messages (Offline sending, at startup) reads only a room's unsent list instead of loading and decoding its whole list of stored message ids: on a 209-room account that was ~110 ms per room, competing with the startup loads behind the splash. Unsent messages in a room with no stored history yet are no longer skipped. Drift store fork `vommet-v6.1.1-db.2` (db.1 + this) | — | branch (`perf/sdk-key-upload-gate`) |
| Saving new messages to the on-device database is lighter: the app used to re-read and re-write a room's whole list of cached message ids for every single message in a sync, and open a nested database transaction per message (each a round trip to the database isolate); now the list is edited in memory and written once per sync, with no nested transactions. Measured 1.5–2.6× faster per sync on a desktop, more on phones (drift store fork tag vommet-v6.1.1-db.1) | — | testing (`feat/sliding-sync`) |

## Debugging and performance diagnostics (telemetry schema v17)

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Opt-in diagnostics only: new `message_send` event per text message, reply, edit, thread message, reaction, redaction and sticker (message length in characters, whether it had formatting, how many people it mentioned, time spent on markdown, time the SDK took to send with its retries, outcome and error kind; never the text or who). New `http_stats` 15-minute summaries per kind of homeserver request (sync, send, media download/thumbnail/upload, keys, profile, state, history, members, push, account data...): count, errors, p95 and worst time, bytes received, and whether it was the user's own server. The kind comes from the shape of the URL's path; the URL is never kept (`telemetry/telemetry_http.dart`, handed to the SDK as its http client). New `call_stats` once a minute during a LiveKit call: connection quality word, participants, how many remote participants report poor quality, packets received and lost, jitter, concealed audio (audible glitches), bitrate, round-trip time, video frame rate and size, and whether a screen share is on (`telemetry/call_stats.dart`). New `crypto_state` once per account: encryption on, cross-signing and key backup set up and their secrets cached, this device verified, device counts (unverified, blocked), room counts (encrypted). New `memory_pressure` event when the OS asks for memory (RSS, image cache, open timelines, foreground). `timeline_crypto` adds why messages couldn't be decrypted (no key, corrupted channel, requestable; counts from the SDK's fixed phrases). `sync_stats` adds foreground gaps between finished syncs (worst, how many over 90 s). `perf_summary` adds open timelines, database size on disk, dropped/overflowed diagnostic events, server clock skew. `app_ready` gains the startup steps' timers (they had never shipped: the general timers are English phrases, now mapped from a fixed list to identifiers; a timer with an account name in it stays out). The report envelope gains total memory, low-RAM flag (Android), screen size and pixel density, text scale and accessibility toggles (bold text, reduce motion, high contrast), the Linux desktop family and software-GL flag. Numbers, booleans and fixed-list values only; the privacy page lists it all | branch (`feat/telemetry-v17-debug`, after `feat/telemetry-resume`) |
| Opt-in diagnostics only (schema v18): Android crash reports carry the build id and the frames' offsets into the app's own instructions (`i+<hex>`/`v+<hex>`), because the APK is built with `--split-debug-info` and its Dart stack traces are non-symbolic, so every Android crash arrived with no location. `flutter symbolize` with that build's symbols turns them into file:line. Repeat-counting now also tells Android crashes apart by their top offset | branch (`feat/telemetry-v17-debug`) |
| Opt-in diagnostics only: the startup report's timers also include how long the splash waited for the rooms' state, the deferred room-state loads, and the time to the first frame since launch (they were missing from the fixed list; the room count in the deferred loads' name is dropped) | branch (`feat/telemetry-v17-debug`) |

## Telemetry: freezes as they happen

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Opt-in diagnostics only (schema v20): a `ui_stall` event the moment the app freezes for 5 s or more, flushed at once so a force-quit doesn't lose it. Kinds: `loop` (the Dart event loop was blocked, reported when it ends), `platform` (the platform/window thread, which on Linux also delivers input and draws, hasn't answered a no-op probe; reported while stuck and when it recovers), `frame` (a frame was requested but none started while focused). Carries the duration, whether it's still ongoing, foreground, whether a call is active, seconds since the last call ended and that call's peak participants. Rides LoopLag's existing 500 ms foreground tick (one probe message every 2 s, a counter bump per frame), at most 20 events per session (`telemetry/ui_stall.dart`) | branch (`feat/telemetry-ui-stall`, after `feat/telemetry-ss-resets`) |
| Opt-in diagnostics only (schema v21): `first_sync`, once per launch: when the first sync's request went out, when its response arrived and when it was applied (counted from launch), and how long the UI isolate was blocked until then (total, worst, stalls over 100 ms); the startup report also times the rooms' deferred state query vs. applying it, and building the room list. Times and counts only | — | branch (`feat/telemetry-startup-trace`, after `feat/telemetry-ui-stall`) |

## Leaving a call doesn't wait on a slow homeserver

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Hanging up waits at most 3 s for the "left the call" state event, then ends the call on screen and keeps retrying the clear in the background (2/5/10/30/60 s backoff, up to 10 min); upstream waited for it, so a slow homeserver kept people in the call for over a minute and each extra hang-up click started another leave. Hanging up twice reuses the pending clear, and rejoining the same room first waits for a clear in flight so it can't wipe the new membership (`matrix_rtc_leave.dart`) | testing (`fix/leave-call-background-state`) |

## Speaking in a call on another homeserver's SFU

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| lk-jwt-service 0.7+ gives users of homeservers it doesn't serve a listen-only LiveKit token, so joining a call whose elected SFU is another homeserver's heard everyone but every unmute timed out after 10 s (`TrackPublishException`, also Commet upstream), with no own tile and not counted in the call. When the call's token can't publish, we now publish on our own homeserver's SFU with a `multi_sfu` membership and listen on the call's SFU (the multi-SFU listener runs for that call even with the experiment off, and never migrates back to a listen-only SFU). With no SFU of our own, unmuting fails at once with a clear reason instead of hanging (`matrix_rtc_publish_rights.dart`, `matrix_livekit_backend.dart`, `matrix_rtc_multi_sfu.dart`, `matrix_livekit_voip_session.dart`) | queued (`fix/call-unmute-dead`) |
| Element Call participants with an opaque LiveKit identity (newer lk-jwt services hash it; no `:`) made the call's track handlers throw a RangeError, so their tracks got no tile (empty grey call view). Their user is now found by matching the identity hash against the call's memberships, falling back to the identity (`livekit_identity.dart`, `matrix_livekit_voip_session.dart`, `matrix_rtc_multi_sfu.dart`) | queued (`fix/call-unmute-dead`) |

## Voice message transcription

The plugin also ships the NDK's `libc++_shared.so` (whisper.cpp links it; nothing else in the APK carries it). SDK `vommet-v6.1.1-ss.12` keeps the bundle's `m.history_not_shared` session ids per room. Opt-in diagnostics only (schema v24): `history_share`, one per bundle sent or received and per new outbound session, with a fixed outcome word (sent, nothing shareable, invitee has no cross-signed devices, identity changed, imported, refused and why, shared / not shared / history visibility unknown) and counts of keys, withheld keys, skipped keys and invitee devices; `timeline_crypto` adds `utd_history_not_shared`. | The MSC4268 "may be shared with people invited later" flag on our message keys goes out under exactly one name, `org.matrix.msc3061.shared_history` (new keys, re-shares to added devices, key backup; SDK `vommet-v6.1.1-ss.14`). We still read all three names | Released matrix-rust-sdk (Element Web, Element X; up to matrix-sdk 0.19.1) reads only `m.shared_history` and the unstable name, so when an Element user invited someone, every message sent from Vommet was held back as not shared (Vommet issue 441). SDK ss.13 then wrote all three names, but matrix-rust-sdk reads them as aliases of one field and drops a key carrying two of them ("duplicate field"), so Element couldn't decrypt anything Vommet sent in a shared-history room, and those keys didn't restore from key backup there either | overlay (`fix/shared-history-diagnostics`) |
| Older messages restored from key backup keep decrypting after a restart (on the web: every page reload): a room key that arrives later for the same session, starting at a later message (sent to this device when someone writes again), no longer replaces the full copy restored from the backup. The SDK compares with the stored session, not only the ones in memory (SDK `vommet-v6.1.1-ss.16`, which also carries ss.15's faster own-device-list load) | After a reload the web app showed older messages as "Failed to decrypt" ("unknown message index") as soon as someone sent a new message (Vommet issue 353) | overlay (`fix/shared-history-diagnostics`) |
| Web (WebAssembly build): signing in works and the cross-signing / key backup state is right: SDK `vommet-v6.1.1-ss.17` (= ss.16 + 2 commits) reads whole numbers back from IndexedDB as `int` and no longer awaits on both sides of `&&` in cross-signing, key backup and verification code. No change on native or in the JS build | Under dart2wasm the browser's numbers arrive as `double`, so every `as int` on stored data threw; and dart2wasm miscompiles `&&` with an await on both sides (a false left side came back as `null` or `true`) | overlay (`fix/shared-history-diagnostics`) |
| Web (WebAssembly build): images, stickers and files from others load, and uploads go through: SDK `vommet-v6.1.1-ss.18` (= ss.17 + 1 commit) awaits once in `Client.authenticatedMediaSupported`. | Messages sent from Vommet decrypt in Element again in rooms where they had stopped: a message key made by SDK ss.13 (the shared-history flag under all three names) is replaced by a new one on the next message, keys we forward on request carry one name, and a one-time pass rewrites backed-up keys that carry several names (the server's own copy, with one name). SDK `vommet-v6.1.1-ss.19` (= ss.18 + 1 commit) | ss.14 only fixed keys made after it. A room kept using its ss.13 key for up to 100 messages or a week, and devices that had dropped that key were never sent it again, so Element (Element X, Element Web) couldn't decrypt anything we sent there; restoring from key backup failed the same way (Vommet issue 519) | overlay (`fix/shared-history-diagnostics`) |
| The MSC4268 "may be shared with people invited later" flag on our message keys now goes out as `shared_history`, `m.shared_history` and `org.matrix.msc3061.shared_history` (new keys, re-shares to added devices, key backup; SDK `vommet-v6.1.1-ss.13`). Remove the extra names once a matrix-rust-sdk release with PR 7190 has been out for a while | Released matrix-rust-sdk (Element Web, Element X; up to matrix-sdk 0.19.1) reads only `m.shared_history` and the unstable name, so when an Element user invited someone, every message sent from Vommet was held back as not shared (Vommet issue 441) | overlay (`fix/shared-history-diagnostics`) |
## Media spoilers, MSC4193 (feat/media-spoilers)

| Change | Why | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Pictures and videos can be sent and received as spoilers (MSC4193, not in the spec yet). Sending: the attachment dialog has a "Mark as spoiler" switch (off by default, pictures and videos only, "Blurred for everyone until they tap it.") with an optional reason; the preview blurs to match; Vommet sends only the unstable `page.codeberg.everypizza.msc4193.spoiler` (+ `.spoiler.reason`) keys. Reading: those and the stable `m.spoiler` / `m.spoiler.reason`. A received spoiler (incl. pictures sent as `m.file`) shows its blurhash or a plain fill with "Spoiler · Tap to reveal" and the reason; nothing is downloaded, decrypted or played until tapped. Revealing is per message, for this viewer, in memory only; a "Hide" chip covers it again. Spoilers stay out of media mosaics; the gallery, the Media tab and photo albums keep them covered until tapped; notifications, reply previews and the room list say "Image (spoiler)" / "Video (spoiler)" with no thumbnail or file name. Edits keep the keys (`utils/media_spoiler.dart`, `ui/atoms/media_spoiler_cover.dart`) | Testers saw Sable cover a picture as a spoiler that Vommet showed in the clear (Cinny and mautrix-discord send the same keys); operator approved implementing the MSC (10-14). Upstream Commet has an open issue for it and no PR | testing (overlay `feat/media-spoilers`) |

## Linux notification markup

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Linux notifications escape message text, link titles, image alt text and the caller's name (`&`, `<`, `>`, and quotes in attributes) before they reach the notification daemon, and drop characters XML can't hold: on daemons that read the body as markup (dunst, KDE, xfce, mako), a message or name containing `<b>` or `<a href=...>` was rendered as formatting or a link. The daemon's "body-markup" capability is read once at startup; daemons without it get plain text and no formatting, and if the capabilities can't be read the body is escaped (`linux_notifier.dart`, `linux_notification_markup.dart`, `linux_notification_formatting.dart`) | testing (`fix/linux-notification-markup`) |

JPEG stays JPEG, other formats become PNG, and EXIF (location) is dropped. GIFs are left alone. Tapping the thumbnail no longer removes it | pending main (`feat/crop-attachment`) |

| Change | Status |
|---|---|

A logout or shutdown still quits, and if the tray goes away while the window is hidden the window comes back (`utils/tray/linux_tray.dart`, `utils/tray/app_tray.dart`, `window_close_handler.dart`, `window_management.dart`, `window_settings.dart`). ## SVG avatars

| Change | Issue | Status |
|---|---|---|
| SVG avatars, room and space icons, banners and emotes show instead of nothing. Servers can't thumbnail SVG (Synapse answers 400), so when a thumbnail is refused the original is fetched if it is an SVG of at most 1 MiB (the download stops after 4 KiB if it isn't one), and SVGs are drawn to a PNG on the device with flutter_svg. Before drawing, the SVG is checked: under 20,000 elements once `<use>`/`url(#id)` references are expanded, no reference loops, no DTD entities, at most 2048 px a side; anything else shows the placeholder. flutter_svg never fetches anything (`<image>` only from `data:` URIs) (`utils/image/svg_image.dart`, `matrix_svg_download.dart`, `matrix_mxc_image_provider.dart`, unit test `svg_image_test.dart`) | Vommet issue 309 | branch (`fix/309-svg-avatars`, after `fix/banner-thumbnail-scale`) |

## iOS and macOS builds

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| iOS: Podfile no longer declares a `RunnerTests` target, which the stock Runner project doesn't have, so `pod install` works (issue 43) | topic (`fix/ios-macos-build`) |
| iOS deployment target 11.0 → 15.0 (Runner project, Podfile, and every pod in `post_install`): Xcode 27 builds nothing older (issue 461) | topic (`fix/ios-macos-build`) |
| macOS deployment target 10.15 → 12.0 (Runner project, Podfile, and every pod in `post_install`): Xcode 27 builds nothing older (issue 461) | topic (`fix/ios-macos-build`) |
| macOS `Podfile.lock` updated: sqlite3 3.51.1 → 3.52.0 (sqlite3_flutter_libs now requires ~> 3.52.0, so `pod install` failed), WebRTC-SDK 137.7151.04 → 150.7871.01 (flutter_webrtc's constraint) (issue 43) | topic (`fix/ios-macos-build`) |
| macOS: `rust_lib_commet.podspec` links libc++ and Accelerate, which whisper.cpp (voice transcription, issue 70) needs; the app failed to link without them (issue 462) | topic (`fix/ios-macos-build`) |
| vodozemac is initialised through `flutter_vodozemac`, which loads `flutter_vodozemac.framework` on iOS and macOS; the plain `vodozemac` init looked for `vodozemac_bindings_dart`, so on Apple platforms E2EE was off and OIDC login failed (issue 459) | topic (`fix/ios-macos-build`) |
| iOS and macOS use the system emoji font (Apple Color Emoji) instead of the bundled Twemoji COLR font, whose glyphs Apple's text stack draws blank, so emoji in messages, reactions and the verification screen show up again (issue 463) | topic (`fix/ios-macos-build`) |
| iOS `Info.plist` explains why Vommet uses the camera, the microphone and the photo library (`NS…UsageDescription`); without them iOS killed the app as soon as a call, a voice message or a photo picker asked for access (issue 43) | topic (`fix/ios-macos-build`) |
| macOS: microphone and camera usage descriptions in `Info.plist` and the sandbox entitlements `device.audio-input` and `device.camera`; without them macOS killed the app when it joined a call (issue 43) | topic (`fix/ios-macos-build`) |
| iOS and macOS: name Vommet (iOS display name and bundle name, macOS `Vommet.app`) and app id `im.nether.chat`, like Android, Linux and Windows (also the macOS display name and the Runner scheme; was `chat.commet.commetapp`, `.macos` on macOS), so the fork installs beside Commet there too (issue 43) | topic (`fix/ios-macos-build`) |

## Flatpak without NetworkManager access

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| The Flatpak no longer asks for NetworkManager on the system bus (`--system-talk-name=org.freedesktop.NetworkManager` dropped from `im.nether.chat.yaml`). On Linux `connectivity_plus`'s backend is replaced at startup (`lib/utils/linux_connectivity.dart`): the Flatpak asks the desktop portal's NetworkMonitor (`GetAvailable`, `changed`), other Linux builds ask NetworkManager and then the portal, and when neither answers within 3 s the network counts as up. Without this, the check never completed once the bus was gone, so LiveKit (which awaits it before joining a call) stalled. The widget runner skips `network_info_plus`'s NetworkManager lookup in the Flatpak (else time-limited) and uses the interface list. Vommet issue 340 | branch (`fix/340-flatpak-network-portal-rebased`) |

## Sticker pack sheet

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Tapping or clicking a sticker in the timeline opens its pack (a bottom sheet on mobile, a dialog on desktop): every sticker in it, the tapped one outlined, and "Add pack…", which copies the pack into a new or existing pack, room, space or sticker room (the pack-import destinations; images are downloaded and uploaded again). Matrix stickers don't name their pack, so the pack is the one whose image URL matches among the packs you can read (the room's, its spaces', favourites, sticker rooms, personal packs). Stickers Vommet sends from a room or space pack carry `im.vommet.sticker_pack` (`room_id`, `state_key`), which other clients ignore and Vommet prefers when you're in that room. When no pack is found, the sheet says the rest of the pack isn't available and offers "Add sticker to…" for that one sticker. With media previews off, the first tap still reveals the sticker; animated stickers keep the hover star and also get Favourite in the sheet (`sticker_pack_sheet.dart`, `sticker_source_pack.dart`, `timeline_event_view_sticker.dart`, `timeline_event_view_message.dart`, `timeline_event_sticker.dart`, `matrix_timeline_event_sticker.dart`, `matrix_room_emoticon_component.dart`; unit test `sticker_source_pack_test.dart`). ## Docked widgets (experiment, Linux)

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Experiment "Docked widgets" (Layout, Linux only): a widget opens inside Vommet's window instead of the separate widget window, and can be popped out into its own window ("Vommet \| <widget>") and docked back without the page reloading (the same WebKit view moves between windows). The GTK runner puts the main view in a GtkOverlay; `linux/widget_dock.cc` holds the WebKitWebView over the rectangle the Flutter side keeps free and talks to Dart on the `vommet/widget_dock` channel (same page messages, camera/microphone prompt, autoplay and user agent as the widget window). While a dialog, menu or another page covers it, the view is swapped for a still picture. It shows in the room it was opened in: a resizable panel beside the room, or a tile above the call while you're in a voice room's call; popped out, that spot says it's open in its own window with Dock back / Show window. A widget's menu names both places: "Open in the room" / "Open in its own window". Windows/macOS need their own backend | topic (`feat/widget-dock`, after `feat/linux-widgets-webkit`; also needs `feat/experiments-opt-out`) |
| Docked widgets follow-up: a video's full screen button makes the widget really full screen (docked, the view covers the whole main window, which goes full screen; popped out, its own window goes full screen; Esc, the page's button or the window manager leaving full screen put it back, and the panel shows a "Full screen" placeholder meanwhile; channel events `fullscreenEntered` / `fullscreenLeft`). A popped out widget no longer shows black with GPU rendering: WebKitGTK 3 draws DMA-BUF frames from GL textures shared only with the first window's GL context, so on Wayland the dock's web views use shared memory frames (`WEBKIT_DMABUF_RENDERER_FORCE_SHM`, set only until the dock's first web process starts; set it to 0 to opt out; X11 maps frames to memory already and is left alone). Measured on an Intel iGPU, 1280x720 view repainting every frame: about +3% of one core in total | topic (`feat/widget-dock`) |

## Docked widgets on Windows (experiment)

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Experiment "Docked widgets" also on Windows: a widget opens inside Vommet's window (beside the room, or as a tile above a voice room's call) and pops out into its own window ("Vommet \| <widget>") and back without reloading. `windows/runner/widget_dock.cpp` takes the same `vommet/widget_dock` calls as the Linux side: a WebView2 view sits in a child window above the Flutter view at the rectangle Dart keeps free, and `put_ParentWindow` moves the same view into its own top-level window and back (closing that window docks it back). Same page messages, user agent, microphone/camera Allow/Block prompt (everything else denied), media allowed to start without a click, new-window links in the default browser, and a still picture while a dialog or menu covers it. A video's full screen button makes the widget full screen as on Linux (WebView2 only reports it, so the backend makes the main window, or the popped out one, full screen; docked, the view covers the whole main window above the other docked views; Esc or the page leaving full screen restore the window; popping out, docking back or closing first leave full screen; `fullscreenEntered` / `fullscreenLeft`). Each widget gets a private (InPrivate) profile in its own WebView2 data folder (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Vommet\WidgetDock`). The WebView2 SDK (NuGet 1.0.3967.48, hash-pinned, static loader) is downloaded at build time. The Linux backend's Dart class is now shared by both (`NativeWidgetDockBackend`); macOS has a placeholder until its own backend lands. Without the experiment Windows keeps the separate widget window | topic (`feat/widget-dock-windows`, after `feat/widget-dock`) |

## Room switching leak (Vommet issue 345)

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Leaving a room releases its view: the timeline view now cancels its "jump to message" listener and the desktop room header menu its settings listener. Before, every room opened stayed alive for the whole session (its chat, timeline view with a key per message, header menu, and their subscriptions), and each jump to a message ran in all of them, so switching rooms got slower the longer the app stayed open. Same bug upstream (Commet issue 970). Regression check: `integration_test/room_switch_runner.dart` | pending main (`fix/345-room-switch-slowdown`) |

## Unread badge on the Linux tray icon

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| The Linux tray icon shows the unread count as a red badge in its lower right corner, 1 to 9 then "9+" (Vommet issue 536), with the count in the tooltip too. It counts the same messages as the taskbar badge (`NotificationUtils.getNotificationCounts().$2`) and updates on the same events. The badge is drawn into the icon pixmaps with `dart:ui` and the whole icon is swapped (`NewIcon`/`NewToolTip`), not sent as an overlay icon, because Waybar (Hyprland, Sway) never draws overlays. Settings › Window Behaviour gets "Unread badge on tray icon" (on), shown while "Show tray icon" is on (`utils/tray/tray_badge.dart`, `utils/tray/app_tray.dart`, `utils/tray/linux_tray.dart`, `window_settings.dart`, `preferences.dart`) | topic (`feat/536-tray-unread-badge`, after `feat/linux-tray`) |

## Undecryptable messages retried when keys can arrive

| Change | Issue | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Messages that failed to decrypt in an open room are asked for again, without "Retry Decrypt": once this device is verified (from the user's other devices and the key backup; before, the SDK never asked while the device was unverified and never asked again after), and when the key backup's key arrives (from the backup). Each session once per moment, at most 50 per room; keys that arrive re-decrypt the message in place. `MatrixUtdRetryComponent`; integration variant "report: verify, no retry" in `utd_vanish_test.dart` | #32, #100 | testing (`fix/32-utd-auto-retry`) |
| Rooms that weren't open when the device was verified or the backup key arrived are asked for when they're opened: their undecryptable messages' keys are asked from the user's other devices (once verified) and the backup (once its key is here), each session once per app run; before, opening such a room only asked the backup. A session asked from the devices before the backup key came is still asked from the backup later | #32 | testing (`fix/32-utd-auto-retry`) |

## Spellcheck in the message box

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Spellcheck in the message box on Linux and Windows, Element-style: Settings › General › Spellcheck downloads Hunspell dictionaries per language (LibreOffice's, pinned, size-checked, about 70 languages) and every ticked language is checked at once. Misspelled words get a wavy underline (not the word still being typed, code, links, mentions, shortcodes, acronyms or camelCase); right-click one for up to five suggestions, "Add to dictionary" (a personal dictionary, editable in settings) or "Ignore in this message". Before any dictionary is downloaded, the right-click menu offers the device's language in one click. On by default once a dictionary exists; phones keep their keyboard's own spellcheck. Checking runs on the device in the Rust library (spellbook, a pure-Rust Hunspell, called over plain FFI; `spellcheck.rs`, `lib/utils/spellcheck/`) | topic (`feat/spellcheck`, overlay) |

## Message header layout

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| The sender name in a message header stays on one line (cut off with "…") instead of wrapping, so the message no longer grows when hovering switches to the detailed timestamp (Vommet issue 446); in a pane too narrow for name and timestamp side by side (e.g. the pinned messages panel), the timestamp goes under the name instead of squeezing the name to one letter per line | topic (`fix/sender-name-wrap`, overlay) |
## Noise suppression at any sample rate, and its telemetry

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Noise suppression also runs when libwebrtc processes the microphone at another rate than 48 kHz: the Rust filter (`rust/voice`, new `resample.rs`) resamples each 10 ms block to 48 kHz for RNNoise/DeepFilterNet3 and back (polyphase windowed sinc, about 1 ms delay each way). Before, those blocks passed through untouched, so on Windows with a 16 kHz headset or Bluetooth microphone (Windows processes at the device's rate) every mode sounded the same. New counter `frames_resampled` in the stats struct | topic (`feat/telemetry-voice-filter`, overlay) |
| Telemetry schema v26: each `call_stats` minute adds the noise suppression's state (experiment on, mode, WebRTC's own suppressor on, microphone volume, processor installed, engine in use and automatic mode's choice, watchdog fallback) and what it did that minute (blocks cleaned, skipped and resampled, the processing rate, DeepFilterNet3's average and benchmark time per block). Counts, the rate and fixed words only | topic (`feat/telemetry-voice-filter`, overlay) |
## Windows screen-share audio in stereo

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Windows screen-share audio reaches the call in stereo. The flutter-webrtc fork's WASAPI loopback capturer averaged the mix format's channels into one and fed the audio source mono frames, so the stereo Opus the livekit fork negotiates for the track carried mono. It now keeps the left/right channels of a multichannel mix (a mono mix stays mono), as the Linux capturer already does. Pin bump to fork branch `windows-stereo` (`windows/application_loopback_capturer.cc`); no Dart changes | topic (`fix/screenshare-audio-windows-stereo`, based on testing for the fork pin) |

## 12-hour or 24-hour clock

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Settings › Appearance › Clock: "Time format" is System default, 12-hour or 24-hour, each shown with a sample time. Message times, the long time on hover, date dividers, thread and chat list times, someone's local time on their profile, the timezone picker and the developer log all follow it. Before, only Android followed the system's 24-hour setting; desktop always showed the language's clock (12-hour for English), and the hover time used the language setting. System default is what the engine reports: the OS setting on Android, iOS and macOS, the user's time format on Windows, GNOME's clock format on Linux (24-hour when the desktop doesn't say); on the web, the app language. `ClockFormatScope` puts the result into `MediaQuery.alwaysUse24HourFormat` above the app, so the MSC3160 timestamp tooltip, calendar event times and Flutter's time pickers follow it too; formatting goes through `utils/clock_format.dart` (unit test `clock_format_test.dart`). ## Confirming a new device right after signing in

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Approving a freshly signed-in device works on big accounts: the SDK (ss.15) loads our own device list without first loading the member list of every encrypted room (after one fresh sign-in with sliding sync to an account with 117 encrypted rooms the list still didn't exist two minutes later, so "Approve from another device" failed and an approval started in Element was cancelled on our side). "Approve from another device" fetches the list itself if needed, and says so when no other device can approve. When another device (e.g. Element) confirms this one, the sign-in setup and Settings › Security notice it within seconds and ask that device for the cross-signing and backup keys (after a fresh sign-in they never did: the status read "unknown" until a restart). Settings › Security › "Confirm this device" now opens the recovery key and approval steps (both buttons closed again at once). Integration tests: `cross_signing_test.dart`, a fast tier in the pre-release gate (approve both ways, recovery key, missing own device list with sliding sync) and a nightly tier (sliding sync, 120-room account, passphrase, start over, Settings › Security, and interop with matrix-js-sdk's Rust crypto, the crypto of Element Web/Desktop and Element X: approvals both ways and MSC4268 shared history both ways) | testing |

| Web: spellcheck's dart:ffi side (`spellcheck_native.dart`) is swapped for a stub on web via a conditional import (`spellcheck_native_web.dart`); spellcheck stays Linux/Windows only. The web build didn't compile since spellcheck landed | `utils/spellcheck/` | overlay (`feat/web-build`) |
| Web releases (Vommet issue 415): the candidate build (`ci/windows-testing`) checks the image but pushes none; when a release is published, `ci/windows-web-release` makes the same build's artifact into `ghcr.io/dark-collective/vommet-web:<release tag>` + `:testing` (`:latest` on a stable release; OCI version/revision/source labels) and deploys it to Cloudflare Pages project `vommet-web` (branch `testing`, skipped while `CLOUDFLARE_PAGES_TOKEN` is unset), then checks what it published (`.vommet/web/check-site.sh`: application/wasm and byte-identical wasm, COOP/COEP, SPA fallback, homeserver). nginx and Pages (`pages_headers`) send `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` + `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: credentialless` for the multi-threaded wasm renderer (`VOMMET_CROSS_ORIGIN_ISOLATION=off` drops them in the image), `.mjs` as JavaScript, and `Cache-Control: no-cache` on everything (no file name is content-hashed) | `.github/workflows/vommet-web.yml`, `.vommet/web/` | overlay (`feat/web-build`) |
| Web build toolchain: the web compile (`pub get`, fallback fonts, `flutter build web --wasm --no-web-resources-cdn`) runs on Flutter **3.47.7** (Dart 3.13.5, `FLUTTER_WEB_VERSION` in `vommet-web.yml`); code generation stays on the main `FLUTTER_VERSION` 3.41.9 (build_runner hangs on 3.47.7). Reason: dart2wasm before Dart 3.12 crashes on this app with a Stack Overflow in its dummy-value generation (dart-lang/sdk 62319). Both the wasm and the JS fallback come from that one SDK. Drop it when the main toolchain reaches Dart 3.12. CanvasKit/skwasm are served from our origin (`--no-web-resources-cdn`) | `.github/workflows/vommet-web.yml` | overlay (`feat/web-build`) |
| Web (WebAssembly build only): the login screen shows the star animation's plain background instead of running `constellation.frag`. Skwasm (Flutter 3.47.7) intermittently fails to compile that shader ("unknown identifier 't'") and then traps with "null function", which crashed the page right after the login screen appeared. The JS fallback and native builds keep the animation (`star_trails.dart`, `kIsWasm`) | `ui/atoms/shader/star_trails.dart` | testing (`feat/web-build`) |
| Web (WebAssembly build): sign-in works. flutter_rust_bridge comes from [nether/vommet-flutter-rust-bridge](https://nether.codes/nether/vommet-flutter-rust-bridge) (tag `vommet-2.11.1-wasm.1` = 2.11.1 + `wasmWireToDart`): the generated web bindings hand back raw JS values, which dart2js treats as Dart lists and ints but dart2wasm doesn't, so vodozemac's first call failed "Runtime type check failed" and the client never initialised. No-op on native and in the JS build. Also needs SDK fork `vommet-v6.1.1-ss.17` (IndexedDB numbers read back as `int`; no `await` on both sides of `&&`, which dart2wasm miscompiles), pinned by the SDK pin carrier | `pubspec.yaml` (dependency_overrides) | testing (`feat/web-build`) |
| Web (WebAssembly build): attaching an image works. `archive` comes from [nether/vommet-archive](https://nether.codes/nether/vommet-archive) (tag `vommet-3.6.1-wasm.1` = 3.6.1 with its web code chosen by `dart.library.js_interop` instead of `dart.library.js`): under dart2wasm 3.6.1 fell through to a stub that throws "Cannot create a zlib decoder", `package:image` 4.3.0 turned that into a null image, and the attachment processor failed on every PNG. No-op on native and in the JS build; drop when `package:image` moves to 4.4+ (archive 4.x) | `pubspec.yaml` (dependency_overrides) | testing (`feat/web-build`) |
| Web release stage no longer fails on "Fetch and verify the build": the build job writes `build.env` shell-quoted (`printf %q`; the label has spaces and parentheses) and checks that it sources back to the same label and sha; the release stage sources it, or reads an older unquoted one line by line | `.github/workflows/vommet-web.yml` | testing (`feat/web-build`) |
| web.vommet.app follows testing releases: the web release stage deploys each testing release to the Pages production branch (`PAGES_BRANCH: production`), which serves web.vommet.app, instead of the unlisted testing branch. | `.github/workflows/vommet-web.yml` | testing (`feat/web-build`) |
| Web (WebAssembly build, Firefox and other non-Chromium browsers): space avatars on the rail and a space's home show their pictures instead of black squares. There skwasm (Flutter 3.47.7) decodes through an `<img>` element and passes the requested decode size to `createImageBitmap` as a crop rectangle, upscaling included, so a 90 px thumbnail decoded for 128 px came out as a 90x128 cut-out (room avatars, decoded smaller, lost their bottom third). Images are now decoded at their own size there and scaled down by the app (`decodeAtTargetSize`, never upscaling); the image bytes also get a buffer of their own on the web, since that path builds its Blob from the whole underlying buffer. No change on native, in the JS build or in Chromium | `utils/image/sized_decode.dart`, `utils/image/engine_crops_target_size*.dart`, `utils/image/lod_image.dart` | testing (`feat/web-build`) |
| Web (Firefox): the space colour scheme taken from a space's avatar no longer fails with "IndexSizeError" (logged as an error for every space at startup). Outside Chromium a decoded image is backed by an `<img>` element and reading its pixels back fails, so on the web the seed-colour step always redraws the image first, as it already did for images over 112 px | `utils/image/image_seed_color.dart` | testing (`feat/web-build`) |

## Web first load (perf/web-first-load)

| Change | Where | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Web: the first load no longer downloads tiamat's 24 MB `NotoColorEmoji.ttf`. Flutter web fetches every `FontManifest.json` font before the first frame; after `flutter build web`, `.vommet/web/trim-fonts.py` drops package font families the app shadows with its own of the same name (tiamat's `EmojiFont` and `RobotoCustom`, never used: tiamat names them without `package:`, so the app's win) (Roboto: three fetches → two). Emoji still draw with the app's Twemoji `EmojiFont`; anything it lacks comes from the engine's Noto fallback in small pieces, on demand. WebAssembly first load (login page, empty cache, uncompressed) 46.0 → 21.9 MB, 43 → 36–40 requests; the JS build loads 24.8 MB. Desktop and Android bundles unchanged. The smoke test starts from an empty cache, fails over a first-load budget (wasm 24 MB, JS 27 MB), on the engine's missing-glyph warning, or when typed text no bundled font has fetches no fallback font | `.vommet/web/trim-fonts.py`, `.vommet/web/smoke.mjs`, `.github/workflows/vommet-web.yml` | overlay (`perf/web-first-load`) |

## Web: encryption survives reloads (fix/web-reload-e2ee)

| Change | Why | Status |
|---|---|---|
| End-to-end test of the web app in real browsers: `.github/workflows/vommet-web-e2e.yml` builds the app and runs `.vommet/web/e2e/reload-e2ee.mjs` (Playwright) in Chromium and Firefox against a throwaway Synapse started in the job. A second device of the same user (matrix-js-sdk, Node) sets up cross-signing, a recovery key and key backup; the web app signs in and unlocks with the recovery key, or is approved from the other device by emoji; then two page reloads and a browser restart, each checking the device keeps its keys and stays verified, no "Is this you?" again, old and new messages decrypt, messages sent from the web decrypt on the other device, and Settings › Security loads. GitHub copy only, no secrets, never contacts our hosts | Vommet issues 318 and 353: after a reload the web app lost the ability to decrypt older messages and Security settings misbehaved; nothing tested the web app in a browser | overlay (`fix/web-reload-e2ee`) |
| Web: opening the database no longer waits for `navigator.storage.persist()` | Firefox shows a permission prompt for it, and until the user answered, sign-in spun forever | overlay (`fix/web-reload-e2ee`) |
| Web e2e runs each browser twice, once on the WebAssembly build and once on the JS build, and fails when the page loaded the other one. Firefox only gets WebAssembly in the test, through `wasmAllowList` (Flutter's loader keeps it on JS by default) | Before, "Chromium" meant WebAssembly and "Firefox" meant JS, so a broken WebAssembly sign-in in Firefox or a broken JS build in Chromium went unseen | overlay (`fix/web-reload-e2ee`) |
| Feature matrix of the web app in real browsers: `.vommet/web/e2e/features.mjs` (flow `features` of vommet-web-e2e, Chromium and Firefox, each on the WebAssembly and the JS build) signs in, unlocks with the recovery key, then checks the room list, encrypted history, send/receive, reply, reactions, edit, delete, threads, encrypted upload, others' images/files/stickers, room emoji packs, sending a sticker, notifications, every Settings page and a reload, records console errors per feature and fails on any request to a Google host; writes `matrix.md`/`matrix.json` per browser | Vommet issue 426: what works on the web compared with the desktop app, kept checked in CI | overlay (`fix/web-reload-e2ee`) |
| Avatar check of the web app in real browsers: `.vommet/web/e2e/avatars.mjs` (flow `avatars` of vommet-web-e2e, Chromium and Firefox, WebAssembly and JS) seeds spaces, subspaces and rooms with two-tone PNG and JPEG avatars (48 px to 3000 px, square, wide and tall), signs in and counts each avatar's two colours on the space rail, a space's home and the room list, after sign-in and after two reloads; a black, cropped or still-blank avatar fails the job | `.vommet/web/e2e/avatars.mjs`, `.github/workflows/vommet-web-e2e.yml` | overlay (`fix/web-reload-e2ee`) |
## Replacing the recovery key

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| "Replace my recovery key" really retires the old key: the SDK (`vommet-v6.1.1-ss.20` = ss.19 + 1 commit) now uploads each secret under the new key only (it kept the old-key copies, so the old key still opened the cross-signing and backup keys, Vommet issue 526), and the replace waits until this device has synced the change. Integration tests: the nightly secure-setup suite checks the server copy after a replace, and its own-password test runs every night instead of skipping on slow runners (native code built optimised for that suite, Vommet issue 527) | topic |
## Notifications right after signing in

| Change | Status |
|---|---|

## Room keys for bridge bots

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Messages sent from Vommet reach bridges in encrypted bridged rooms again (Vommet issue 334): before keeping a room key from a device that looks unsigned by its owner's cross-signing, the SDK (`vommet-v6.1.1-ss.21` = ss.20 + 1 commit) re-fetches that user's keys, at most every 10 minutes per user. Our copy can predate the device signing itself (mautrix bridge bots with `self_sign`), and when the server never announces the change (Tuwunel before 1.6.1) the bridge got no keys until the next sign-in. Who gets keys is unchanged | topic |

## Shared history keeps its mark on earlier key copies

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Invite bundles no longer hold back sessions whose sender marked them shareable (MSC4268, Vommet issue 436): when this device got a key from the sender's later messages (flagged) and then a copy from an earlier message (a key forwarded by another of our devices, whose flag we drop, or a key backup copy without it), the SDK kept the earlier copy and lost the mark, so the session was listed as "not shared". The mark now belongs to the session (SDK `vommet-v6.1.1-ss.22` = ss.21 + 1 commit), whichever copy arrives first. Older sessions without a mark stay withheld (Vommet issues 439/440). Integration test in the fast tier of `cross_signing_test.dart` | topic |

## Approving a device on a slow machine

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| "Approve from another device" no longer fails on a slow device mid first sync (the 2026-10-20 report from a Pinebook Pro). The SDK refreshed a device list by clearing it and refilling it across database awaits, so for a while our own devices were missing and starting the verification threw. It now checks the database first and builds the new list from the live one with no await before the swap, so a block or verification made meanwhile is kept, and starting olm sessions checks the claimed one-time keys against the devices it was asked for (keys for devices it didn't ask for are ignored). SDK `vommet-v6.1.1-ss.24` = ss.23 + 1 commit, tests in `test/vommet/device_list_race_test.dart`. The sign-in setup also waits for the first sync without the 30 s limit ("Continue without checking" still skips it): on a slow device it gave up and closed without asking anything. Integration test in the fast tier of `cross_signing_test.dart` | topic |

| Diagnostics (when switched on) send an `ssss_repair` event when entering the current recovery key cleaned up (or tried to clean up) secret copies an old, replaced recovery key still opened, and once per session at start-up while such copies wait for the key: what brought the key (`unlock`, `check`, `startup`), the outcome from a fixed list, and counts (copies waiting, secrets cleaned, copies removed, kept, failed, old keys seen). Never key ids, secrets or which secrets | To see how many accounts still carry old-key copies (Vommet issue 526) and that the cleanup only ever removes what it could prove | overlay (`feat/telemetry-ssss-repair`) |

## Old recovery key copies cleaned up

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| One-time cleanup after Vommet issue 526: before SDK ss.20, "Replace my recovery key" left every secret (cross-signing keys, backup key) readable with the OLD key too. When the user next enters their current recovery key (unlocking secure messaging, or checking the key), Vommet removes the copies under every other key from the account data. A copy is only removed after the current key's copy, read fresh from the server, decrypts (MAC checked) to the live secret: the published master key for the master key; the SDK's check against the published key / current backup plus this device's cached copy for the others. Anything unprovable, and other apps' secrets, stays; key descriptions stay; it stops if another device changes the key meanwhile; nothing is sent when there's nothing to clean. Every non-default key counts as retired (Element Web and matrix-rust-sdk only ever use the default key). No UI; the app never keeps the recovery key, so there is no silent startup cleanup. Telemetry event `ssss_repair` (counts and outcome only). SDK `vommet-v6.1.1-ss.25` = ss.24 + 1 commit, tests in `test/vommet/ssss_retired_keys_test.dart`; integration test in `secure_setup_test.dart` (slow tier) | overlay (`fix/ssss-repair-old-key-copies`) |

## Recovery key check-in brought forward for the old-key cleanup

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| Follow-up to Vommet issue 526: while old-key copies of the secrets wait for the user's current recovery key (counted locally, cleanup not done yet) and this device is confirmed with secret storage, the existing "Still have your recovery key?" check-in is due at the next start instead of in up to 30 days, also on accounts that had no check-ins (e.g. devices approved from another one). Once per pending cleanup: its own buttons still decide what follows ("Remind me later" or closing it = the usual 3-day snooze; passing = the usual 30 days, or no check-ins again on an account that had none). Once the copies are gone the earlier schedule comes back. Never while a setup page is open, and only after the first sync with the device confirmed. While copies wait, the check-in accepts only the CURRENT key: the old one gets the existing "That's not it" message instead of "That's the one. Keep it safe." (telemetry `ssss_repair` outcome `not_default_key`, trigger `check`). No new screen or wording. Unit tests `secure_setup_repair_checkin_test.dart`; integration test in `secure_setup_test.dart` (slow tier) | overlay (`fix/ssss-repair-checkin-early`) |

## Recovery key check-in confirmation inside the dialog

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| When the "Still have your recovery key?" check-in passes, the same dialog switches to a success state (green check, "That's the one. Keep it safe.", a Done button) and closes by itself after about 1.5 s, or at once on Done, back or a tap outside; all of these count as passed, recorded once. It used to show that text in a snack bar after closing the dialog (Vommet issue 129 check-in), but the main page has no Scaffold: in debug builds it tripped an assertion, in release builds it didn't show (or showed later on another page). No animation, no new wording. Unit tests `secure_setup_checkin_ok_test.dart`; the slow-tier integration test passes the check-in on the main page itself | overlay (`fix/ssss-repair-checkin-early`) |

## Recovery key check-ins further apart as they pass

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| "Still have your recovery key?" check-ins: still 3 days after setup, then each check-in passed in a row moves the next one further out, 30 → 90 → 180 days, then every 180 days (was every 30 days). A per-account streak is stored next to the other check-in records (`vommet_secure_checkin_streak_<user>`); installs from before have none, which counts as 0, so the next gap is 30. A wrong key at the check-in (including an old, replaced key while old-key copies wait), "I've lost it, make a new one", or any setup (new key, replaced key, unlocking with the key on this device, or approving it from another device) resets it, so the next pass gives 30 days. A check that fails for another reason (e.g. offline) doesn't. "Remind me later" keeps the 3-day snooze and the streak. A check-in brought forward only for the old-key cleanup (Vommet issue 526) doesn't add to the streak (it came early, so it says nothing about keeping the key over a longer gap); accounts without check-ins still get none. Unit tests `secure_setup_checkin_streak_test.dart` | overlay (`fix/ssss-repair-checkin-early`) |

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| "Unlocking your messages" restores the key backup much faster: the SDK (`vommet-v6.1.1-ss.26` = ss.25 + 2 commits) now stores backup keys 250 per database transaction instead of several writes per key, re-decrypts a room's last message once per batch (one UI update for all rooms) instead of once per key, and gives the UI a turn between batches. What gets kept and the per-session `onSessionKeyReceived` announcements are unchanged. `loadAllKeys`/`loadAllKeysFromRoom`/`loadFromResponse` take an optional `onProgress(done, total)`. SDK benchmark (`test/vommet/backup_bulk_import_test.dart`, 5,000 sessions, sqlite file): 86.3 s → 7.3 s. ## Less database work after each sync (perf/sdk-db-load)

| Change | Why | Status |
|---|---|---|
| SDK vommet-v6.1.1-ss.27 (= ss.26 + 1 commit, SDK branch perf/db-load): the "already seen" device-id and key checks of a device-list refresh run against an in-memory copy of those tables, read in bulk instead of three sequential reads per device, and their new entries are written in the refresh's transaction instead of one commit each; devices that didn't change aren't rewritten. Presence is written only when it changed (newest per user per sync), users without stored presence aren't read again; a member event marks the profile outdated once per user per sync and not again when sliding sync re-sends it; the SSSS cache lookups are kept in memory. The checks refuse exactly what they did before; a failed refresh still stores its "already seen" entries and is redone in full | Telemetry from a Pinebook Pro after a fresh sign-in: about 3,300 device checks, each 1-2 database round trips queued behind the sync, plus per-event presence and profile writes, kept the database busy for minutes. SDK benchmark: 1,500 new devices 4,503 commits to 0; re-query after the lists were dropped 10,830 to 1,820 calls; 500 unchanged presences 500 writes to 0; 1,000 member events 1,000 profile marks to 50; SSSS lookups 150 to 3 | overlay (`perf/sdk-db-load`) |

## Recovery key check-ins shared across devices (feat/recovery-checkins-shared)

| Change | Why | Status |
|---|---|---|
| The "Still have your recovery key?" schedule (last pass, passes in a row, next check, "Remind me later"s in a row, on/off, how the key was set up) is shared by the user's Vommet devices in the account data event `im.nether.vommet.recovery_checkins`, encrypted on the device: AES-256-CTR + HMAC-SHA256 (the SDK's secret storage helpers) with a key derived by HKDF-SHA256 from the message backup's private key under its own info string `im.nether.vommet.recovery_checkins.v1`, so the server sees an opaque blob. The local preferences stay as a cache (and keep the old separate values for an older Vommet); an install's old values are migrated and merged. Copies merge by event times (newest pass with its streak and next check; a failure or new key after it resets; snoozes after it carry; newest on/off and setup method win), unit-tested in `unit_test/recovery_checkins_test.dart`. Writes fetch and merge the server's copy first and happen only when something changed. A device without the backup key, or with an old one, uses its local copy and never overwrites the shared one; after a backup key change the record is rewritten under the new key. Approving a new device adopts the schedule (not a pass); entering the key at setup or unlock is a pass. Other Matrix apps ignore the event | Passing the check-in on one device asked again on every other one, and turning check-ins off has to apply everywhere | overlay (`feat/recovery-checkins-shared`) |
| Settings › Security › Encryption & recovery has a "Recovery key check-ins" switch under the Recovery key row: on shows "Next check: around <month>" and a "How often?" explainer; off shows a "Not recommended" note. Turning it off asks first ("They're rare", Keep check-ins on, a 2 s "Hold to turn off"); the switch doesn't move until then, and turning it on again asks nothing. Off also drops the check-in brought forward for the old-key cleanup (Vommet issue 526). In settings search | Operator request 10-21 (mockups approved) | overlay (`feat/recovery-checkins-shared`) |
| The check-in is worded for how the key was set up: recovery key (password manager), phrase (6 words), own password, or neutral when unknown (set up in another app or before this change), each with its own field label and wrong-entry hint. Phrase and password offer "Have a recovery key or key file instead?" (switches to neutral); key and neutral offer "Open a file", which reads a recovery key from a text file such as Element's recovery-key.txt (a key export is told apart and refused). After 3 "Remind me later"s in a row (counted across devices) the next check-in has no "Remind me later", can't be dismissed, says so, and links to the switch ("Rather not be asked? Turn off check-ins in Settings") | Operator request 10-21: wording that matches what the user actually saved, a file option for people who kept the key as a file, and an end to putting it off forever | overlay (`feat/recovery-checkins-shared`) |

## Widgets in the web app (feat/web-widgets)

| Change | Why | Status |
|---|---|---|
| The web app opens room widgets in an `<iframe>` on its own page (a Flutter platform view in the usual widget overlay window), talking to the existing widget API host (capabilities, permission dialog, remembered choices) over `window.postMessage`. It takes only messages whose `source` is the frame's own window and whose `origin` is the widget URL's origin, and posts with that exact origin, never `*`. Binary data is passed as ArrayBuffers/Blobs both ways, like the other runners. Frame sandbox and `allow` as Element Web (camera, microphone, display capture, clipboard write, autoplay, fullscreen); `parentUrl` is the app's page. A widget on the app's own origin is refused. The tile menu's other place is "Open in a new tab"; catalog widgets marked direct open in a new tab too. The Widgets tab and the room menu's Widgets entry are no longer hidden on the web | Commet's web build had no working widget host (the embedded runner needs a native web view), so the tab said "Widgets aren't available in this room." | overlay (`feat/web-widgets`) |
| The app is cross-origin isolated (COEP credentialless, for the WebAssembly renderer's threads), which blocks frames of pages that don't send COEP themselves. Widgets are framed as `credentialless` iframes while the page is isolated: no COEP needed from the widget, but it gets no cookies and fresh storage each time. Firefox has no credentialless frames, so there only widgets that send COEP (+ CORP) load in the frame (checked in the browser test: one without them never loads), and the hint "Nothing showing? Some widgets only work in a tab of their own." shows next to "Open in a new tab" from the start; elsewhere it shows after 15 s without a widget API message | Dropping COEP would make the renderer single-threaded for everyone | overlay (`feat/web-widgets`) |
| Browser test `.vommet/web/e2e/widgets.mjs` (flow `widgets` in vommet-web-e2e.yml): a widget on another origin gets a capability through the dialog and reads the room topic through the app; a second frame on the widget's origin is ignored. Unit test `unit_test/widget_frame_origin_test.dart` | Regression tests | overlay (`feat/web-widgets`) |

| Change | Why | Status |
|---|---|---|
| SDK vommet-v6.1.1-ss.29.4 (= ss.29.3 + 1 commit, SDK branch fix/idb-abort-and-room-state-prefix-ss29.4; the same commit was first tagged ss.30 on ss.29 and ss.31 on ss.29.1, never shipped): an IndexedDB transaction the browser aborts (QuotaExceededError at commit) now fails with `IndexedDBTransactionAborted` instead of never finishing; a blocked database open logs a warning | A tester's private browser window (small in-memory storage, ~1800 rooms) stayed on the splash forever after a reload: the aborted transaction held the store's transaction lock, so every later write (Client.init's first `updateClient`) waited forever. Reproduced on CI with a zero storage quota | after `feat/telemetry-room-key-share` |
| SDK ss.29.4: `getUnimportantRoomEventStatesForRoom` reads one room's deferred states with a key-prefix range (`getAllValuesWithPrefix` on the IndexedDB and sqflite boxes; the prefix ends in the `|` separator, cached writes win like `get`) instead of filtering every room's keys per room | The deferred room loads at startup were quadratic in the room count: on the web, 1800 rooms × 30 states took 16–17 s to the first frame after a reload, 4.7–5.9 s with the prefix read. SDK test `test/vommet/web_startup_storage_test.dart` | |
| SDK ss.29.4: `Client.init` rethrows a storage refusal (an aborted IndexedDB transaction) without clearing the store | Clearing would sign the user out and drop their encryption keys because the browser was out of room for one write. Same SDK test (a refusal keeps the store, another error still clears it) | |
| A startup watchdog: if the accounts haven't loaded after 40 s, the splash says it is taking longer than usual; when the browser's storage quota is small (< 1.5 GB) or ≥ 90 % used, it says private windows have little storage and to use a normal window. It is cancelled when the app (or the fatal error page) is shown and never fires after that | The splash used to sit with no explanation; Vivaldi/Chromium private windows get a small store | `commet/lib/utils/startup_watchdog.dart`, unit test `startup_watchdog_test.dart` |
| An account that fails to load with QuotaExceededError gets a "Browser storage is full" alert explaining private windows, instead of the generic "Unable to load account" | Says what to do about it | `matrix_client.dart` |
| The "Is this you?" secure-messaging setup at sign-in, and the "Your messages aren't backed up" banner, skip an account that failed to load | With the store refusing writes, the account's crypto state can't be read, so the setup asked a verified device to verify again (seen in the zero-quota CI trial) instead of leaving the storage alert to explain | `secure_setup_gate.dart` |

## Room keys reach devices they missed (fix/room-key-retries)

| Change | Why | Status |
|---|---|---|
| SDK vommet-v6.1.1-ss.29.5 (= ss.29.4 + 1 commit, SDK branch fix/key-share-retries-and-requests): a device the room key couldn't be encrypted for (no olm session: no one-time key, or the claim failed) is sent the key again with a later message at that message's index (backoff per session and device: 30 s doubling to 30 min). Every device the key was meant for still counts as possibly holding it, so removing, blocking or re-keying one rotates the session exactly as before. Failures in the to-device chunks after the first 20 devices are now logged and counted instead of lost. Key-request handling is unchanged | 10-22: CK's new sign-in sent 4 messages nobody could read; besides the missing device lists (ss.29.2/29.3), a device whose one-time-key claim failed was silently skipped and never retried. An answer-key-requests-from-members variant was built and dropped after an adversarial review: a server-injected or post-takeover device could have obtained past keys. SDK test `test/vommet/room_key_retries_and_requests_test.dart` | after `fix/web-startup-storage` |

Your own device isn't affected | Tuwunel and conduwuit set a renamed session's `last_seen_ts` to now and `last_seen_ip` to the renaming device's address on `PUT /devices/{id}`; Synapse doesn't | overlay (`feat/security-settings-refresh`) |
## Telemetry v34: verification step timings (feat/telemetry-verification)

| Change | Why | Status |
|---|---|---|
| New opt-in diagnostics event `verification` (schema v34), one per device or person verification this device took part in, when it ends: role (requester/responder), kind (self/user), in a room or to-device, method (sas/qr/none), outcome (done/cancelled/error/abandoned after 15 min) with the cancel code from a fixed list and who cancelled; ms from the request for each step seen (ready, start, accept, key sent/received, emoji shown, confirmed here, mac received, done), the responder's dialog time and how long the person took to tap Accept, the request's age on arrival, whether it came in the app's first sync response (cold start) or before the first sync finished; and the sync loop's share: rounds and their apply time during it, and for the steps received, how long their response had been in before the SDK got to them and how long the loop was busy with the previous response before that request went out. `lib/telemetry/verification_telemetry.dart` (attached from `SyncStats.attach`; requests we start are registered right after `startVerification()` in the secure setup approval, session list and DM trust banner; a 100 ms timer plus a chained `onUpdate` watch each live request, no SDK change). Unit test `unit_test/verification_telemetry_test.dart` | A new desktop's "verify with another device" took ~65-70 s and the phone sat on a waiting screen before the emoji, with no per-step data to say whether people, the network or a busy sync was the cause | overlay (`feat/telemetry-verification`) |

## Key backup import no longer freezes big accounts (perf/history-import-slices)

| Change | Why | Status |
|---|---|---|
| SDK vommet-v6.1.1-ss.29.7: the history import after sign-in/approval (`KeyManager.loadFromResponse`) works in 30 ms slices (16–250 keys per database transaction) and lets the UI run between them and while it re-decrypts rooms' last messages; those go out in fake syncs of at most 50 rooms, at most once a second (plus one at the end), each followed by its sessions' announcements. Senders' devices for backup keys without an ed25519 key come from an index built for the import instead of a scan of every device per key. Backup-only single-key lookups (`request(onlineKeyBackupOnly: true)`, e.g. every undecryptable last message once the backup key arrives) run 4 at a time, wait for a running whole-backup import, and skip keys it settled. Which keys are kept, the sender keys recorded and who gets keys are unchanged. SDK tests `test/vommet/backup_import_slices_test.dart`, `backup_import_blocking_test.dart` | A tester's fresh sign-in on a big account (1,792 rooms) froze the app for minutes after approval: the import held the main thread ~0.4 s per 250-key batch back to back (worst 426 ms in the CK-scale bench, 46 ms now), and thousands of single-key backup requests (2,918 "keys" requests, 2,401 errors) ran at once | overlay (`perf/history-import-slices`) |

## Encrypted search index (feat/encrypted-search-index, Vommet issues 602 and 611, stage 1)

| Change | Why | Status |
|---|---|---|
| A local search index of the account's ENCRYPTED rooms, built in the background so search and the coming Shared counts don't page through a room's whole history each time. Stored per account in `<drift dir>/<client>/search_index.db`, beside the message store `data.db` (which already holds the same decrypted messages: same directory, same protection); deleted on logout, emptied by Settings › Advanced › Clear cache. `ClientManager.close()` now awaits every client's `close()` (10 s each), so the index isolate has shut its database before a caller deletes the data directory (the integration teardown's `clearUserData` also retries a delete that hit a vanishing -wal/-shm file). /messages pages (100) are fetched and decrypted on the main isolate, stored and queried by a separate isolate (`SearchIndexWorker`, SQLite). Each stretch of history is scanned once: per-room "segments" (backfill to the room start; top scan of what arrived while closed/off; the gap a limited sync left) and live sync messages added as they come. Edits (own sender only), redactions and messages that didn't decrypt yet (retried every 10 min) are handled. Web has no index (search unchanged there). New setting Settings › Privacy › Search › "Index encrypted chats" (`vommet_index_encrypted_chats`: Off / Wi-Fi only / Always; default Always on desktop, Wi-Fi only on phones, via connectivity_plus as for auto-download) with "Indexed N of M encrypted chats", a progress bar, its state and "Clear index". Off = nothing in the background, but a search still pages back and keeps what it scanned. Search in encrypted rooms now uses `MatrixIndexedRoomEventSearchSession` (instant indexed results, then 10 pages per call while the room isn't fully indexed; same search UI and `has:`/`from:`/`type:` filters). **API for stages 2/3:** `MatrixEncryptedSearchIndexComponent` (`lib/client/matrix/components/encrypted_search_index/`): `available`, `progress` (ValueNotifier `EncryptedIndexProgress` indexed/total/state), `onRoomUpdated` (room id stream), `coverage(roomId)` → `RoomCoverage` (complete/upToDate/oldestTs, for "37+"), `counts(roomId)` → `SharedContentCounts` (photosAndVideos, gifs, filesAndAudio, voice, links), `search(roomId, IndexQuery)`, `list(roomId, kinds:, linksOnly:, beforeTs:)` → `IndexHit` (decrypted event JSON + links), `indexOlder(roomId)` (scan one more page now), `clear()`; search sessions expose `progress` (`EncryptedSearchProgress`: searchedBackTo, found, complete). Unit test `unit_test/encrypted_search_index_test.dart` | Vommet issues 602 (Shared counts in DMs) and 611 (in-chat search): the server can't search or count encrypted messages, and the old encrypted search paged the timeline again for every search | overlay |
| A local search index of the account's ENCRYPTED rooms, built in the background so search and the coming Shared counts don't page through a room's whole history each time. Stored per account in `<drift dir>/<client>/search_index.db`, beside the message store `data.db` (which already holds the same decrypted messages: same directory, same protection); deleted on logout, emptied by Settings › Advanced › Clear cache. /messages pages (100) are fetched and decrypted on the main isolate, stored and queried by a separate isolate (`SearchIndexWorker`, SQLite). Edits (own sender only), redactions and messages that didn't decrypt yet (retried every 10 min) are handled. Web has no index (search unchanged there). Off = nothing in the background, but a search still pages back and keeps what it scanned. Search in encrypted rooms now uses `MatrixIndexedRoomEventSearchSession` (instant indexed results, then 10 pages per call while the room isn't fully indexed; same search UI and `has:`/`from:`/`type:` filters). **API for stages 2/3:** `MatrixEncryptedSearchIndexComponent` (`lib/client/matrix/components/encrypted_search_index/`): `available`, `progress` (ValueNotifier `EncryptedIndexProgress` indexed/total/state), `onRoomUpdated` (room id stream), `coverage(roomId)` → `RoomCoverage` (complete/upToDate/oldestTs, for "37+"), `counts(roomId)` → `SharedContentCounts` (photosAndVideos, gifs, filesAndAudio, voice, links), `search(roomId, IndexQuery)`, `list(roomId, kinds:, linksOnly:, beforeTs:)` → `IndexHit` (decrypted event JSON + links), `indexOlder(roomId)` (scan one more page now), `clear()`; search sessions expose `progress` (`EncryptedSearchProgress`: searchedBackTo, found, complete). Unit test `unit_test/encrypted_search_index_test.dart` | Vommet issues 602 (Shared counts in DMs) and 611 (in-chat search): the server can't search or count encrypted messages, and the old encrypted search paged the timeline again for every search | overlay |

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
