## Where the UI isolate's time goes: named spans (perf/native-stall-spans)

| Change | Why | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Opt-in diagnostics: the UI isolate's work runs in named spans (`lib/telemetry/main_spans.dart`). A zone span names a subsystem and times every callback scheduled inside it (`App` = the rest, `Matrix_client`, `Matrix_sdk` with the SDK's sync loop stages `Sdk_sync_request`/`Sdk_handle_sync`/`Sdk_device_keys`/`Sdk_encryption_on_sync`/`Sdk_to_device_queue` via the SDK's `MainSpanHooks` (vommet-v6.1.1-ss.29.10), `Notifications`, `Notify`, `Tray`, `Search_index`, `Http`, `Telemetry`, `File_cache`, `Window_management`, `Title_bar`, `Single_instance`, `System_integration`, `Shortcuts`, `Post_login_init`, `Linux_connectivity`, `Rust_lib_init`); sync spans time single sections (`Sync_*` steps of the account's sync handler, `Space_rooms_list`/`Space_top_level`/`Space_on_sync`, `Notification_counts`, `List_refilter`; SDK `Sdk_tracked_users`, `Sdk_backup_names_repair`, `Sdk_key_backup_upload`, `Sdk_sliding_sync_translate`). Own time leaves out inner spans. LoopLag's late ticks (≥ 1 s) are split by each span's own time since the previous tick (`Stall_<span>`, rest `Stall_none`), which also catches a block made of a microtask chain. Reported as more `timers` entries: app_ready `startup` (since launch; Stall_*, Main_*, Main_*_max, Phase_*) and perf_summary `timers` (since the previous summary). No schema change (validated with the collector's validator, v34). app_ready is now recorded from a timer so LoopLag's overdue tick runs first. Unit test `unit_test/main_spans_test.dart` | A tester's AppImage froze twice for ~11 s at startup (1,704 rooms) while every timed startup step was short; nothing said which code held the loop | overlay (`perf/native-stall-spans`) |

## Where a block outside every span sat, and what the UI thread did (perf/native-ffi-spans)

| Change | Why | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Opt-in diagnostics, more `timers` entries from `MainSpans` (no schema change, validated with the collector's validator, v35). The SDK's `runInRoot` work (sync loop, to-device handling, olm restore, key requests, last-event refresh…) now runs in named spans `Sdk_root_*` through `MainSpanHooks.rootZone` (vommet-v6.1.1-ss.29.11), so it is no longer counted as `Stall_none`. A block no span accounts for is placed in time: `Stall_after_<span>` (the span whose callback ran last before the longest quiet gap of a blocked tick), `Stall_phase_<span>` (the last finished phase), `Stall_pending_<call>` (platform calls waiting for their reply all through it). Every platform call goes through a timing messenger (`lib/telemetry/platform_calls.dart`, `ScaledWidgetsFlutterBinding.createBinaryMessenger`): names are the channel's last part and the method's name only; replies taking ≥ 1 s are `Platform_slow_<call>`. On Linux a helper isolate (`lib/telemetry/native_thread_probe_io.dart`) samples the UI thread from /proc while the loop is blocked: `Stall_thread_<class>` (run, disk, futex, poll, read_socket, ioctl_gpu…), every thread's CPU in blocks (`Stall_cpu_ui_thread`, `_dart_workers`, `_raster`, `_other_threads`, `Stall_dart_workers_busy`), `Stall_major_faults`, `Stall_probe_blocks`, `Stall_probe_paused` (the helper held up too: the VM paused the isolate group, e.g. a garbage collection), and `Stall_worst_rss_mb`/`Stall_worst_mem_avail_mb`, `Mem_total_mb`, `Ui_thread_separate`. Stall figures may now take two thirds of the list. Linux: `VOMMET_UI_THREAD=separate` (env, opt-in, testing only) runs the Dart UI isolate on its own thread instead of GTK's main thread (`linux/my_application.cc`). Unit tests `unit_test/main_spans_test.dart`, `unit_test/platform_calls_test.dart`, `unit_test/native_thread_probe_test.dart` | The ~11 s startup block on a tester's AppImage (1,704 rooms) was almost all `Stall_none` (10,962 of 11,110 ms): no Dart span ran in it, so the cause is native code on GTK's main thread (the UI isolate's thread on Linux), a VM pause, or root-zone SDK work; these figures tell them apart | overlay (`perf/native-ffi-spans`) |

## Messages sliding sync skipped are paged back (fix/sliding-sync-gaps)

| Change | Why | Status |
|---|---|---|
| SDK `vommet-v6.1.1-ss.29.12` (ss.29.11 + this): under sliding sync, a room whose unread count rose by more than the new events that came (server-side counts), or that is a suspect (events in the first rounds after resuming an old position, or activity moved with no timeline), is treated as having a gap: the stored timeline is set aside like after any limited sync and the room pages back across the gap when opened (a suspect is checked with one `/messages` call when opened). Nothing is fetched for rooms that aren't opened, no new UI. The encrypted search index maps the gap marker to "from the newest message". Integration test `integration_test/matrix/sync_gap_test.dart` (silent and post variants). | Tuwunel 1.9.x moves a room's position on a connection as soon as a request collects it, even without a timeline (timeline_limit 0), and then sends only newer events with `limited: false`: the ones in between never reached the app (seen on a device that was offline). | Operator-approved 2026-10-23 |

## On-device message translation, phase 1 (feat/680-message-translation)

| Change | Why | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Other people's text messages in another language get a **Translate** pill at the end (Linux and Android 9+; elsewhere nothing changes). Detection is CLD2 on the device, shown only for a reliable guess that differs from your language and that a model covers. The first tap asks once to download the language model (about 37 MB per direction, 120 directions, most through English) from Mozilla's Firefox Translations CDN; each file is checked against the SHA-256 pinned in `lib/utils/translation/models.dart` (generated by `packages/bergamot_translator/tool/gen_catalog.py` from Remote Settings `translations-models`, release-channel models only) and kept under app support `translation_models/`. The translation folds out under the original behind a divider, with "Spanish → English · translated on this device" and a chevron to fold it away; language pairs without English use two models. New **Settings › App › Translation** tab (before Advanced, only where translation runs): "Translate messages into" (new pref `message_translation_language`, `auto` = the system language, else English) and "Downloaded languages" with each direction's size on disk, Delete and Delete all (both confirm). Text never leaves the device, and translations are kept in memory only. Engine: Bergamot/Marian (Firefox Translations), vendored as the Dart FFI plugin `packages/bergamot_translator` (jesses2025smith/bergamot_translator, MPL-2.0), with the C++ sources (bergamot-translator, CLD2) fetched at pinned commits at build time. Linux x86_64 is built for x86-64-v2 (SSE4.2; older CPUs hide the button), Linux arm64 for armv8-a, Android for API 28 (the plugin keeps minSdk 24; Android 8 hides the button). The release builds are the first to compile the native code. `lib/utils/translation/`, `message_translation_fold.dart`, `translation_settings_page.dart`; unit tests `unit_test/translation/message_translation_test.dart` | Vommet issue 680 (operator 10-25: all recommendations — translation under the original, button only, all rooms, Bergamot; Settings page mockup OK 10-25) | overlay (`feat/680-message-translation`) |
| Message translation on **Windows** too (x64): the plugin builds with MSVC (Flutter's Visual Studio build). `packages/bergamot_translator/windows/CMakeLists.txt`, `pubspec.yaml` `windows: ffiPlugin`, a Windows block in `third_party_config.cmake` (no threads, internal PCRE2, library only), static `/MT` runtime for every target, NOMINMAX, using-declarations instead of `using namespace marian::bergamot` in `src/bergamot_translator.cpp` (MSVC found its Logger ambiguous), GCC-only flags behind `if(NOT MSVC)`, Marian's `/WX` off for its GCC pragmas, and a patch series in `third_party/patches/` (new `01-vommet-msvc-pcre2.patch`: ssplit's PCRE2 as `pcre2-8-static`) applied by `sources.cmake` with Git's own `patch` and LF patches (`.gitattributes`). `engine_bergamot.dart` enables Windows. Built and translating on GitHub's windows-2022 runner; not yet tested on a real Windows PC (no tester machine). | Vommet issue 680 (operator 10-25: "Go ahead" on the Windows engine) | overlay (`feat/680-message-translation`) |

| Web (WebAssembly build, Firefox and other non-Chromium browsers): space avatars on the rail and a space's home show their pictures instead of black squares. There skwasm (Flutter 3.47.7) decodes through an `<img>` element and passes the requested decode size to `createImageBitmap` as a crop rectangle, upscaling included, so a 90 px thumbnail decoded for 128 px came out as a 90x128 cut-out (room avatars, decoded smaller, lost their bottom third). Images are now decoded at their own size there and scaled down by the app (`decodeAtTargetSize`, never upscaling); the image bytes also get a buffer of their own on the web, since that path builds its Blob from the whole underlying buffer. No change on native, in the JS build or in Chromium | `utils/image/sized_decode.dart`, `utils/image/engine_crops_target_size*.dart`, `utils/image/lod_image.dart` | testing (`feat/web-build`) |

Outside Chromium a decoded image is backed by an `<img>` element and reading its pixels back fails, so on the web the seed-colour step always redraws the image first, as it already did for images over 112 px | `utils/image/image_seed_color.dart` | testing (`feat/web-build`) |

## Rooms the server dropped us from without a leave (fix/667-room-removed-banner)

| Change | Why | Status |
|---|---|---|
| A room the server no longer has us in, though no leave ever reached the app, now says so. Found two ways: when a send is refused with `M_FORBIDDEN` "not in room" (text and files), and once per start after the first sync, by comparing the rooms the SDK holds as joined with `GET /joined_rooms` (only rooms joined before and after the request count). Such a room stays readable; its composer becomes a notice "You're no longer in this room." with **Rejoin** (joins through the room id's server and the servers with the most members, never only our own) and **Forget** (asks first, then marks the room left locally the way the SDK's own leave does for an unknown room, and forgets it). Its sidebar row is faded with a broken-link icon and a Forget menu entry, like a banned room. No read receipts are sent from it. The flag clears when the room's events arrive in a real sync again (rejoined anywhere), on Rejoin, or when the leave finally arrives. Kept per account (`vommet_removed_rooms_<account>`). `MatrixRemovedRooms` (matrix_removed_rooms.dart), `MatrixClient._reconcileJoinedRooms`, `RemovedRoomNotice`, `ComposerNotice` second action. Unit tests `unit_test/removed_rooms_test.dart` | Vommet issue 667: after a Synapse admin purged a room (Delete Room API), the app kept showing it as joined with old messages and every send failed with no explanation | overlay (`fix/667-room-removed-banner`) |
## A large account's start no longer floods the server (perf/startup-request-storm)

| Change | Why | Status |
|---|---|---|
| SDK `vommet-v6.1.1-ss.29.14`: a profile the server failed to give is remembered per user (not found / not allowed for 1 h, rate limits as the server says, other errors 30 s doubling to 15 min; a member event or a success clears it) and answered with the stale copy or the same error meanwhile, logged once per user; at most 4 profile, 6 member lookups and 2 preview refreshes in flight per account, with the fill-in lookups of names and avatars (room list rows, DM partners, push rules) behind anything someone waits for (which waits at most its timeout for a turn); a timed-out request keeps its slot until the server answers (capped), so it can't pile up sockets. App: the encrypted search index starts its background backfill 45 s after sign-in (90 s on phones; a network or setting change doesn't shorten it), rests at least 1 s (1.5 s) and twice as long as each page took, and syncs no longer cut that pause short; searches and the Shared tabs still scan right away. Thumbnails download 6 at a time per account (only the download, not the cache reads; a silent download lets go of its slot after 60 s). At most 64 connections to a server (dart:io's client had no limit), 30 s to connect. Linux: the soft open-file limit is raised to 8,192 (many desktops start apps with 1,024). Unit tests `unit_test/startup_request_storm_test.dart`, `unit_test/matrix_http_client_test.dart`, SDK `test/vommet/request_storm_test.dart` | A tester's AppImage start (1,700 rooms, 6,600 users): ~24,000 "Unable to fetch profile" log lines; in the first 15 minutes 501 profile requests (441 failed, p95 48 s), 1,938 member lookups (1,058 failed), 306 thumbnails (299 failed), 2,815 /messages (76 MB), then ~1,300 /messages (~90 MB) every 15 minutes for hours from the index backfill; a FileSystemException from File.open during the burst | overlay (`perf/startup-request-storm`) |
## Copy message link (feat/665-copy-message-link)

| Change | Why | Status |
|---|---|---|
| "Copy message link" in the message menu (right-click on desktop, long-press on phones), for any sent Matrix event: copies an Element-style matrix.to permalink, `https://matrix.to/#/<room id>/<event id>?via=…`, built by the forward's existing `ForwardContent.eventPermalink`. `via` is chosen like Element's: the server of the highest-powered member (power level 50+), then the servers with the most joined members, three at most, skipping IP literals and servers the room's `m.room.server_acl` denies (`lib/client/matrix/matrix_permalink.dart`). Opening a link to a message in Vommet (in a message, a room pill, or from another app) now opens the room's chat and jumps to the message like picking a search result (`RoomOpenArgs.eventId`, `EventBus.setPendingJump`/`takePendingJump`, taken by the room's timeline view once it lays out; a jump not taken within a minute is dropped); the join dialog only shows when you aren't in the room. Fixes the cause of links to a message offering to join a room you're already in: the event id stayed glued to the room id (`!room/$event`), so no room matched; `MatrixClient.parseMatrixLink` and `LinkUtils` now split it off and keep every `via`. Unit tests `unit_test/matrix_permalink_test.dart`, `unit_test/matrix_link_parse_test.dart` | Vommet issue 665: share a link to a message, interoperable with Element | overlay (`feat/665-copy-message-link`) |

| Link previews the sender's app bundles in the event (MSC4095 `m.url_previews`, unstable `com.beeper.linkpreviews`) now show from that data: no homeserver `preview_url` request, so they also show in encrypted rooms where homeserver previews are off by default (they're hidden only when the user, or in an unencrypted room the admins, turned previews off). Reads the stable `matrix:matched_url`/`matrix:image:encrypted` and unstable `matched_url`/`beeper:image:encryption`; the issue-352 allow-list now reads the stable key too. Images only from `mxc://` (plain or an EncryptedFile, decrypted locally), never a web address, and downloads stop at 10 MB; no video. Cached per event, never per link. The first bundled preview from someone else in a chat shows a consent card instead ("Show in this chat" → room account data `im.vommet.bundled_url_previews` `{"allowed": true}`, synced; "Show in all chats" → new pref `vommet_bundled_url_previews_ask` off; "Not now" → that message only); your own previews never ask. Every bundled preview shows the link's real domain under it ("… · preview made by the sender's app"). Settings › General gets "Ask before showing sender-made link previews"; Room settings › URL previews gets "Show without asking" for the chat. `bundled_url_preview.dart`, `bundled_url_preview_consent_card.dart`, `url_preview_room_policy.dart`; unit tests `unit_test/bundled_url_preview_test.dart` | Vommet issue 676 phase 1 (operator 10-24 approved the plan: per-chat consent, bundled-only default for encrypted chats). Phase 2 (sending) and phase 3 (Bundled-only setting + defaults) follow as their own topics | overlay (`feat/676-bundled-previews-receive`) |

## Bundled link previews, phase 2: send (feat/676-bundled-send)

| Change | Why | Status |
|---|---|---|
| The message box makes a preview for the first previewable http(s) link (same one the timeline previews; not `<url>`, not matrix.to) after an 0.8 s pause in typing, like Signal: this device fetches the page itself, never via the homeserver's `preview_url`. Guards: http(s) only; every connection resolves the host and refuses non-public addresses (loopback, RFC 1918, link-local, CGNAT, ULA, multicast/reserved, IPv4 inside IPv6), also after redirects (max 3); no proxy, no cookies; 5 s timeout each for page and image; at most 1 MB of HTML; image (JPEG/PNG/GIF/WebP) at most 5 MB, decoded in an isolate (refuses > 40 MP) and re-encoded at most 800 px on the longest side (drops EXIF). A bar above the box shows the preview with an × ("Send without preview"). On send it goes into the event as `com.beeper.linkpreviews` (`matched_url`, `og:*`, `matrix:image:size`); the image is uploaded on send, encrypted (`beeper:image:encryption` EncryptedFile, no `og:image`) in an encrypted room — left out if file encryption is off — and plain (`og:image` mxc) in others; a failed upload sends the preview without its image. Edits get none; a preview whose link left the text isn't attached. New pref `vommet_bundled_url_previews_send` (on; Settings › General "Attach previews to links I send", with the IP-address note). Web doesn't make previews (CORS; a proxy would see every link): no toggle there. `Room.sendMessage`/`ThreadsComponent.sendMessage` gain `urlPreviews`. `outgoing_url_preview.dart`, `link_preview_fetcher{,_io,_stub}.dart`, `composer_link_preview.dart`; unit tests `unit_test/outgoing_url_preview_test.dart` | Vommet issue 676 phase 2 (operator 10-24 approved: fetch in the composer after a pause, guards, on by default, web shows but doesn't make) | overlay (`feat/676-bundled-send`, after `feat/676-bundled-receive`) |

## Key backup misses remembered (perf/backup-key-miss-cache)

| Change | Why | Status |
|---|---|---|
| SDK vommet-v6.1.1-ss.29.15: a room key the online backup does not have (404) is not looked up again for 1 h by background lookups (search index backfill, automatic requests, retries) or 5 min by ones the user sees (Retry Decrypt, a message being shown); other errors back off 30 s doubling to 5 min, rate limits wait retry_after. Bounded (5,000), per (room, session); dropped on a new backup version, the backup key being cached, or the session arriving another way. Never permanent: another of the user's devices may upload the key later. SDK test `test/vommet/backup_key_miss_cache_test.dart` | A tester's telemetry: ~1,900 `keys` requests / ~1,800 errors in 15 min, each undecryptable event of a session asking the backup again | overlay (`perf/backup-key-miss-cache`) |

## Lazy Overview (perf/new-home-lazy-overview)

| Change | Why | Status |
|---|---|---|
| New Home: the Overview is a flat `CustomScrollView` of slivers instead of one `ListView` holding a `Column` of every card. Room-list cards (Recent activity, Favourites, Standalone rooms, Unread, Mentions, Low priority, Space, Tags, Invites) are a `NewHomeCardSliver` (the same box via `DecoratedSliver` around one `SliverList.builder`: header, then the rows with the same paddings), so only the rows near the screen are built. No `SliverMainAxisGroup`: in Flutter 3.41 it places the slivers after a long card on screen for focus order, so Tab jumped past the unbuilt rows to the Add a card tile; the other cards stay plain boxes. Same look, spacing, menus and "Show N more"; customize mode (drag and drop) is unchanged and still builds whole cards. Known differences, none visible with the bundled themes: while a long card is only partly built the scroll length is an estimate (the scrollbar thumb can shift slightly as rows appear); earlier cards paint over later ones (a custom theme `shadows` entry wider than the 12 px gap overlaps the next card from above instead of below); a row scrolled far away is rebuilt when it comes back (the row holding the keyboard focus stays built, so focus and Enter stay on it; Tab after scrolling away with the mouse continues from the rows on screen); a card wholly off screen paints no shadow at the edge. Unit tests `unit_test/new_home_overview_lazy_test.dart` (1000 standalone rooms build < 60 rows; Tab and Shift+Tab walk the rows in order and the focused row survives scrolling away; sliver and box lay out identically for 8, 1 and 0 rows; a reordered list shows the new order) | The default Overview's Standalone rooms card (since testing-2026-10-23e) kept a live row per standalone room: +80 MB peak memory at 250 rooms, more on big accounts. Operator 10-24: option (a), no visual change | overlay (`perf/new-home-lazy-overview`) |

## Gray and red badges (feat/719-badges)

| Change | Why | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Three kinds of badge on rooms, spaces, folders, New Home sections, the rooms (#) button, Home and People: an unread dot; a **gray** number for silent notifications (the push rule notifies without a sound); a **red** number for noisy ones (mentions, keywords, or messages whose push rule has the `sound` tweak). Counts add up into spaces and sections, and red wins. A room on All messages counts every notifying message (it showed only a dot unless mentioned); Mentions & Keywords counts the mentions. "Noisy" is the account's own push rules evaluated for an ordinary message in that room (`MatrixRoom.messagesAreNoisy`, room rules included), so under the spec's defaults DMs are red and group chats gray, and Element-made settings are followed. Mentions in encrypted rooms are found on the device as messages decrypt and added to the server's highlight count until the account's read receipt passes them (in memory only). Rule: `lib/utils/badge_rules.dart`; tests `unit_test/badge_kinds_test.dart`; New Home section badges (Vommet issue 627) now total their rooms' counts instead of mentions plus a red DM dot. Tray/taskbar unchanged (chats, Vommet issue 654). Vommet issue 676, phase 3 (operator 10-24: option B, "Automatic" default).

  homeserver previews, or Off. Any choice but Automatic applies to every chat. Stored as `vommet_url_preview_mode`
  ("auto"/"bundled"/"all"/"off").

  homeserver) instead of on/off. Stored in Element's keys (on/off) plus room account data `im.vommet.url_previews`
  `{"mode":"bundled"}` for Bundled only, so Element sees Bundled only as off.
- Settings search entries moved to Privacy › Link previews.

## On-device message translation, phase 2 (feat/680-composer-translation)

| Change | Why | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **Translate button when writing in DMs.** In a DM, while the draft isn't empty, a `文A ES` chip sits inside the text field, left of the emoji button (Linux and Android 9+, like phase 1). It translates into the language the other person writes in: the most common reliable CLD2 guess over their last 10 text messages in the loaded timeline (ties go to the newest). Tap translates the draft on the device (source = a reliable guess at the draft's language, else your translation language), asking before a missing model downloads with phase 1's dialog, then replaces the draft and shows a line above the composer in the Reply/Edit line's style: ⊗ (hide the line, keep the translation) · 文A "Translated to Spanish on this device" · "Yours: …" (one line) · **Undo** (puts back what you wrote). It never sends by itself; sending clears the line. Right-click or long-press opens **Translate into** (✓ on the current one; languages picked before first, then the others a model reaches from the draft's language); when no language is known yet, a plain tap opens it too. The pick is remembered per room (new pref `message_translation_compose`, JSON: per-room language + the last 8 picked) until changed. New switch in **Settings › App › Translation**: "Translate button when writing in DMs" (new pref `message_translation_compose_button`, default on). The engine now runs one translation at a time (messages and the composer share a queue). `lib/utils/translation/composer_translation.dart`, `lib/ui/molecules/composer_translation.dart`, `message_input.dart`, `chat_view.dart`; unit tests `unit_test/translation/composer_translation_test.dart` (the fake engine moved to `translation_fakes.dart`) | Vommet issue 680 (operator 10-25: phase 2 + room mode mockups OK, all recommendations) | overlay (`feat/680-composer-translation`) |
| **Translate this room** (all room types, where translation runs). A new room quick-access entry (文A, next to Search/Widgets in the desktop header and in the phone's room panel; the app has no ⋯ menu there) switches it per room (new pref `message_translation_rooms`, JSON per room: on, "Messages are in", "Translate what I write"). While it's on, the header shows `文A Translating from Spanish ▾` (the language you picked, else the most common reliable guess over others' last 10 text messages; `文A ES ▾` on phones; a spinner while a model downloads); tapping it opens a sheet with **Translate this room**, **Messages are in** (Detected / a language) and **Translate what I write before sending** (default on). "Show the original: when I tap 文A" is the only behavior, so that row is left out. **Reading:** other people's text messages in a language that isn't yours and that a model covers are translated as they're built on screen (the timeline builds lazily, so only what you scroll to), one at a time through a queue that skips messages already scrolled away; the original shows dimmed meanwhile. A translated message shows the translation in place of the original, followed by a small 文A (at the end of the text rather than after the timestamp, which lives in the shared layout); tapping it shows the original under it in a quiet box with **Copy**. Missing models are asked for once per room and language pair (phase 1's dialog); saying no leaves that pair to the phase 1 Translate pill for the session (switching the mode off and on asks again). Switching the mode off folds the room-made translations away (the pill's "Show translation" brings one back). Translations stay in memory only, as in phase 1. **Writing:** with "Translate what I write" on, a strip above the composer shows the translation while you type (500 ms after you stop): accent bar · 文A "Will send in Spanish:" · the translation (or why there isn't one). **Send sends only the translation**; if it isn't ready yet, it translates first (asking for a missing model), and if that fails or is declined the draft stays with "Not sent. …" above it, never sending untranslated. The DM chip shows filled in this mode; there it turns "Translate what I write" off and on, and right-click/long-press picks the room's language. Commands (`/…`) and messages sent as another account (account switch prefix) go out as typed. **Your messages sent this way** show what you wrote, with a quiet "Sent in Spanish: …" under it; the device keeps the newest 100 (room, sent text, what you wrote, language) in new pref `message_translation_sent`, matched by room and the sent text. **Limits:** only the plain-text body is translated and shown (formatting, links and mention pills in a translated message show as plain text; mentions in what you write are translated as text, so a display-name mention may change); messages with code (```` ``` ````, `<pre>`, `<code>`) and messages with attachments are left alone by the room mode; edits and replies are translated from their plain body. `lib/utils/translation/room_translation.dart`, `lib/ui/molecules/room_translation_views.dart`, `message_translation_fold.dart`, `composer_translation.dart`, `message_input.dart`, `timeline_event_view_message.dart`, `room_header.dart`, `room_quick_access_menu.dart`; unit tests `unit_test/translation/room_translation_test.dart` | Vommet issue 680 (operator 10-25: phase 2 + room mode mockups OK, all recommendations) | overlay (`feat/680-composer-translation`) |

## A dropped call ends instead of staying open (fix/749-dropped-call-ends)

| Change | Issue | Status |
|---|---|---|
| When the call connection drops for good (LiveKit gives up reconnecting, or the server removes us), the call now ends on our side too: it leaves, clears our call membership (retrying in the background while offline) and stops the heartbeat. Before, the call stayed open on screen and our membership kept being refreshed, so the other person saw us in the call for hours. Hang up also always ends the call now: a leave step that fails while offline (closing the LiveKit connection, cancelling the heartbeat) used to stop the call from ending, so it couldn't be hung up at all (`MatrixRtcLeave.runSteps`). The leftover membership after a restart is cleared by `fix/call-leftovers-and-errors` | #749 | testing (topic `fix/749-dropped-call-ends`) |

## Chat wallpapers (1:1 chats)

| Change | Issue | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Experiment "Chat wallpapers" (`vommet_experiment_chat_wallpapers`, on by default): a 1:1 chat (a DM with at most two people) can have a wallpaper both people see, set from the room menu (Discord-style layout: the ▾ menu) or the chat's Appearance settings. The dialog uploads a picture (scaled to at most 2560 px, made upright, EXIF removed, JPEG), has Darker / lighter and Blur sliders, a preview with sample messages, a Recent grid (one entry per picture, newest first, Select mode to remove entries) and Remove wallpaper; nothing changes until Apply. Protocol: state event `im.nether.chat_wallpaper` (state key "") holds only `{"event_id"}` (`{}` = none), because state events are never encrypted; that id is an ordinary `im.nether.chat_wallpaper` room event (encrypted in encrypted rooms) with `file` (encrypted) or `url`, `info`, `dim` (-1..1), `blur` (0..1) and `source` (sha256 of the uploaded picture). Re-applying a picture reuses its upload. Your own `hidden` flag and `recent` event ids are room account data `im.nether.chat_wallpaper` (no picture keys). The state change shows as "X changed / removed the chat wallpaper"; the picture event is hidden (other clients don't know its type). Settings › Appearance › "Show chat wallpapers" hides them on a device. `MatrixChatWallpaperComponent`, `ui/organisms/chat_wallpaper/`, `MatrixTimelineEventChatWallpaper`. New Intl strings aren't in intl_en.arb yet, and the experiment key isn't in the telemetry schema's `experiment_key` list (reported as "other"). Unit test `unit_test/chat_wallpaper_test.dart` | Vommet issue 746 | overlay (`feat/746-chat-wallpaper`) |

## Push rule evaluation fixes (fix/push-rule-eval-sdk)

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| SDK `vommet-v6.1.1-ss.29.17`: the push rule evaluator counts `room_member_count` from the room summary (joined members, as the homeserver does; loaded members only as a fallback), so a big room with two members loaded no longer matches the one-to-one rule (desktop notified for every message in big rooms set to mentions only) and a direct message without loaded members does; it checks content (keyword) rules before room and sender rules, as the spec orders them, so keywords notify in rooms set to Mentions & Keywords; and in encrypted rooms `onNotification` no longer requires the server's notification count (the server can't see mentions or keywords inside the ciphertext): a new decrypted event (at most 10 minutes old, not covered by our own read receipt) notifies on the local match, also when its key arrives later, and no event is notified twice. The desktop notification's sound and mention flag and `eventMentionsMe` use `MatrixPushRules.match`, the same match as `shouldNotify` (legacy mention rules off when `m.mentions` is present, members counted like the server). (`pubspec.yaml`, `matrix_room.dart`, `unit_test/matrix_push_rules_test.dart`) | overlay (`fix/push-rule-eval-sdk`) |

## Sharing packs (feat/731-sharing)

| Change | Issue | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Sharing for the Library (Vommet issue 731, phase 2). A collection is a sticker room; its admin gets "Share…" in the pack pane: "Sharing applies to every pack in <room>", modes Private (join rule `invite`), Followers (`public`, "Anyone with the link can follow", only admins edit) and Community (Followers plus contributors at power level 50; its switch picks `public` or `invite`), applied as picked. A mode switch starts from the room's current `m.room.power_levels`, forces the pack-room map (packs 50, redact 100, `events_default` 100, new `im.vommet.collection_mode` at 100), `users_default` 0, then sets exactly the contributors to 50 (Community) or drops everyone at 50 (Private/Followers); admins are never touched and from room version 12 the creators stay out of `users`. The mode is room state `im.vommet.collection_mode` `{"mode": "private"\|"followers"\|"community"}` (key ""); without it, a public room counts as Followers (Community if anyone is at 50), else Private. Community lists contributors with Add contributor (person picker; invites non-members) and remove, plus "Contributors can also remove anyone's items. The room history shows who changed what."; shared modes show a copyable matrix.to link (alias, else room id with up to three `via` servers) and "Followers join this room, so its members can see who follows."; every mode has "Invite people…". Following: the sticker sheet (tap a sticker in chat) offers "Follow pack" when the sticker's pack tag names a room you're not in, and the Library's new FOLLOWING sidebar group (pack rooms you're in but can't edit) ends with "Follow a pack…" (matrix.to link, `matrix:` URI, `#alias:server` or `!roomid`, optional `?via=`); both confirm "Following joins <room>. Its members and its server can see that you follow it.", join (with `via`), check it is a pack room (else leave again and say so; 403 and not found get their own messages) and turn on all its packs in both enable lists in one write (new `setEmoticonRoomPacks`). Followed packs are view only with Unfollow and "Make my own copy" (downloads and uploads every image again into your own sticker room, a new one if you have none). Sticker rooms get Leave; leaving or unfollowing turns the room's packs off in both enable lists, and warns "You're its only admin. Nobody will be able to change its packs after you leave." when others are in it. "Send a copy…" on a selection: pick a person, confirm "They get a copy of these N items. Later changes you make won't reach them.", and a new private sticker room "<pack> for <their name>" holds one pack with the items (same mxc URLs), the person invited as an admin through the `trusted_private_chat` preset (their level is set to 100 afterwards if the server didn't), `im.vommet.collection_mode` gets `"sent_to"`; leaving it before they joined warns. Changed since you last looked (followed and Community collections): account data `im.vommet.library_seen` `{"<room id>": {"<pack state key>": "<event id>"}}`; a pack whose current event (the one the pack is read from) differs and wasn't sent by you gets a dot in the sidebar and "Changed by <name>, <time ago>" in the pane subtitle; opening it marks it seen (written 2 s later, once per burst, never when unchanged); rooms never looked at are noted on first sight instead of all showing as changed. | In unencrypted rooms the Media and Files tabs page older history with a server-filtered `/messages` (`{"contains_url": true, "types": ["m.room.message"]}`, 50 per request, own token; `RoomMediaHistoryComponent`) instead of the room timeline's 30-event pages; results merge with what the timeline already shows (deduped by event id, newest first), messages deleted later drop out, and the Links tab and encrypted rooms keep paging the timeline. ## Pending-decryption queue keeps events still waiting for their key (feat/room-notify-use-default, SDK)

| Change | Issue | Status |
|---|---|---|
| SDK `vommet-v6.1.1-ss.29.20` (on ss.29.19, commit f6c0fb60be, branch `fix/pending-decrypt-queue`): after a room key arrives, the SDK's queue of events waiting for their keys only drops the events of that room that decrypted (by event id). Upstream compared `content['event_id']`, null on both sides, so one decrypted event emptied the whole queue (every room) and events waiting for another session's key were never retried when it came: no late notification for them (ss.29.17's notify-on-late-decrypt) and their stored copy stayed encrypted until the room's timeline decrypted it. Tests `test/vommet/encrypted_notifications_test.dart` (two events, two keys, both orders; failed before) | operator 10-26 | overlay (`feat/room-notify-use-default`) |

## Search index v2 for Deep Search (feat/search-index-v2)

| Change | Issue | Status |
|---|---|---|
| The on-device search index (encrypted chats) is upgraded in place for the coming Deep Search: a real v1 → v2 migration (new columns `doc_id`, `mention_ids`, `mentions_me`, `thread_root`, `is_reply`, `v2`; rooms `saw_create`) keeps every stored message, and the full-text tables (FTS5 `unicode61 remove_diacritics`, prefix 2/3; a trigram side table for Chinese, Japanese and Korean text) are filled from the stored rows in small resumable background steps; rows not yet filled, and a SQLite without FTS5, are still found with `instr()`. Every DM is now indexed too, encrypted or not; unencrypted group rooms stay with server search. Build order: DMs, favorites, rooms active in the last 30 days, the rest, low priority last. New cross-room `searchAll` (newest 5,000 matches read newest first, then bm25 × recency with a 30-day half-life × caller boosts for exact phrase, DMs, favorites, rooms I posted in; per-room counts; filters for senders, ignored senders, rooms, kinds, links, mentions me incl. display names at query time, before/after) on a second read-only connection in its own isolate, with stale searches dropped. Reply fallbacks (`> ` lines) are no longer searchable. Coverage totals (complete, in progress, undecryptable, history-visibility limit). Undecryptable messages are retried a few seconds after their room gets a key (live or from the backup), not only every 10 minutes. Indexing pauses on battery saver or below 20% while not charging, and whenever the device runs on battery while Settings › Privacy › Search › "Pause on battery power" is on (Vommet issue 845, operator 10-29: option A toggle, on by default on laptops, off on phones; the row shows only on devices with a battery; "Paused to save battery"). Battery readers, no new plugin: Android `VommetPower.kt` channel; Linux `/sys/class/power_supply` (only system batteries count, a wireless mouse or headset with `scope=Device` is ignored; an online AC adapter or USB-C charger means plugged in); Windows `GetSystemPowerStatus` via `win32` (already in the lockfile, now a direct dependency; `power_state_windows.dart`, conditional import so web builds skip `dart:ffi`). macOS doesn't pause yet (phase 2: an IOKit channel, needs a Mac check). `indexOlderNeedsConfirmation` + `allowMobileDataThisSession()` for the Deep Search UI. Settings › Privacy › Search shows the index size; progress reads "Indexed N of M chats". ## Use less data for calls (fix/776-call-data-saver)

| Change | Issue | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Settings › Data and storage › Calls gets "Use less data for calls": Never / Roaming only / Mobile data and roaming / Always (default Mobile data and roaming; on Linux and Windows the middle choice reads "Metered connections", roaming is phones only, and macOS and web offer Never / Always). While it is in effect, group (LiveKit) calls send the camera at 360p 15 fps, screen shares at 720p 15 fps 1 Mbps and voice at 32 kbps, overriding the Voice and video settings, and receive the lowest layer of other people's cameras and at most the middle layer of a screen share (also when watched with stream watching); classic 1:1 calls ask for a 360p 15 fps camera and a 720p 15 fps screen share. A "Saving data" label shows next to "Voice connected" in the call panel. When the network changes mid-call, the voice bitrate and receiving change at once, a running camera restarts at the new size, a stopped one uses it at its next start, and a screen share at the next share. The camera still starts off. ## HEIC pictures in full on Android (fix/778-heic-pictures)

| Change | Issue | Status |
|---|---|---|
| HEIC/HEIF pictures (and AVIF from Android 12) show as pictures on Android 9+ even when the sender attached no thumbnail, in full in the timeline and viewer, and count as pictures in search and photo albums. Flutter hands formats it can't read to the platform decoder, and only Android has one (`ImageDecoder`, API 28+), so the types are picked from the Android API level read once at startup (`platform_image_types.dart`, `AttachmentMime.isFullPicture`). iOS, macOS, Windows, Linux and web are unchanged: thumbnail-only through the sender's thumbnail (Vommet issue 329), else a file tile; no new native libraries. Tests `unit_test/platform_image_types_test.dart` | Vommet issue 778 | overlay (`fix/778-heic-pictures`) |

## HEIC pictures in full on Linux and Windows (fix/778-heic-pictures follow-up)

| Change | Issue | Status |
|---|---|---|
| HEIC/HEIF pictures show in full on Linux and Windows too (timeline, viewer, search, photo albums, copy as picture), through the system's own decoder: on Linux the installed libheif with its HEVC plugin (opened at runtime, not linked or bundled), on Windows WIC with Microsoft's "HEIF Image Extensions" + "HEVC Video Extensions". The picture is decoded in a background isolate into a BMP the engine reads; WIC's orientation is applied, libheif applies it itself. A 16x8 HEIC test picture is decoded once at startup and only when that works do HEIC/HEIF count as decodable (`PlatformImageTypes`); otherwise they keep the thumbnail-only path or a file tile as before. Saving keeps the original file. Web uses a stub (no dart:ffi). No new dependencies or packaging changes. (`heif_decode.dart`, `heif_decode_ffi.dart`, `heif_decode_stub.dart`, `platform_image_types.dart`, `sized_decode.dart`, `image_save.dart`, tests `unit_test/heif_decode_test.dart`) | Vommet issue 813 | overlay follow-up (`fix/778-heic-pictures`) |

## Telegram themes (feat/telegram-themes)

| Change | Issue | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Settings › Appearance gets a **Telegram** row with Telegram's eight built-in themes: Desktop Classic, Day, Tinted, Night and Android Blue, Arctic Blue, Dark Blue, Night (`telegram_themes.dart`, ids `telegram-<slug>`, with `:<accent>` or `:#rrggbb`). Each has **accent circles**: the theme's own, Telegram's accents and a custom color. Like Telegram, Android accents also recolor your own bubbles and the chat background. The themes fill the Light/Dark slots when following the system, like the gradients. **Behind the messages**, a theme can now draw a color or gradient with Telegram's doodle pattern (`ChatStyle` theme extension, theme.json `"chat": {background, pattern, patternStrength, bubbleRadius}`; `ChatBackdrop`, behind the timeline, so it shows in every message layout; a room's own wallpaper covers it). The pattern is Telegram Desktop's `background.tgv` (GPLv3+), shipped as `assets/images/telegram/pattern.svg.gz`. The Telegram themes have it on. The theme editor gets: Background › "Behind messages" colors (up to 4), Pattern Off / Telegram doodles with a strength slider, and Shape › "Message bubble corners" (0–24; Chat bubbles layout only). Telegram themes are start points. **Import**: the + button also takes Telegram theme files (`.tdesktop-theme`, a Telegram Desktop `.zip`, `.attheme`; `telegram_theme_import.dart`). They open in the theme editor with an "Imported from Telegram" banner and are saved only when you save. Their colors map to the editor's slots. A Desktop .zip's background picture, or an `.attheme`'s embedded one, becomes its average color. Nothing from the file is written to disk, and other .zip files install as before. Telegram Desktop (GPLv3+) and Telegram for Android (GPLv2+) are credited on the licenses page. Emoji presets and own-art patterns are not in this change. Tests: `unit_test/telegram_themes_test.dart`. | operator 10-26 (premium-free batch, F2) | overlay (`feat/telegram-themes`) |

## Chat wallpapers: colors, groups, only for me

| Change | Issue | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Builds on the chat wallpapers experiment (same switch). **Groups:** any chat can have a wallpaper now, not only 1:1 chats; in a group "For everyone" needs the power level to send the `im.nether.chat_wallpaper` state event, everyone else can still pick one only for themselves. **Only for me:** the dialog's "For both of us" (1:1) / "For everyone" (groups) / "Only for me" choice; your own wallpaper is room account data `im.nether.chat_wallpaper` → `own` (the same fields as the shared event; a picture is always uploaded encrypted, its key in that account data, so in encrypted chats the dialog notes the homeserver could open it), synced to your devices, shown instead of the shared one, and dropped when you set one for everyone; room Appearance settings get "Use the shared one" / "Use the group's". **Colors:** a Colors tab with 8 presets and 1–4 custom colors (theme color picker); the event (or `own`) carries `fill: {"colors": ["#rrggbb", …], "animate": bool}` instead of a picture, so nothing is uploaded. 1 color = solid, 2 = diagonal gradient, 3–4 = a four-point gradient (our own drawing: colors on every other point of an 8-point ring, weight `max(0, 0.9 − distance)^4`, a 16×16 vertex mesh) that moves one step (0.5 s) on each new message when "Move with new messages" is on, never with reduced motion. **Layouts:** with message bubbles off (Discord style, or a Custom mix without bubbles) a color wallpaper is washed 60% with the chat background so plain text stays readable, and the dialog preview draws messages the way the layout does. Older Vommet versions ignore a `fill` event and show no wallpaper. Unit test `unit_test/chat_wallpaper_fill_test.dart` | premium-free batch F5 | topic `feat/chat-wallpaper-colors` (after `feat/746-chat-wallpaper`) |

## New Home ranked search (feat/new-home-ranked-search)

| Change | Issue | Status |
|---|---|---|
| New Home's side list search covers every joined room and DM of the filtered account (not only the shown sections; rooms hidden from New Home and replaced room versions left out; the same room on two accounts once, another account's rows with its avatar) and ranks the matches in groups, each room once: NAME (name or a DM's user id; at the start, then a word's start, then inside; newest first; all shown), IN <space path> (rooms in a space or subspace whose name matches; three and "Show N more", which expands in place; "all N ›" scopes to it), TAGGED <tag>, TOPIC (a snippet around the hit) and at most three SPACES to open. Matching ignores case and accents; the hit is bold in the accent color, and a row's second line is its space path ("Nether › Software Development"). While searching, the tab rows hide and a chips row shows DMs n, Rooms n and the matched spaces (same-named ones with their parent, "Infra · Nether") and tags; a chip becomes a token in the field (its × removes it; Backspace in the empty field too) that narrows the search; a space token shows a breadcrumb ("All results › Nether › Software Development") that widens it, subspace chips that narrow it, and "Open <space>" first. Enter (the phone's search key) opens the highlighted result, Up/Down move the highlight, Esc clears, Alt+Up/Down follow the results' order. A room's hold / right-click menu in the side list and in results starts with "Go to <space>" for each of its spaces and "Search in <space>". The index is built once per sync, space or account change, not per keystroke. Ctrl+K's Quick Switcher ranks with the same engine through a small adapter (`vommet_quick_switcher_rank.dart`, replacing Commet's fuzzy match in `quick_switcher.dart`). Look further back asks first when indexing is off or would use mobile data. Entry points: the strip, the row menu, the side list's room menu "Search messages here", and the in-chat search's new "Search all chats" button (keeps the words and the chat as a chip). **Side list:** its search always ends with "Search messages for “X” ›" (Shift+Enter). **Shortcuts:** Ctrl+Shift+F anywhere; "/" only when no text field has focus. **Opening a result** jumps to the message in its chat (outlined for 3 s); a thread reply also opens its thread; a room you left says "You left this room". A results bar over the chat shows ‹ Results, the search, "3 of 14", ↑ ↓ across chats (Ctrl+Shift+G / Ctrl+G) and ×. ‹ Results returns to the list with its query, filters and scroll, with ✓ seen and "last opened" marks. ## Encrypted-room media sealed in the cache, cache off /tmp (fix/encrypted-media-cache)

| Change | Issue | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Media from encrypted rooms (pictures, thumbnails, videos, GIFs, audio, voice messages, files, inline HTML images; also link-preview images, which share one cache across rooms) is never written to disk in plaintext. Each cache entry is sealed with XChaCha20-Poly1305 (`cryptography`'s Dart implementation) under a key derived by HKDF-SHA256 from a random 256-bit cache key, in 64 KiB segments (format "VME2": a random 128-bit prefix per entry plus the segment counter as the nonce; the header, identifier, segment index and a last-segment flag bound as associated data, so a truncated, reordered or extended file doesn't open). File names and database rows are an HMAC of the identifier (`e1_<hex>`, `enc1:<hex>`). A changed, cut-short or swapped file is a cache miss and is deleted. The key is a 0600 file next to the app databases (`<db>/app/media_cache.key`), so it has the same protection as `data.db`, which already holds every attachment's key. A key file that is lost, damaged or replaced is detected (`e1.keycheck`) and the sealed entries are wiped. Signing out deletes the key and every sealed entry. Entries are sealed and opened off the UI isolate: one worker isolate for small ones; entries of 1 MB or more get their own isolate that streams file to file, so opening a big video into its player copy holds about one segment in memory. Signing out crypto-shreds first (key file and key check), then wipes; key loads wait for a sign-out and never bring the old key back. A key file that exists but can't be read turns sealed caching off for that run (sensitive media just isn't cached) instead of replacing the key; another engine of the app (the Android background service) notices a forgotten or replaced key before it writes. The key file is kept 0600 and its folder (`<db>/app`) 0700, read back after chmod; if either can't be made owner-only, or the cache directory can't be made 0700, sealed caching is off for that run. A freshly downloaded encrypted video plays from its private copy at once and is sealed into the cache behind it; a write asked for before or during a sign-out is dropped, never sealed under the next key. On Linux the old /tmp cache is only deleted when its owner can be checked (`lstat`, or `__lxstat` on glibc before 2.33); otherwise only its rows are forgotten. Size limit, retention, per-type usage and clearing all still work. (`media_cache_crypto.dart`, `media_cache_key.dart`, `drift_file_cache.dart` `readFile`/`writeFile`/`forgetSensitive`, `matrix_media_privacy.dart`, `matrix_mxc_image_provider.dart`, `matrix_mxc_file_provider.dart`; tests `unit_test/encrypted_media_cache_test.dart`) | operator 10-26 | overlay (`fix/encrypted-media-cache`) |
| The media cache moved from the temporary directory (`/tmp/chat.commet.app/file_cache` on Linux, shared by every user of the machine) to `media_cache` in the app's own per-user cache directory, made 0700. At start rows pointing outside the new directory are forgotten and interrupted writes are swept; the old directory is deleted only if every part of its path under the temporary directory is a real directory (no links), it resolves to itself and, on Linux, every part is ours (owner checked with lstat). Anything else is left alone. | operator 10-26 | overlay (`fix/encrypted-media-cache`) |
| Players (video, GIF, audio, voice messages), the share sheet and the voice recorder need a file path. They get a short-lived copy in `media_open` in the app's cache directory (0700 directory, 0600 files, random names), never /tmp. It is deleted when the player is disposed, after sharing (Android at once, iOS/macOS after 5 minutes), and anything a crash left behind is swept at the next start. If the folder or a copy can't be made owner-only (checked on disk; Windows relies on the profile's ACLs), no copy is written and playback or sharing fails with a logged error. Unencrypted media keeps its plain cache file. "Save as" is unchanged. (`private_media_files.dart`, `owner_only*.dart`, `image_share.dart`, `voice_recorder.dart`, the four players) | operator 10-26 | overlay (`fix/encrypted-media-cache`) |
| Linux notification images (a message's picture, a link preview's image, custom emoji) no longer go into the file cache (they were plain PNGs named after the event id or URL, kept 5 days). They are private copies in `media_open` under random names, deleted when the notification is closed (checked every minute, and on clear) or after an hour at most, and swept at start. (`linux_notification_formatting.dart`, `linux_notifier.dart`; tests `unit_test/encrypted_media_paths_test.dart`) | operator 10-26 | overlay (`fix/encrypted-media-cache`) |
| A session the server ended (signed out from another device, token revoked) wipes the same local data as signing out here: the encrypted search index, the sealed media cache and its key, saved voice transcripts, the private player/share copies (`media_open`) and, on Android, the share_plus and "Copy image" copies (also swept at start; a copied image is kept 10 minutes so it can still be pasted). Running both is harmless. (`sign_out_wipe.dart`, `matrix_client.dart`, `private_media_files.dart`) | operator 10-26 | overlay (`fix/encrypted-media-cache`) |
| Saved voice transcripts are sealed with the media cache key under keyed names (`<hmac>.vt`) instead of plain JSON; the old JSON files are deleted at start-up. With no cache key they aren't saved. (`voice_transcription.dart`) | operator 10-26 | overlay (`fix/encrypted-media-cache`) |
## Scheduled send (feat/scheduled-send)

| Change | Issue | Status |
|---|---|---|
| "Schedule message" sends the typed text later, held by the homeserver as an MSC4140 delayed event (`PUT …/send/…?org.matrix.msc4140.delay=`), so it goes out even when Vommet is closed; no local queue. Entry: the composer's + menu in Discord style (once the box has text), right-click or long-press on Send in Telegram style, both in Custom (and on iOS, whose + skips the pickers, Send in every style). Picker: in 1 hour, 18:00 today or tomorrow, tomorrow 09:00, next Monday 09:00, or a date and time; a note says the homeserver holds it and that in an encrypted room it is encrypted right away. The normal send path builds the message (markdown, mentions, emoji, reply, translation), then `MatrixRoom.sendMessage` hands it to `ScheduledMessages.sendScheduled` through a zone value; encrypted rooms encrypt it now (`encryptGroupMessagePayload`). Only new text messages: not edits, files, forwards, commands or threads. A bar above the message box ("N scheduled messages · View") opens the room's list (from `GET …/delayed_events`): Send now, Edit (unschedules and puts the text back), Change time (schedules again, then cancels the old one), Delete. Homeservers that don't advertise `org.matrix.msc4140` in `/versions` get the item grayed out; tapping it explains why. Errors (time in the past, too far ahead with the server's `max_delay`) are shown and the text is put back. (`client/components/scheduled_messages/scheduled_messages.dart`, `ui/organisms/scheduled_messages/scheduled_messages_view.dart`, hooks in `message_input.dart`, `matrix_room.dart`, `chat_view.dart`, `intl_en.arb`; test `unit_test/scheduled_messages_test.dart`) | operator 10-26 (premium-free feature batch: delayed events only, grayed out without them) | overlay (`feat/scheduled-send`); nether.im's Tuwunel doesn't advertise MSC4140 yet |

## Media tab: encrypted rooms page the search index (perf/media-tab-encrypted-index)

| Change | Issue | Status |
|---|---|---|
| In encrypted rooms the Media and Files tabs page older history from the encrypted search index (Vommet issues 602, 611) instead of the room timeline: one local query per 50 files, newest first (`IndexMediaHistory`, behind the same `RoomMediaHistoryComponent` seam as the unencrypted rooms' filtered `/messages`; tokens `idx:<ts>:<event id>`, ties ordered by event id via the new `beforeEventId` of `SearchIndexStore.list`). Where the index hasn't reached yet it scans the next 100 messages itself (`indexOlder`, at most 3 steps per page, shared with the background indexer), and stretches that arrived while the app was closed are scanned first (paging then starts over from the newest; the feed dedupes by event id). Deleted files drop out and edited ones show their new content, as the index keeps them. The web version, the setting at Off, "Wi-Fi only" on mobile data, or an index that stops getting further keep paging the timeline (the same test as Deep Search's `indexOlderNeedsConfirmation`); a battery pause only stops the background indexer, the tab still pages and scans. Pages are read on index v2's read-only connection. Encrypted picture tiles are unchanged: there is no protected on-disk media cache to keep decrypted tile copies in. ## Deep Search (feat/deep-search)

| Change | Issue | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **Deep Search** finds messages across every DM and room of the filtered account (All accounts: all of them, an account dot per row). On encrypted chats and DMs it searches this device's index; unencrypted group rooms are searched on the homeserver, in their own section below. A new **Deep Search** card comes first on Home's Overview: on desktop, a field ("Search messages, files and links", Ctrl+Shift+F), a coverage line ("Encrypted chats: 412 of 480 fully indexed · building on Wi-Fi") and "Last search: … ›"; on phones, a one-line "Search messages" bar with an index dot and %. New users, Reset and untouched layouts get it; customized layouts get it once, and removing it sticks. It opens the Deep Search page: in Home's main area on desktop (the side list stays), a full page on phones. **Empty field:** shortcuts (@ Mentions me, Links, Files this week, Images), the last 5 recent searches with Clear and ×, and "type to narrow" examples. **Filters:** chips From ▾, In ▾, DMs, Rooms, Date ▾ (7 / 30 days, 12 months, range), Has ▾ (link, image, video, file, voice; a bottom sheet on phones), @ Mentions me, plus a Best match / Newest toggle. The typed tokens `from:` `in:` `has:` `is:dm` `is:room` `mentions:me` `before:` `after:` become the same chips, with pickers for in:/from:/has:, and Backspace in the empty field removes the last chip. **Results:** this device's hits paint at once (200 ms after typing; nothing for one character), best match first. Each row shows avatar, sender, "in #room · space path" or DM, time and a snippet around the first hit (highlighted, reply quotes stripped), plus tags (edited, file name, link, in thread). Nearby hits in one chat fold into "+N more here", and a hold / right-click menu offers "Search only this chat". A MOST MATCHES strip ("#recipes · 9", "99+", "+5 more") scopes to a chat. The homeserver section ("UNENCRYPTED ROOMS · SEARCHED ON YOUR HOMESERVER · NEWEST FIRST") follows after a 600 ms pause or Enter, with its own spinner, "Load more from the server", and a retry on failure. A filter-only search notes that unencrypted rooms need words. Ignored users are hidden. **Coverage** lines always show what was searched (building, paused for Wi-Fi or battery, off, web, keys missing, one chat's depth), each with at most one action (Index on mobile data this session, Settings, Look further back). Look further back asks first when indexing is off or would use mobile data. A footer covers chats still indexing. **One chat:** `in: #room` plus an "All chats › #room" breadcrumb; it follows room upgrades, with older-room hits labeled "(old version)". Entry points: the strip, the row menu, the side list's room menu "Search messages here", and the in-chat search's new "Search all chats" button (keeps the words and the chat as a chip). **Side list:** its search always ends with "Search messages for “X” ›" (Shift+Enter). **Shortcuts:** Ctrl+Shift+F anywhere; "/" only when no text field has focus. **Opening a result** jumps to the message in its chat (outlined for 3 s); a thread reply also opens its thread; a room you left says "You left this room". A results bar over the chat shows ‹ Results, the search, "3 of 14", ↑ ↓ across chats (Ctrl+Shift+G / Ctrl+G) and ×. ‹ Results returns to the list with its query, filters and scroll, with ✓ seen and "last opened" marks. Jumping to a message the app must fetch now times out after 15 s with "Couldn’t load that message…" or "That message isn’t available anymore." (previously it could spin forever). Screen readers hear the result count once typing settles, and the chips have labels. **Settings** › Search index: "Remember recent searches" (off clears the list; kept on this device only). ## Encrypted-room media sealed in the cache, cache off /tmp (fix/encrypted-media-cache)

| Change | Issue | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Media from encrypted rooms (pictures, thumbnails, videos, GIFs, audio, voice messages, files, inline HTML images; also link-preview images, which share one cache across rooms) is never written to disk in plaintext. Each cache entry is sealed with XChaCha20-Poly1305 (`cryptography`'s Dart implementation) under a key derived by HKDF-SHA256 from a random 256-bit cache key, in 64 KiB segments (format "VME2": a random 128-bit prefix per entry plus the segment counter as the nonce; the header, identifier, segment index and a last-segment flag bound as associated data, so a truncated, reordered or extended file doesn't open). File names and database rows are an HMAC of the identifier (`e1_<hex>`, `enc1:<hex>`). A changed, cut-short or swapped file is a cache miss and is deleted. The key is a 0600 file next to the app databases (`<db>/app/media_cache.key`), so it has the same protection as `data.db`, which already holds every attachment's key. A key file that is lost, damaged or replaced is detected (`e1.keycheck`) and the sealed entries are wiped. Signing out deletes the key and every sealed entry. Entries are sealed and opened off the UI isolate: one worker isolate for small ones; entries of 1 MB or more get their own isolate that streams file to file, so opening a big video into its player copy holds about one segment in memory. Signing out crypto-shreds first (key file and key check), then wipes; key loads wait for a sign-out and never bring the old key back. A key file that exists but can't be read turns sealed caching off for that run (sensitive media just isn't cached) instead of replacing the key; another engine of the app (the Android background service) notices a forgotten or replaced key before it writes. The key file is kept 0600 and its folder (`<db>/app`) 0700, read back after chmod; if either can't be made owner-only, or the cache directory can't be made 0700, sealed caching is off for that run. A freshly downloaded encrypted video plays from its private copy at once and is sealed into the cache behind it; a write asked for before or during a sign-out is dropped, never sealed under the next key. On Linux the old /tmp cache is only deleted when its owner can be checked (`lstat`, or `__lxstat` on glibc before 2.33); otherwise only its rows are forgotten. Size limit, retention, per-type usage and clearing all still work. (`media_cache_crypto.dart`, `media_cache_key.dart`, `drift_file_cache.dart` `readFile`/`writeFile`/`forgetSensitive`, `matrix_media_privacy.dart`, `matrix_mxc_image_provider.dart`, `matrix_mxc_file_provider.dart`; tests `unit_test/encrypted_media_cache_test.dart`) | operator 10-26 | overlay (`fix/encrypted-media-cache`) |
| The media cache moved from the temporary directory (`/tmp/chat.commet.app/file_cache` on Linux, shared by every user of the machine) to `media_cache` in the app's own per-user cache directory, made 0700. At start rows pointing outside the new directory are forgotten and interrupted writes are swept; the old directory is deleted only if every part of its path under the temporary directory is a real directory (no links), it resolves to itself and, on Linux, every part is ours (owner checked with lstat). Anything else is left alone. | operator 10-26 | overlay (`fix/encrypted-media-cache`) |
| Players (video, GIF, audio, voice messages), the share sheet and the voice recorder need a file path. They get a short-lived copy in `media_open` in the app's cache directory (0700 directory, 0600 files, random names), never /tmp. It is deleted when the player is disposed, after sharing (Android at once, iOS/macOS after 5 minutes), and anything a crash left behind is swept at the next start. If the folder or a copy can't be made owner-only (checked on disk; Windows relies on the profile's ACLs), no copy is written and playback or sharing fails with a logged error. Unencrypted media keeps its plain cache file. "Save as" is unchanged. (`private_media_files.dart`, `owner_only*.dart`, `image_share.dart`, `voice_recorder.dart`, the four players) | operator 10-26 | overlay (`fix/encrypted-media-cache`) |
| Linux notification images (a message's picture, a link preview's image, custom emoji) no longer go into the file cache (they were plain PNGs named after the event id or URL, kept 5 days). They are private copies in `media_open` under random names, deleted when the notification is closed (checked every minute, and on clear) or after an hour at most, and swept at start. (`linux_notification_formatting.dart`, `linux_notifier.dart`; tests `unit_test/encrypted_media_paths_test.dart`) | operator 10-26 | overlay (`fix/encrypted-media-cache`) |
| A session the server ended (signed out from another device, token revoked) wipes the same local data as signing out here: the encrypted search index, the sealed media cache and its key, saved voice transcripts, the private player/share copies (`media_open`) and, on Android, the share_plus and "Copy image" copies (also swept at start; a copied image is kept 10 minutes so it can still be pasted). Running both is harmless. (`sign_out_wipe.dart`, `matrix_client.dart`, `private_media_files.dart`) | operator 10-26 | overlay (`fix/encrypted-media-cache`) |
| Saved voice transcripts are sealed with the media cache key under keyed names (`<hmac>.vt`) instead of plain JSON; the old JSON files are deleted at start-up. With no cache key they aren't saved. (`voice_transcription.dart`) | operator 10-26 | overlay (`fix/encrypted-media-cache`) |
## Scheduled send (feat/scheduled-send)

| Change | Issue | Status |
|---|---|---|
| "Schedule message" sends the typed text later, held by the homeserver as an MSC4140 delayed event (`PUT …/send/…?org.matrix.msc4140.delay=`), so it goes out even when Vommet is closed; no local queue. Entry: the composer's + menu in Discord style (once the box has text), right-click or long-press on Send in Telegram style, both in Custom (and on iOS, whose + skips the pickers, Send in every style). Picker: in 1 hour, 18:00 today or tomorrow, tomorrow 09:00, next Monday 09:00, or a date and time; a note says the homeserver holds it and that in an encrypted room it is encrypted right away. The normal send path builds the message (markdown, mentions, emoji, reply, translation), then `MatrixRoom.sendMessage` hands it to `ScheduledMessages.sendScheduled` through a zone value; encrypted rooms encrypt it now (`encryptGroupMessagePayload`). Only new text messages: not edits, files, forwards, commands or threads. A bar above the message box ("N scheduled messages · View") opens the room's list (from `GET …/delayed_events`): Send now, Edit (unschedules and puts the text back), Change time (schedules again, then cancels the old one), Delete. Homeservers that don't advertise `org.matrix.msc4140` in `/versions` get the item grayed out; tapping it explains why. Errors (time in the past, too far ahead with the server's `max_delay`) are shown and the text is put back. (`client/components/scheduled_messages/scheduled_messages.dart`, `ui/organisms/scheduled_messages/scheduled_messages_view.dart`, hooks in `message_input.dart`, `matrix_room.dart`, `chat_view.dart`, `intl_en.arb`; test `unit_test/scheduled_messages_test.dart`) | operator 10-26 (premium-free feature batch: delayed events only, grayed out without them) | overlay (`feat/scheduled-send`); nether.im's Tuwunel doesn't advertise MSC4140 yet |

## Linux: customization in the XDG config folder (fix/836-xdg-config-dir)

| Change | Issue | Status |
|---|---|---|
| On Linux, custom themes, fonts, sounds and app icons live in `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/<app>` (`~/.config/im.nether.chat`; `~/.var/app/im.nether.chat/config/im.nether.chat` on Flatpak) instead of the data folder, so a setup can be copied or shared without the account data. Account databases, crypto stores, keys and downloaded models stay in `$XDG_DATA_HOME`; caches were already in `$XDG_CACHE_HOME`. Existing installs move once at startup (`initNecessary` → `AppConfig.moveConfigFolders`, right after the settings load): each folder is copied next to its new place, compared byte for byte, renamed into place, stored settings pointing into it are rewritten, and the old folder is deleted only once nothing refers to it and every file in it has an identical copy (a crash leaves the old folder or a complete new one; until the move succeeds the old folder stays in use). Other platforms unchanged. Settings (SharedPreferences) and IPC sockets are not split yet. ## Unread count clears when the newest message is yours, and when you read a thread (fix/843-own-newest-unread)

| Change | Issue | Status |
|---|---|---|
| A room (often a direct message) could keep a red count of 1 when its newest message was your own, and opening it didn't clear it: with sliding sync the server doesn't always send the cleared count again, so the stored count stayed. The SDK (pin `vommet-v6.1.1-ss.29.25`) now counts a room whose newest message is yours as read, both with the server's counts and with local counting. It looks at the whole update, not only new messages, and only lowers a server count (min). It also clears such stored counts once after sign-in, and lowers a room's count locally on each read receipt (thread receipts too: replies in a thread you just read stop counting). Thread replies by others after your message still count. The gap check (more new notifications than new events) now compares with the count the server sent last, not the locally lowered one, so a lowered count never resets the room's timeline. Vommet: every threaded receipt (`ThreadReceipts._post`: main, thread, and "Threads I'm in" auto-reads) now calls the SDK's `onOwnReceipt`, so reading a thread to its end clears the room's and the tray's count without replying. The issue 704 "resend the main receipt" step now also fires after a restart: the main timeline counts as read when the stored own main or unthreaded receipt is on its newest message, or that message is yours. The room's quiet unread mark (`utils/vommet_unread.dart`) also takes the thread's own receipt when the newest event is a thread reply (before, only the unthreaded and `main` receipts counted, so with per-thread read state only sending a message cleared it), and with "Threads I'm in" reading the room auto-reads others' new thread replies even when the newest main message hasn't changed. (`threads/thread_receipts.dart`, `utils/vommet_unread.dart`; test `unit_test/unread_thread_receipts_test.dart`; SDK `unread_counts.dart` + `test/vommet/sliding_sync_client_test.dart`) | Vommet issue 843 | overlay (`fix/843-own-newest-unread`) |
| A room (often a direct message) could keep a red count of 1 when its newest message was your own, and opening it didn't clear it: with sliding sync the server doesn't always send the cleared count again, so the stored count stayed. The SDK (pin `vommet-v6.1.1-ss.29.25`) now counts a room whose newest message is yours as read, both with the server's counts and with local counting. It looks at the whole update, not only new messages, and only lowers a server count (min). It also clears such stored counts once after sign-in, and lowers a room's count locally on each read receipt (thread receipts too: replies in a thread you just read stop counting). Thread replies by others after your message still count. The gap check (more new notifications than new events) now compares with the count the server sent last, not the locally lowered one, so a lowered count never resets the room's timeline. Vommet: every threaded receipt (`ThreadReceipts._post`: main, thread, and "Threads I'm in" auto-reads) now calls the SDK's `onOwnReceipt`, so reading a thread to its end clears the room's and the tray's count without replying. The issue 704 "resend the main receipt" step now also fires after a restart: the main timeline counts as read when the stored own main or unthreaded receipt is on its newest message, or that message is yours. (`threads/thread_receipts.dart`; SDK `unread_counts.dart` + `test/vommet/sliding_sync_client_test.dart`) | Vommet issue 843 | overlay (`fix/843-own-newest-unread`) |

## Local data encryption, opt-in (feat/local-data-encryption)

| Change | Issue | Status |
|---|---|---|
| The media cache is always encrypted with a key derived from a master key kept in the system keyring (Linux Secret Service or the Flatpak portal, Windows DPAPI, Android Keystore, iOS Keychain), or in a key file when there is no keyring. Encrypting the databases (each account's `data.db`, its search index and `app_data.db`, with SQLite3 Multiple Ciphers) is **off by default** for new and existing installs; the choice lives in `<database dir>/keys/data_encryption.json`, which is read before any database opens. Installs from a test build that already encrypted keep it on. New installs are asked on a first-run page after "Encrypt new rooms?" (Not now is the default); existing users get one dismissible notice (Home Alerts panel in the Discord layout, a banner above the chat list in the Telegram and Custom mix layouts). Settings › Privacy › "Data on this device" turns it on or off and shows where the key is kept, with a way to move it. Turning it on encrypts at the next start, and turning it off decrypts at the next start, both behind a splash with a progress bar. After a decrypt the database keys are forgotten and the media key is kept. A locked keyring, a missing or unreachable key, or a message store that won't open get their own start-up screens (Try again, Start over with a copy kept, Continue without the account, Reset the account). A damaged search index or media cache is rebuilt without asking. With encryption off, a locked keyring never blocks the start. Diagnostics schema v42 (`local_data_state`, `local_data_choice`, `local_data_migration`, `local_data_unlock`). Unit tests `local_data_*_test.dart`, `database_keys_test.dart`, `telemetry_v42_test.dart`, `onboarding_test.dart`; integration test `local_data_migration_test.dart` (off by default, opt in → encrypted, opt out → decrypted with the keys forgotten) | Local data at rest was readable by anything that could read the files | branch (`feat/local-data-encryption`) |
| New Home (Discord layout experiment) shows the app's alerts, which it never showed (it has no Alerts panel): one banner each atop the main area on every tab, under the backup banner, the same banner Telegram and Custom mix show above their chat list, e.g. "You can now encrypt your messages on this device" with Set up, and "Your key is kept in a file". Closing one hides it for the session in every layout; closing the encryption offer answers Not now (`new_home/new_home_alerts.dart`, `new_home_main.dart`, `unified_chat_source.dart`; unit test `new_home_alerts_test.dart`) | — | branch (`feat/local-data-encryption`) |
| Local data encryption hardening (security review 1): an unreadable setting file keeps encryption on (never decrypts); whether a new database is encrypted is decided from the files on disk only; a key found in the keyring is set aside, never overwritten; Start over and Reset ask with "Keep a copy" (on by default, kept with what opens it) and Reset is offered only for a damaged file, not a busy or locked one; Android backups leave out kept copies; a failed setting save says so in Settings; turning encryption off no longer claims the key leaves the keyring; error messages name only the file, not its folders; key files are checked owner-only; keys/.lock is refreshed while held | — | branch (`feat/local-data-encryption`) |

The issue 704 "resend the main receipt" step now also fires after a restart: the main timeline counts as read when the stored own main or unthreaded receipt is on its newest message, or that message is yours. (`threads/thread_receipts.dart`; SDK `unread_counts.dart` + `test/vommet/sliding_sync_client_test.dart`) | Vommet issue 843 | overlay (`fix/843-own-newest-unread`) |
| A room (often a direct message) could keep a red count of 1 when its newest message was your own, and opening it didn't clear it: with sliding sync the server doesn't always send the cleared count again, so the stored count stayed. The SDK (pin `vommet-v6.1.1-ss.29.25`) now counts a room whose newest message is yours as read, both with the server's counts and with local counting. It looks at the whole update, not only new messages, and only lowers a server count (min). It also clears such stored counts once after sign-in, and lowers a room's count locally on each read receipt (thread receipts too: replies in a thread you just read stop counting). Thread replies by others after your message still count. The gap check (more new notifications than new events) now compares with the count the server sent last, not the locally lowered one, so a lowered count never resets the room's timeline. Vommet: every threaded receipt (`ThreadReceipts._post`: main, thread, and "Threads I'm in" auto-reads) now calls the SDK's `onOwnReceipt`, so reading a thread to its end clears the room's and the tray's count without replying. The issue 704 "resend the main receipt" step now also fires after a restart: the main timeline counts as read when the stored own main or unthreaded receipt is on its newest message, or that message is yours. ## Windows quits without crashing (fix/883-windows-quit-teardown)

| Change | Issue | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Quitting on Windows no longer crashes, so a Windows shutdown, restart or logout is no longer held up by Vommet's "memory could not be written" error dialog. `WindowManagement.quit()` and the installer update ended the process with dart:io `exit(0)`, which calls `ExitProcess` on the UI thread while the engine, the plugins, the tray icon and the WebView2 widget dock are still running, so their teardown ran underneath them. On Windows, `exitApp()` now sends "quit" on `im.nether.vommet/session`; the runner posts itself a message and destroys the window, the same teardown as closing a plain Flutter app (engine shut down, widget dock and tray icon removed, message loop ends). `exit(0)` stays as the fallback when the runner doesn't answer or the window is still open 5 s later. `WM_ENDSESSION` now runs the message loop for up to 4 s, until Dart has closed its clients and asks to quit, because Windows can end the process as soon as it returns. Linux is unchanged. (`utils/app_exit.dart`, `window_management.dart`, `release_update.dart`, `windows/runner/flutter_window.cpp`/`.h`; test `unit_test/app_exit_test.dart`) | Vommet issue 883 | overlay (`fix/883-windows-quit-teardown`) |

## Videos play while they download, encrypted rooms and Tuwunel included (fix/encrypted-video-streaming)

| Change | Issue | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Videos in encrypted rooms, and any video from a homeserver that ignores range requests (Tuwunel, e.g. nether.im), had to download completely before playing. They now go through a small HTTP server inside the app, on 127.0.0.1 only, with a random 256-bit address per video. It downloads the file once into an owner-only private copy, decrypting it on the fly (AES-CTR at any offset), and serves the player whatever range it asks for as soon as those bytes have arrived. When the homeserver supports ranges, a seek more than 2 MB past the download is fetched on its own. The attachment's SHA-256 is checked when the download ends; a mismatch (or a file cut short) stops the player and nothing is cached. A video that checks out is cached as before (sealed in encrypted rooms). mpv's network timeout is raised to 10 minutes for these local streams. Unencrypted videos on servers with range support still stream directly. Limitation: an MP4 whose index is at the end still waits for the whole file on a server without ranges. (`cache/media_stream_server.dart` new; `StreamSource.verified`/`close`; `matrix_mxc_file_provider.dart` `getStreamSource`, `_localStream`; `video_player_implementation.dart`; unit test `unit_test/media_stream_server_test.dart`) | operator 10-28 | overlay (`fix/encrypted-video-streaming`) |
